cookie-run-crumble-accuracy-focus-guide.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Your team has enough power. The boss still shrugs off the opener, Scorpion Cookie stacks poison at a snail's pace, and a skill that should have landed seems to disappear. Adding more ATK will not fix every one of those failures.

Late-stage progression starts checking two stats that are easy to ignore early: Accuracy and Focus. One decides whether the skill connects. The other decides whether its debuff sticks. Mixing them up wastes gear, and ignoring both can turn a repeatable clear into twenty restarts.

<GuideSection id="accuracy-vs-focus" title="Accuracy and Focus solve different misses">

Accuracy counters enemy Evasion. When your Accuracy is too low, the enemy can avoid the skill completely. The damage misses and any effect attached to that hit never gets a chance to work.

Focus counters enemy Resistance. A skill can connect and deal damage, yet its poison, DEF Down, or another debuff may fail. That points to Focus.

| Stat | It fights | Failure you see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accuracy | Evasion | The attack or skill misses |
| Focus | Resistance | The hit lands, but the debuff does not |

Giving Scorpion Cookie more Accuracy may help her hit, but it will not solve Venom Sting getting resisted after the hit connects. The equipment screen can make the wrong fix look convincing, so identify the failure before chasing a larger number.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="late-stage-checks" title="Expect the checks around Chapters 70 to 80">

Early chapters let you get away with messy stats. Around Chapters 70 to 80, missed hits and failed debuffs become easier to notice. Bosses live through a rotation that used to work. Damage stalls for several seconds. The same team clears once, then fails three times with no obvious change.

The requirements rise at a fairly steady pace. One early checkpoint around Chapter 34 uses 273 Accuracy and 232 Focus. A late checkpoint in Chapter 83 reaches 558 Accuracy and 473 Focus. These snapshots are not permanent targets for every stage. They explain why a build that felt fine earlier can suddenly become unreliable.

Check the current fight instead of copying one number forever. If the stage wants less than your Cookie already has, another Accuracy or Focus roll is dead weight. When the Cookie sits below the check, the missing stat may beat another offensive line.

<GuideTip title="Do not overcap blindly">

A Scorpion Cookie with roughly 700 Focus already has room above a 473 Focus check. If her Accuracy remains below the stage target, adding more Focus polishes the stat that was already working.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="diagnose-missed-skills" title="Read the failed run before changing gear">

Watch the first rotation at normal speed. If the entire skill misses, compare Accuracy with the current stage. If damage appears but the status icon does not, check Focus. Scorpion Cookie makes this easy to see because Venom Sting needs to stack. Devil Cookie and Dark Choco Cookie expose the same problem when DEF Down fails to appear.

The opening matters more than the final damage screen. Scorpion wants to reach ten poison stacks quickly. Missing an early application delays every tick that follows, so the loss grows through the fight. Devil Cookie without DEF Down is taking a team slot without doing the job you brought him to do.

Run the same stage several times before spending materials. One unlucky attempt proves little. A repeated pattern does. Swap one gear piece, rerun, and compare how often the opener works. Changing Cookies, Pets, and six items together only hides the answer.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="gear-slot-setup" title="Build gear around each slot's stat pool">

Every equipment piece has its own substat pool. Weapons such as the sword, bow, and staff make useful offensive rolls easier to find. Accessories have more possible results, so forcing a perfect accessory can chew through time and materials.

Use this late-stage setup as a starting point:

1. Put Skill Amp on the top six slots when the pieces allow it.
2. Add Accuracy to three or four of those six pieces.
3. Spend the remaining top rolls on CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, Focus, or Skill Haste according to the Cookie.
4. Favor Focus and Skill Haste on the bottom-right group.
5. Use the bottom-left group to fill Power or the build's remaining shortage.

Keep a strong piece when the stage check is already covered. When the team repeatedly fails its setup, trade a little theoretical damage for the stat that makes the rotation happen.

The broader [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) covers Skill Amp, Skill Haste, damage stats, and upgrade materials across every role.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="scorpion-and-debuffers" title="Give debuffers enough Focus to do their job">

Scorpion Cookie is the cleanest test case. Her single-target damage depends on Venom Sting landing and stacking. Full offense can produce a faster clear when every application works, but a Focus build produces fewer dead attempts. For daily farming or a boss I plan to repeat, I would rather clear reliably than restart until the game cooperates.

Devil Cookie and Dark Choco Cookie follow the same logic. Their DEF Down opens the team's damage window. When it fails, the rest of the lineup can look weak even though their builds did not change. Check the debuffer before replacing the damage dealers.

Focus belongs on Cookies that apply a useful debuff. A pure attacker gains nothing from it. The [Cookie list](/cookies/) shows roles, buffs, and Synergy information, which makes it easier to find a real owner for a Focus piece.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="power-still-matters" title="Keep enough Power for the stage multiplier">

Accuracy and Focus do not replace combat Power. Stages can reduce your damage when the lineup falls below the expected total. A team that lands every debuff can still time out if the stage multiplier cuts its output too far.

Raise Power until the damage multiplier gives the team a workable attempt, then use Accuracy and Focus to make the rotation dependable. Roughly 35% or 55% of the available stage damage can be enough for a push, while the highest thresholds may demand far more investment than a first clear needs. The display changes with the stage, so judge the result in combat.

A higher-Power item with poor substats may win while you sit under a harsh penalty. Once the team reaches a usable multiplier, move back toward stats that fit each Cookie. A green arrow can help with Power. It cannot diagnose a missed Venom Sting.

Use the [Tier List](/tier-list/) to compare late-game investment value after the stage checks are covered. A high rank can tell you which Cookie is worth building next, but it cannot turn an Accuracy shortage into an ATK problem.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="upgrade-without-perfect-gear" title="Progress without waiting for perfect equipment">

Perfect sets are slow because accessories can roll so many stats. Most accounts will mix a few clean pieces with several compromises. Cover the current Accuracy and Focus checks, keep enough Power, and improve one slot when a good replacement appears.

Sugar Runes can patch a shortage on one Cookie. This helps when Scorpion needs more Focus but changing shared equipment would hurt someone else. Check what the stage asks for before locking expensive rolls. SSR lettering cannot rescue a stat that already sits above the target.

You can clear below the ideal checks by retrying until the right hits and debuffs land. That works for a one-time push. It gets miserable when you farm the stage. If every clear takes five restarts, consistency will save more time than another small CRIT DMG increase.

When the stats look correct and the run still fails, compare the shape of the lineup with the [recommended teams](/teams/), then test your exact roster in the [Team Builder](/tools/team-builder/). A missing tank, support, or Synergy match needs a lineup change rather than more Accuracy.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="quick-checklist" title="Use this card when a stage feels random">

- Raise Accuracy when the whole skill misses.
- Raise Focus on the debuffer when the hit lands but poison or DEF Down fails.
- Check the Power multiplier and offensive stats when debuffs work but damage stays low.
- Fix survival or healing when the front line dies before the setup starts.
- Compare several openers when one attempt works and the next collapses.
- Spend the slot elsewhere when the Cookie already exceeds the check.

Build enough Accuracy and Focus for the fight in front of you, then go back to damage. Stacking either stat past its job only replaces one bad build with another.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="accuracy-focus-faq" title="CookieRun: Crumble Accuracy and Focus FAQ">

### What does Accuracy do in CookieRun: Crumble?

Accuracy counters enemy Evasion. If a Cookie has too little Accuracy for the fight, an attack or skill can miss completely.

### What does Focus do in CookieRun: Crumble?

Focus counters enemy Resistance. It helps poison, DEF Down, and other debuffs land after the skill hits.

### How much Accuracy and Focus do I need?

Match the current stage check instead of using one permanent target. A Chapter 83 example asks for 558 Accuracy and 473 Focus, but earlier stages need less and later stages can ask for more.

### What is the best late-stage equipment setup?

Favor Skill Amp on the top six slots, then add Accuracy to three or four of those pieces. Use Focus and Skill Haste on the bottom-right group, while the other slots cover Power and role-specific needs.

### Can I clear a stage below the Accuracy or Focus check?

Yes. Repeated attempts can produce a run where the important hits and debuffs land. That is acceptable for one clear, but meeting the checks makes farming and repeated boss runs far more consistent.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-arena-healing-down-te.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

If your Arena team keeps dying despite several healers, check whether Pinot Noir is cutting their recovery. Another healing slot may add little against that debuff, especially when it leaves fewer attackers to finish the fight.

Start by checking overlapping buffs and healing reduction. The support effects that help your attackers still have a job. A spare healing slot is where a shield or control Cookie may buy more time.

The lineup below keeps Herb and Milk. It is a practical starting point for moving toward a more aggressive team, with the full Cookie and Pet order intact. If your Herb still saves fights, you do not need to remove him to follow an Arena trend.

<GuideSection id="arena-lineup" title="Copy the full lineup before changing slots">

This Strawberry Crepe Rapid AoE team mixes damage with a familiar support group. Read the rows from left to right: slots 1 through 6 on top, then 7 through 12 below.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Strawberry Crepe Rapid AoE Team"
  description="This damage-focused baseline keeps Herb and Milk for recovery. Test the shield and control swaps below only after checking how the full formation performs."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0181", "cookie3001", "cookie0126", "cookie4024", "cookie0063", "cookie4013", "cookie0515", "cookie4010", "cookie4019", "cookie0518", "cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet4005", "pet4001", "pet0111"]}
/>

The top row is Macaron, Scorpion, Melon Soda, Pomegranate, Nameless Cake Hound, and Herb. The bottom row is Brightseeker, Rye, Pinot Noir, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, Strawberry Crepe, and Dark Choco.

Use Chargemellow, Holy Baby Drop, and Hot Doggie in that order. The example has 129.33M displayed Power, with Pet levels 13, 15, and 15. Those numbers describe one account, not an entry requirement or a promise of wins.

Herb occupies slot 6, so this is not a no-healer lineup. Milk also heals while supplying ATK support. The formation gives you a clear baseline: keep its damage package, then decide how much recovery your Arena opponents allow.

You can find this exact ordered lineup on the [Teams page](/teams/). Save the original setup before testing replacements so you can compare results without rebuilding it from memory.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="healing-and-buffs" title="Why stacking healers can lose the damage race">

Pinot Noir's Healing Received Down changes the value of recovery in Arena. A team can have several healing skills available and still fail to refill health fast enough. That makes a spare healer slot harder to justify when it could provide damage, shielding, or crowd control.

Buff overlap adds another problem. Milk and Cheesecake do not provide two fully stacked versions of the same ATK buff. The stronger applicable buff takes over. Once Milk's buff exceeds Cheesecake's, keeping both purely to multiply healing gives you less than the lineup suggests.

Macaron creates a similar reason to check duplicate CRIT buffs. Compare the specific effects, their strength, and what else each Cookie contributes. Two support portraits do not automatically mean two independent layers of the same stat.

This does not mean every buff conflicts, or that a support becomes useless when one effect overlaps. Synergies and other abilities can still justify the slot. The mistake is counting the same benefit twice when choosing all twelve Cookies.

Against a healing-heavy opponent, Pinot Noir helps your damage stick. Against a team that barely heals, the heal cut has less work to do. His repeated-hit support and knock-up resistance can still matter, but the matchup changes why you bring him.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pinot-damage-core" title="Keep Pinot Noir's damage partners working">

Pinot Noir supplies the Multi-strike synergy that supports repeated-hit attackers. Strawberry Crepe, Rye, and Melon Soda benefit from that package in the displayed formation. Cutting Pinot to squeeze in another healer can weaken several damage slots at once.

Grapevine also supplies Multi-strike, so she needs a clearer reason to join a team that already uses Pinot. Her healing may still help a particular account, but she no longer fills an otherwise empty synergy role. Check that contribution before replacing an attacker with her.

Strawberry Crepe needs the team around them to keep the damage cycle moving. A Defense label does not mean you should expect a conventional tank. The [Strawberry Crepe build guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-strawberry-crepe-cookie-build-team/) covers the damage setup behind this formation.

Brightseeker and Scorpion add more pressure, while the support group keeps the attacks useful. Preserve that relationship when swapping. Removing the first Cookie with low personal damage can cost more team damage than replacing an underperforming attacker.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rockstar-shields" title="Test Rockstar when healing cannot keep up">

Rockstar offers a different way to survive. His shield scales with his maximum HP, and healing reduction does not cut a shield in the same way it cuts a heal. That makes him worth testing when health bars collapse despite repeated healing casts.

The HP scaling also means Rockstar's shield does not depend on stacking Milk and Cheesecake's ATK buffs. You still need enough protection to survive the enemy burst, but you are solving that problem with a different defensive effect.

For the displayed lineup, one sensible experiment is Herb out and Rockstar in. Treat this as a suggested swap, not a second fixed lineup. Keep the other eleven Cookies and the Pets unchanged for the first comparison.

Nameless Cake Hound already gives the baseline a damage-reduction option. Avoid removing that protection at the same time you remove Herb. Otherwise, a failed run will not tell you whether you needed more healing or simply stripped away too much defense.

A shield is not proof that you can ignore survival stats. If Rockstar or an attacker dies before contributing, the experiment needs more work. Look at the opening sequence rather than assuming all shield-based teams beat all healing teams.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-control" title="Use control when another attacker adds little">

Aggressive Arena teams still need time to act. Stuns and knockback can delay an enemy skill or interrupt pressure long enough for your own damage to finish a target. That can make a control slot useful even when its personal damage looks poor.

Milky Way is an option when you want knockback alongside wider damage. Other control Cookies can fit too, but check their promotion and whether they survive in your matches. Do not copy a leaderboard slot without checking what your own version can do.

If Strawberry Crepe contributes little before the team collapses, test a control replacement rather than automatically adding more healing. If Crepe is carrying the damage, keep them and review a different slot.

Wind Archer is another possible damage choice once your copy has enough investment. Five stars is a reasonable point to revisit that swap in this approach. It is not a guarantee that Wind Archer improves every account. Compare the whole team result, including any protection you gave up to fit him.

Use the [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/) to narrow down investment choices, then let the fights decide the slot. A high rank cannot compensate for a Cookie that never gets a useful cast.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-pets" title="Choose Pets for the failure you can see">

Holy Baby Drop provides ATK support, which helps the attackers and the healing or buffs that scale with ATK. It remains useful even when you reduce dedicated healing slots.

Hot Doggie adds Skill Amp. That makes it a useful partner for a lineup with several active damage skills, but it does not make every effect scale identically. Read the effect you are trying to improve.

Chargemellow supports the rapid repeated attacks in this setup. Keep it for the first test with Strawberry Crepe, Rye, and Melon Soda. If you replace one of those attackers, revisit how much the remaining lineup gets from Chargemellow.

A defensive Pet becomes worth testing when you deal enough damage but lose the opening exchange. Start by comparing that option against the third Pet rather than rebuilding all three slots.

Pet choices should follow the actual lineup. There is no need to buy a premium alternative simply because another account uses it. Better promotion, different attackers, or a more fragile front line can change which option helps.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="keep-or-cut-herb" title="Read the result before removing Herb">

Healing totals can mislead you. A team that takes more damage has more missing health to restore. A team that dies quickly also has less time to heal. Compare survival and the final outcome alongside the recovery numbers.

Healing reduction may also fail to land or meet resistance. If Herb suddenly restores a large amount, do not assume the strategy stopped working. Check whether the debuff applied and how long the healer stayed alive.

Herb is still a reasonable choice when you want one dedicated healer. Keep him when his recovery buys another useful attack cycle. Drop him when repeated attempts show that a shield or control effect gives your damage dealers more time.

For a fragile Cookie that falls before casting, levels can help with HP and DEF. The [level-100 EXP priority guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-level-100-exp-priority-guide/) explains why Arena investment should follow the teammate who dies first after you cover Milk and your carries.

Save a second preset for experiments. Try one replacement against comparable opponents, review the opening deaths, and keep the version that performs better. You do not need to dismantle a working team just because another account wins with less healing.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-faq" title="Arena healing reduction FAQ">

### Is this lineup a no-healer team?

No. The displayed formation contains Herb and Milk. It is a damage-focused baseline that keeps recovery, with suggested swaps for players who want to test less healing.

### Should I remove Herb when I use Pinot Noir?

Not automatically. Keep Herb if his healing helps your attackers survive another skill cycle. Test Rockstar or a control Cookie when healing reduction makes that slot less useful.

### Does Rockstar's shield avoid healing reduction?

Healing reduction does not reduce shields in the same way it reduces healing. Rockstar's shield scales with his maximum HP, but the team still needs enough durability to survive incoming damage.

### Should Milk and Cheesecake share an Arena team?

Do not pair them solely to stack the same ATK buff. The stronger applicable buff takes over. Keep both only when their other contributions justify the two slots.

</GuideSection>

segments.text: Rockstar offers a different way to survive. His shield scales with his maximum HP, and healing reduction does not cut a shield in the same way it cuts a heal. That makes him worth testing when health bars collapse despite repeated healing casts.

The HP scaling also means Rockstar's shield does not depend on stacking Milk and Cheesecake's ATK buffs. You still need enough protection to survive the enemy burst, but you are solving that problem with a different defensive effect.

For the displayed lineup, one sensible experiment is Herb out and Rockstar in. Treat this as a suggested swap, not a second fixed lineup. Keep the other eleven Cookies and the Pets unchanged for the first comparison.

Nameless Cake Hound already gives the baseline a damage-reduction option. Avoid removing that protection at the same time you remove Herb. Otherwise, a failed run will not tell you whether you needed more healing or simply stripped away too much defense.

A shield is not proof that you can ignore survival stats. If Rockstar or an attacker dies before contributing, the experiment needs more work. Look at the opening sequence rather than assuming all shield-based teams beat all healing teams.
Test Rockstar when healing cannot keep up
segments.name: title

segments.text: Aggressive Arena teams still need time to act. Stuns and knockback can delay an enemy skill or interrupt pressure long enough for your own damage to finish a target. That can make a control slot useful even when its personal damage looks poor.

Milky Way is an option when you want knockback alongside wider damage. Other control Cookies can fit too, but check their promotion and whether they survive in your matches. Do not copy a leaderboard slot without checking what your own version can do.

If Strawberry Crepe contributes little before the team collapses, test a control replacement rather than automatically adding more healing. If Crepe is carrying the damage, keep them and review a different slot.

Wind Archer is another possible damage choice once your copy has enough investment. Five stars is a reasonable point to revisit that swap in this approach. It is not a guarantee that Wind Archer improves every account. Compare the whole team result, including any protection you gave up to fit him.
Use the
CookieRun: Crumble Tier List
to narrow down investment choices, then let the fights decide the slot. A high rank cannot compensate for a Cookie that never gets a useful cast.
Use control when another attacker adds little
segments.name: title

segments.text: Holy Baby Drop provides ATK support, which helps the attackers and the healing or buffs that scale with ATK. It remains useful even when you reduce dedicated healing slots.

Hot Doggie adds Skill Amp. That makes it a useful partner for a lineup with several active damage skills, but it does not make every effect scale identically. Read the effect you are trying to improve.

Chargemellow supports the rapid repeated attacks in this setup. Keep it for the first test with Strawberry Crepe, Rye, and Melon Soda. If you replace one of those attackers, revisit how much the remaining lineup gets from Chargemellow.
A defensive Pet becomes worth testing when you deal enough damage but lose the opening exchange. Start by comparing that option against the third Pet rather than rebuilding all three slots.

Pet choices should follow the actual lineup. There is no need to buy a premium alternative simply because another account uses it. Better promotion, different attackers, or a more fragile front line can change which option helps.
Choose Pets for the failure you can see
segments.name: title

segments.text: Healing totals can mislead you. A team that takes more damage has more missing health to restore. A team that dies quickly also has less time to heal. Compare survival and the final outcome alongside the recovery numbers.

Healing reduction may also fail to land or meet resistance. If Herb suddenly restores a large amount, do not assume the strategy stopped working. Check whether the debuff applied and how long the healer stayed alive.

Herb is still a reasonable choice when you want one dedicated healer. Keep him when his recovery buys another useful attack cycle. Drop him when repeated attempts show that a shield or control effect gives your damage dealers more time.
For a fragile Cookie that falls before casting, levels can help with HP and DEF. The
level-100 EXP priority guide
explains why Arena investment should follow the teammate who dies first after you cover Milk and your carries.

Save a second preset for experiments. Try one replacement against comparable opponents, review the opening deaths, and keep the version that performs better. You do not need to dismantle a working team just because another account wins with less healing.
Read the result before removing Herb
segments.name: title

segments.text: Is this lineup a no-healer team?
No. The displayed formation contains Herb and Milk. It is a damage-focused baseline that keeps recovery, with suggested swaps for players who want to test less healing.
Should I remove Herb when I use Pinot Noir?
Not automatically. Keep Herb if his healing helps your attackers survive another skill cycle. Test Rockstar or a control Cookie when healing reduction makes that slot less useful.
Does Rockstar's shield avoid healing reduction?
Healing reduction does not reduce shields in the same way it reduces healing. Rockstar's shield scales with his maximum HP, but the team still needs enough durability to survive incoming damage.
Should Milk and Cheesecake share an Arena team?
Do not pair them solely to stack the same ATK buff. The stronger applicable buff takes over. Keep both only when their other contributions justify the two slots.
Arena healing reduction FAQ
segments.name: title

cookie-run-crumble-arena-power-gap-guide.text:
import { GuideSection } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

You pick an Arena opponent with less Combat Power, expect a comfortable win, and watch your team disappear. You spend materials on another upgrade, then lose the same kind of fight.

CookieRun: Crumble uses different rules for Arena and stage progression. Arena carries over only part of your account's growth, while equipment options and Sugar Runes can change how a fight plays out. The displayed total cannot explain all of those differences.

**Before spending to fix an Arena loss, check the equipment preset on your attack team.** Then look at the stats and the lineup. A higher number still tells you something about the account; it does not promise that your damage dealer will survive long enough to use a skill.

<GuideSection id="arena-growth-rules" title="Check which upgrades Arena carries over">

Arena's growth rules include Cookie levels and promotions, ownership effects, collection bonuses, equipment, Plate enhancement, and Sugar Runes. They do not carry over every account growth system that helps raise your general Combat Power.

That distinction explains why two accounts can look far apart on paper yet fight a close match. One player may have invested heavily in broader progression. The other may have better equipment options and Runes on the Cookies entering Arena. Those are different advantages, and the larger displayed total does not tell you which matters more in that match.

Stellar Link, Resolve, Fame, and research still deserve attention for account growth and stage progress. Keep their purpose separate from the Arena improvements you are trying to buy. If a specific upgrade sits outside Arena's listed growth factors, raising it will not fix your PvP build in the way a useful equipment roll might.

Check the mode's rules when deciding where to spend. You need the effects that apply to the fight ahead of you, especially when materials only cover one meaningful upgrade.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="equipment-power-gap" title="Read the equipment options behind the number">

Two pieces of equipment can add very different amounts of Combat Power. That does not mean the one with the larger increase helps your Arena lineup more. The total compresses several stats into a single figure, which hides whether those stats solve your problem.

Suppose your main attacker dies before its first useful skill. A damage upgrade can make that Cookie look stronger without giving it any more time to act. Damage Reduction may produce a better result even if the equipment comparison makes it look less exciting.

Or suppose the team survives, but the opponent's healing keeps undoing your damage. Another defensive roll may only stretch out the loss. Check your damage cycle and whether the composition can handle that opponent's sustain before rolling more defense.

Sugar Runes create another gap. Opponents with modest displayed Power can have carefully chosen Runes on their active Cookies. If your own Runes contain whatever happened to roll first, similar promotions will not make the two builds equivalent.

Compare useful effects rather than equipment rarity alone. A rare piece with the wrong options can lose to a lower-Power piece that keeps your team functioning.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-stat-priorities" title="Start with broadly useful Arena stats">

Skill Amp, Skill Haste, and Damage Reduction are the practical starting pool for Arena equipment. They address skill output, casting frequency, and survival. You can use them as a baseline without assuming that every server faces the same popular formation.

Skill Amp makes sense when the relevant skill effect benefits from it. Check the Cookie's job before treating it as a universal answer; a stat debuffer and a damage dealer do not necessarily gain the same value from that roll.

Skill Haste helps the skill cycle. It deserves attention when the lineup relies on support casts or needs an attacker to act sooner. Extra output does little for an opening that ends before the important skill arrives.

Damage Reduction buys time for that cycle. Favor it when repeated losses begin with a Cookie dropping before the team can recover. Once the formation survives comfortably, compare more offensive options instead of adding defense out of habit.

CRIT Chance and CRIT DMG are the next offensive options to consider. Their place depends on the Cookie and what your opponents are doing. Treat this as a pool of useful stats, not a demand to force one exact roll onto every slot.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="accuracy-and-focus" title="Add Accuracy or Focus for a visible reason">

Accuracy and Focus need more context. Their value changes with the formations common on your server and the opponents you choose. A build that needs them badly in one set of matchups may get less from the same investment elsewhere.

Accuracy addresses attacks failing to connect. Focus addresses debuff reliability against Resistance. They solve related problems, but they do not replace each other. The [Accuracy and Focus guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-accuracy-focus-guide/) explains how to tell those failures apart.

Watch several attempts before turning either stat into a permanent farming target. Repeated misses justify an Accuracy check. Important debuffs failing despite attacks connecting justify a Focus check. If your team simply dies at the start, neither observation has established that you need more of those stats yet.

There is no single Arena Accuracy or Focus target that fits every server. Copying a number without copying its matchup can waste equipment rolls. Start with the failure you can see, change one relevant option, and compare the next attempts.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-plate-preset" title="Farm an Arena Plate without replacing your stage set">

You can keep a separate equipment setup for Arena. Switch to another Plate preset before farming, build that equipment set there, and then select that Plate in your Arena attack-team setup.

The final selection matters. Creating a good second set does not help if the attack team still points to the Plate you use for pushing stages.

Use this sequence when you decide to build a separate set:

1. Check which Plate currently holds the stage equipment you want to keep.
2. Switch to a different preset before farming Arena equipment.
3. Keep options that suit the Arena lineup and the losses you need to fix.
4. Open the Arena attack-team settings and select the Plate you just prepared.
5. Confirm the equipped set before spending attempts on the comparison.

You do not have to farm a dedicated Arena set immediately. A shared set can be a reasonable compromise when stage progression is your main goal or managing another preset feels like extra work. Skill Amp and Skill Haste can help in both settings, though the best balance still depends on the team.

The cost is what you pass up while farming. An Arena-focused session may produce a piece you would rather use for stages, or take time you wanted to spend improving the main set. Build the second preset when repeated Arena problems give it a clear purpose.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="team-matchups" title="Inspect the lineup before buying another upgrade">

Equipment is only part of the explanation. Cookie combinations and the rest of the team setup can turn an apparently favorable Power comparison into a poor matchup. Even strong Cookies can struggle together if you leave out the healing or synergy they need.

Use the [recommended teams](/teams/) to compare support roles and synergy packages. Look for a missing job in your own formation before swapping the lowest-Power Cookie. Removing the healer or synergy provider may raise the total while making the formation less reliable.

The [Cookie tier list](/tier-list/) helps you decide which replacements deserve investment. Use it alongside your current promotions and equipment. A highly ranked Cookie with unfinished Runes may not improve the team as soon as you put it in.

For the next loss, note who falls first and whether the team gets to use its intended skills. That gives you a useful next action: test survival, adjust a skill cycle, or reconsider the matchup. If you buy more general Power first, you may spend the materials and still lose to that opponent.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="stage-power-tradeoff" title="Keep raising Power when stages are the problem">

Stage progression gives Combat Power a much more direct job. The team's Power affects its damage through the stage adjustment system. Raising the total can improve damage across the lineup, even when the printed stat increase on one upgrade looks small.

This is a battle scaling effect, not evidence that the game permanently weakened a Cookie's skill. The [stage Power guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-power-guide-stage-damage/) covers the progression check in more detail. For your spending plan, remember that an upgrade can help a stage wall without solving an Arena loss.

GingerBright against GingerCraven shows the tradeoff. GingerBright's ATK Down can reduce pressure from the boss. But a lower-rarity Cookie can also bring less Power than the replacement, pulling down the team's total and reducing damage through the stage scaling.

That makes GingerBright a conditional survival choice. If the debuff prevents a wipe, it can still earn the slot. If your team already survives and the boss keeps living until time runs out, the Power loss may cost more than the debuff gives back. Compare both versions of the team before deciding.

For broader Power growth, review Stellar Link, Resolve, Fame, research, equipment enhancement, and useful Rune upgrades. Choose what your account can finish, then retry the stage with a working lineup. Your Arena equipment plan can stay separate while those upgrades improve progression.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-power-faq" title="Arena Combat Power FAQ">

### Why do I lose to lower-Power Arena teams?

Arena applies only part of account growth. Better equipment options, Sugar Runes, and a stronger matchup can outweigh your displayed Power lead. Check your attack team's Plate and active Cookie builds before buying more general upgrades.

### What equipment stats should I start with for Arena?

Start with Skill Amp where it applies, Skill Haste, and Damage Reduction. Consider CRIT Chance and CRIT DMG for offense. Add Accuracy or Focus when your opponents and failed attempts give you a reason to need them.

### Do I need a separate Arena equipment preset?

No. A shared set can work while you prioritize stages. If you farm another Plate for Arena, select it in the attack-team settings so the team uses the equipment you prepared.

### Should I ignore Combat Power after an Arena loss?

No. Keep it as context, then inspect the actual build and matchup. Power remains important for stage damage scaling, so a disappointing Arena result does not make your wider account upgrades useless.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-bari-story-boss-team-.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

A team clears several stages without trouble, then spends the next fight airborne. You add defense, reach another boss, and suddenly cannot deal enough damage. Rebuilding all twelve slots after every loss gets old fast.

Keep **three saved story presets**: a Princess Bari and Cherry Cola team for routine progression, an anti-knock-up team, and a GingerCraven team that keeps Power in mind. Redberry needs a separate adjustment because chasing that enemy can make the fight worse.

These are developed rosters. Copying the portraits will not copy the promotion and equipment behind them. If your Cookies have lower promotion or weaker equipment, use the survival adjustments below before judging the entire team. Finishing story opens access to the Dimensional Rift, so a reliable clear matters more than squeezing out a prettier damage chart.

<GuideSection id="choose-story-preset" title="Choose the preset from the failed fight">

Start with the Bari and Cherry Cola lineup for ordinary stages. Keep it while the team survives and finishes its targets. You do not need a specialized answer to every boss name.

Switch to the anti-knock-up setup when repeated lifts interrupt the formation. Hammer attacks and Cool Mint fights are the obvious cases. A support who cannot finish casting is not doing much supporting, however good the Rune page looks.

For GingerCraven, check whether your problem is incoming damage or damage that barely moves the boss's health bar. The third preset includes Wind Archer to help raise Power on an account where that slot offers a useful increase. You can use Cherry Cola in that slot if she works better on your account.

All three complete lineups also appear on the [Teams page](/teams/). Save them separately so you can return to a working setup after a failed experiment. Keep the Cookie and Pet order when you copy them; the numbered portraits make comparisons easier.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-cherry-cola-team" title="The everyday Bari and Cherry Cola team">

Use this as the default preset while moving through story. Bari and Cherry Cola share the lineup, with Scorpion for boss pressure and the familiar support group around them. Nameless Cake Hound does not occupy a slot in this version.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Bari and Cherry Cola Story Team"
  description="Default progression preset. Swap Strawberry Crepe for Ion or Herb when survival fails."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059","cookie0181","cookie0037","cookie0018","cookie4019","cookie0250","cookie4013","cookie4010","cookie0126","cookie0081","cookie0518","cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet0111","pet4005","pet4001"]}
/>

The first row contains Macaron, Scorpion, Cheesecake, Skating Queen, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, and Cherry Cola. The second row contains Brightseeker, Pinot Noir, Pomegranate, Princess Bari, Strawberry Crepe, and Dark Choco.

The Pets are Hot Doggie, Chargemellow, and Holy Baby Drop, in that order. This loadout uses level 20 Pets. It keeps the offensive Pet package rather than reserving a slot for knock-up resistance.

Start here, then let a failed fight tell you whether to switch. If a boss repeatedly throws the group into the air, use the next preset. If the team stays on its feet but loses Cookies to damage, make a survival swap within this one.

Keep Cherry Cola when you can. For Bari's own Rune choices and the difference between story and Arena survival, use the [Princess Bari build guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-princess-bari-cookie-build-team/). This guide focuses on which whole team to bring, rather than prescribing a new Rune page for every encounter.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="anti-knock-up-team" title="The anti-knock-up team and its Pet slot">

The second preset uses Wind Archer, Ion Cookie Robot, and Herb. It does not include Bari or Cherry Cola. Copy it as its own formation instead of assuming it is the first team with one Pet changed.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Story Knock-up Resistance Team"
  description="Wind Archer, Ion, and Herb with Candy Shade Pouch for knock-up resistance."
  cookieIds={["cookie0070","cookie4013","cookie4010","cookie0018","cookie0136","cookie0063","cookie0059","cookie0181","cookie0126","cookie4019","cookie0518","cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet0228","pet0111","pet4001"]}
/>

The first row contains Wind Archer, Brightseeker, Pinot Noir, Skating Queen, Ion Cookie Robot, and Herb. The second row contains Macaron, Scorpion, Pomegranate, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, Strawberry Crepe, and Dark Choco.

Use Candy Shade Pouch, Hot Doggie, and Holy Baby Drop. Candy Shade Pouch is level 12 in this preset; the other two Pets are level 20. The pouch is the round, red-and-green Pet, which makes it easy to distinguish from Panda Dumpling.

**Use Candy Shade Pouch for the knock-up resistance job when you own it.** Its resistance and extra HP make it worth trying even at level 1. If you do not own the pouch, keep Panda Dumpling as the fallback.

Against Cool Mint, try pulling the fight toward the seven o'clock or eleven o'clock corner instead of staying in open space. Think lower-left or upper-left on the arena. Get the group into position, then let it attack; repeatedly dragging everyone around can make it harder to judge whether the setup works.

Ion and Herb already occupy slots in this team. Do not try to add either again by removing Strawberry Crepe. If you need the simpler Crepe replacement rule, apply it to the default lineup, where those Cookies are absent.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="gingercraven-power-team" title="GingerCraven: check Power before adding more protection">

This third preset keeps Bari, adds Herb, and uses Wind Archer. It leaves out Cherry Cola and Strawberry Crepe. Wind Archer is here for accounts that gain useful Power from including him.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Bari and Wind Archer GingerCraven Team"
  description="Bari and Herb stay. Use Wind Archer when his investment helps close the Power gap."
  cookieIds={["cookie0070","cookie4013","cookie4010","cookie0126","cookie0081","cookie0063","cookie0059","cookie0181","cookie0037","cookie0018","cookie4019","cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet4001","pet0111","pet4005"]}
/>

The first row contains Wind Archer, Brightseeker, Pinot Noir, Pomegranate, Princess Bari, and Herb. The second row contains Macaron, Scorpion, Cheesecake, Skating Queen, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, and Dark Choco.

The Pet order is Holy Baby Drop, Hot Doggie, and Chargemellow. All three are level 20 in this setup.

Wind Archer's slot answers a specific problem: the team survives, but damage hardly lands. If your Wind Archer raises the formation's Power enough to help, he can earn that place even when you rarely use him elsewhere. Cherry Cola can take his slot instead. Compare the result on your account; a poorly developed Wind Archer is not automatically the stronger choice.

The [stage Power and damage guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-power-guide-stage-damage/) explains why an apparently sensible team can still struggle below a stage's recommended strength. Check that gap before spending another evening rearranging supports.

GingerBright needs the same context. His ATK Down can help beginners survive, but keeping him by habit can cost a developed team Power and damage. Once incoming hits are manageable, the extra protection may no longer justify that trade. Use him while his ATK Down keeps you alive. Reconsider the slot once you can survive without it.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="story-survival-swaps" title="Fix survival without replacing the whole roster">

In the default Bari and Cherry Cola formation, replace Strawberry Crepe with Ion Cookie Robot if the team needs a shield. Try Herb in that slot if another healer would help the group recover. Start with one change and repeat the same stage.

Watch who dies and when. A Cookie that falls before the supports act needs a different answer from a team that survives most of the fight but slowly runs out of healing. Keep Cherry Cola while testing these support changes, rather than removing an attacker and a protector together.

Story difficulty reductions also change how much defense a developed account needs. If the hits no longer threaten the team, an old survival-heavy preset can become unnecessarily slow. Restore damage when the defensive slot has finished its job.

Use the [Cookie tier list](/tier-list/) to compare longer-term investments, but judge a substitution in the fight where you need it. A high-ranked Cookie with weak promotion can still lower the useful strength of your current formation. Check whether the replacement solves the problem that stopped your last run.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="redberry-staircase" title="Redberry: stop chasing and use the stairs">

Redberry is the awkward exception to the default progression team. Close contact can trigger another teleport, leaving your attackers chasing instead of finishing the enemy. More retries with the same approach can repeat the same problem.

Remove Princess Bari and Cherry Cola, then add Tiger Lily and Cool Mint. Treat this as a separate Redberry adjustment; the three complete presets above cover the broader story plan. Watch whether the replacement changes the enemy's movement before judging only the final damage total.

Move toward six or seven o'clock from the opening, as though you are retreating. The useful landmark is the staircase toward the bottom of the arena. **Stop just below the stairs with the enemies above them.** Do not continue all the way to the bottom edge of the map.

Start fighting from that arrangement. The clock direction gets you into the right area, while the staircase tells you where to stop. If the first attempt looks wrong, adjust where you halt rather than changing several Cookies and the route at once. It may take a couple of attempts to stop in the right place.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="story-retry-check" title="Keep the next retry useful">

Before you spend, name the failure. If the formation stays airborne, try the resistance preset. If allies die, test the appropriate shield or healing slot. If everybody survives while the boss barely loses health, inspect Power and damage. If Redberry keeps escaping, change the approach and stopping point.

Save a successful version before moving on. You can keep the ordinary team ready for the next stretch of stages and return to a boss preset only when its mechanic appears again. That saves more effort than rebuilding all twelve slots from memory after every roadblock.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="story-presets-faq" title="Story team FAQ">

### Which team should I try first?

Start with the Bari and Cherry Cola preset for routine story stages. Switch when a specific failure gives you a reason: repeated knock-ups, a GingerCraven damage problem, or Redberry teleporting away from close-range attackers.

### Should I level Candy Shade Pouch before using it?

Try it in the anti-knock-up slot as soon as you have it. The recommendation favors its resistance and HP contribution even at low level. Keep Panda Dumpling as the fallback when you do not own the pouch.

### Is Wind Archer required for GingerCraven?

No. His role in this preset is to help an account raise Power when damage barely lands. Cherry Cola can replace him. Choose the version that works with your promotion and equipment instead of forcing an underbuilt Wind Archer into the team.

### Where should I stop when pulling Redberry south?

Stop just below the southern staircase while the enemies remain above it. Head toward six or seven o'clock from the start, but do not retreat all the way to the arena's bottom edge.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-beginner-progression-.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Most early walls in CookieRun: Crumble are self-inflicted. The game throws ten upgrade systems at you, covers the screen in claim buttons, and quietly lets you spend premium currency on the least useful banner. Then a boss survives the 30-second timer with a sliver of health and your account feels broken.

It probably is not broken. Your power is sitting in unclaimed menus, or you spent materials on a system that pays back too slowly. Fix the route and the same account can move again.

<GuideSection id="protect-your-crystals" title="Protect your crystals from bad pulls">

Cookie and Pet pulls have separate Gacha levels. Every pull adds one EXP to the matching Gacha level, and higher levels add higher rarities to the pool. That means a pull gives you a unit or duplicate now and moves the account toward a better pool later.

Pet Gacha reaches its top listed rarity sooner. SSR Pets can appear from level 2, where the displayed SSR rate is 1.6%. Cookie Gacha takes longer. SSR Cookies enter the regular pool at level 4, while TSSR Cookies do not enter that pool until level 6. A special Oven Wanderer banner can give you access to a TSSR much earlier than the normal level gate.

The easy mistake is dumping crystals into Premium Cookie Gacha because it looks permanent and safe. Pickup banners are usually the better place for those crystals. Their pulls still count toward Cookie Gacha EXP, but their milestone track can also give extra rewards and copies of the featured Cookie. The base rates are not magically better. You simply get more back for crossing the same number of pull milestones.

Pet Gacha needs a different rule. Use Pet tickets from quests, missions, and check-ins. Keep crystals for Cookie pickup banners. Pet rates become generous early enough that spending premium currency there solves a problem you were likely to solve with free tickets anyway.

<GuideTip title="The short version">

Spend crystals on a Cookie pickup banner you are willing to commit to. Spend Pet tickets in Pet Gacha. Use the special currency from check-ins and the free pass track on the Oven Wanderer banner because crystals cannot replace that currency.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="use-the-quest-loop" title="Use the quest loop until it stops paying">

The repeating quest chain can feel tedious, but it is the engine behind fast early progress. Its rewards feed Cookie pulls, Pet pulls, Bakery gear rolls, account EXP, and duplicates. Those pulls raise Gacha levels, which improve future pools. One boring quest can touch half the account.

Follow the chain instead of wandering between menus. When it asks for summons, use the tickets it just handed you. When it points to the Oven, stoke or roll the requested amount. The next quest often replaces enough of what you spent to keep the loop moving.

Do the daily and weekly missions before they reset. Open check-in rewards even on days when you do not plan to play. The free side of each pass also matters. It can hold regular summon currency and the special material used for the Oven Wanderer banner. You do not need to buy a pass to claim its free track.

Claim collection bonuses when new Cookies, Pets, or promotions add a notification. They include crystals and permanent stats. Leaving ten red dots untouched is like keeping cash under the doormat, except the doormat is also making your team weaker.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="level-the-oven" title="Level the Oven without gear panic">

The Oven has its own progress bar. Stoke it enough times and its level rises, which opens better gear rarities. Early gear is temporary by design, so treating every piece like an endgame project burns time for almost no return.

Excellent+ works at the very beginning. Move Auto to Magic+ once its appearance rate is practical. Pick the best tier sitting around a 10% rate or lower, then check the Oven when the quest loop brings you back.

Equip the piece with higher displayed power. Sell the weaker leftovers and feed the returned red currency back into Oven levels. Early Epic gear may have only one substat slot, so a perfect substat hunt barely has room to matter. Damage is nice when two pieces are close, but raw power is a better sorting tool during the first stretch.

Gear presets become useful when you own several developed PvP or specialized teams. Before that, one general set is easier to maintain. Presets full of half-finished equipment create work without clearing another stage.

<GuideTip title="When to care about substats">

Wait until higher rarity gear stays equipped for more than a few hours and gives you enough substat slots to build around. Early on, wear the bigger number, sell the smaller number, and keep the Oven moving.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="push-dungeons" title="Push dungeons before farming old floors">

Daily Dungeon tickets refill, so capped tickets are lost progress. Clear each dungeon every day, but do not settle into an easy floor too early. New levels carry first-clear rewards, and milestone rewards add another layer on top. Every fifth level can pay summons. EXP stages also hand out a large burst when you push their first clears.

Coin Dungeon matters because its rewards feed Resolve upgrades. Other Daily Dungeons provide research materials and the account currencies that unlock permanent power. If the next floor is close, improve the team and try it. Repeating the comfortable floor first means giving up the exact first-clear reward that might have pushed the account forward.

Crumble Dungeon scores the wider roster rather than only your usual lineup. Keep the main team capped, then spread spare Cookie EXP across units that will join the attempt. Broad leveling pays back immediately here.

In Arena, set both attack and defense lineups. Spend attacks on opponents below your displayed power while the account is young. Losing one match is not a disaster, but allowing attempts to sit at the cap throws away Fame currency and rank rewards.

Plaque Tower is worth climbing until the next floor refuses to move. Floor 21 can secure Cheesecake Cookie if your pulls missed her, and later floors award useful SR Cookies such as Orange Cookie. A wall around floor 100 is normal for an early account. Take the rewards below it, improve elsewhere, and come back.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="build-permanent-power" title="Build permanent account power before blaming the team">

Resolve turns ordinary coins into stats that apply across the account. Put early points into attack, then fill defensive stats. Many campaign walls are timer failures, so more damage usually changes the result sooner than extra durability. If Cookies are dying well before the timer, adjust that order and buy the defense you are missing.

Arena feeds Fame, another permanent damage upgrade. This is why Arena attempts should not sit unused. You are building a stat layer that follows the account back into other modes.

Gnome Laboratory research works the same way. Follow the damage path while normal progress is cheap. For special research choices, research speed is a strong first pick because time becomes the gate before materials do. Extra Daily Dungeon entries are also useful, but a faster laboratory keeps every later project moving.

Stellar Links adds stats through constellation coverage. Shuffle until an early layout reaches roughly 60% area or better. Lock a strong section if the rest needs rerolling, but watch the rising cost. A perfect day-one board can consume currency that would have produced several good boards. Constellation points come from check-ins, pass rewards, and unlocked exchanges.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="move-cookies-in-combat" title="Move your Cookies when the timer is the enemy">

You can drag the whole Cookie group during combat with a finger or mouse. The team stops attacking while it moves, so random shuffling loses damage. One deliberate move can save far more time than it costs.

Bosses sometimes spawn away from your starting position or arrive with enemies spread around them. Drag the team into the middle of the pack as soon as the targets appear. Area attacks begin connecting with more enemies, short-range Cookies spend less time walking, and the 30-second timer starts producing damage instead of travel time.

Try this before spending another pile of upgrades on a stage that ends at 2% boss health. If the same lineup clears after one clean reposition, the account was strong enough. It was standing in the wrong place.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="build-a-lineup" title="Build a lineup that works with your account">

Keep the active lineup at its current level cap. Level reset is free while the reset screen shows no cost, so a new pull does not force you to abandon all the EXP invested in the old slot. Check the confirmation screen before every reset in case the rule changes, reclaim the materials, and move them to the replacement.

Start with one Defense Cookie. Move to two when the front line collapses, and use a third only when a mode keeps deleting the team. Two Supports is a dependable baseline. Attack buffs, defense reduction, or healing can add more than another mediocre attacker. Fill the rest with damage dealers that connect to your Synergy setup.

Hold a Cookie in the lineup screen to inspect its Synergy. Granted effects need matching receivers. Duration, for example, increases skill duration for allies that receive that Synergy. A row of impressive Granted icons does nothing for Cookies that cannot receive them. Use the [Team Builder](/tools/team-builder/) to check which matches become active before spending EXP on a replacement.

Sugar Runes unlock early. Put the main Rune effect on every Cookie in the working lineup before chasing ideal rolls. More slots open with promotion stars, so heavy rerolling makes more sense after those slots exist.

You do not need twelve SSR Cookies to start. Popcorn Cookie brings strong area damage. Orange Cookie adds CRIT Chance Up and grants Multi-strike. Cheesecake Cookie supplies ATK Up. Poison Mushroom Cookie is an accessible R option for area damage over time, while Blackberry Cookie and Dark Cherry Cookie can fill early damage slots. Browse their exact Role, Element, Buff, and Synergy data in the [Cookie index](/cookies/), then use the units your account can level now.

Before committing rare materials, check the current [Tier List](/tier-list/) for long-term value and the [recommended teams](/teams/) for complete lineups. Those pages are a filter, not a shopping list: keep the cheaper Cookie when it already fills the same role and Synergy on your account.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pick-pets" title="Pick Pets for the problem you can see">

Damage Pets are the default because the timer causes more early failures than survival. CRIT damage and Element-specific bonuses become better when the lineup already leans into those stats. If a team uses several Fire Cookies, a Pet that buffs Fire allies has a real job. Adding it to a mixed roster because its rarity is high does not create the same payoff.

Sweet and Sour is a CRIT damage option tied to the referral menu. It accepts another player's MID once. Your own reward progresses when invited players clear Chapter 1, and five successful referrals can complete the duplicate track if that reward is still listed. Check the in-game panel because referral rewards can rotate.

Do not force damage if Cookies are dying. Swap one Pet for recovery or defense and run the same stage again. The searchable [Pets page](/pets/) includes full effect text, which makes this comparison much faster than opening every shelter portrait.

Visit the Shelter whenever it shows a claim notification. Pet levels, promotions, and collection bonuses are small alone, but ignoring all of them creates a surprisingly large stat hole.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="join-a-guild" title="Join a guild before you feel ready">

A guild gives you gift boxes, research buffs, a help system, and its own shop. Ask for help on long Gnome Laboratory timers. Return the favor when other members request it. This costs very little and cuts one of the slowest early gates.

Donate, but do not empty your crystal balance to prove that you are friendly. Normal play produces guild currency, and that currency is the part you care about. Sugar Flame is a strong first shop purchase while Oven levels are cheap. Its value drops once a single Oven level costs hundreds of thousands, so switch priorities instead of buying it forever.

Dungeon keys, Sugar Rune materials, constellation points, and random SSR boxes become reasonable later purchases. Buy what opens the next useful action. A key you can spend today beats a material for a system you have not developed.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="use-idle-rewards" title="Use idle rewards correctly when progress stops">

Offline Auto Hunt stores up to eight hours by default. Research can extend the cap. Claim before the timer fills, use the lucky rolls available each day, and convert the haul into levels, Resolve, gear, and research before attempting the wall again.

While you are online, the offline box does not appear to fill because income goes straight into your inventory. Watch the gold counter and item totals instead. The system is still working.

At some point, strategy stops fixing the numbers. The boss survives too long and every sensible upgrade is spent. Close the game. The idle system turns time away into stats for the next attempt. Logging off can be faster than rearranging a team that already makes sense.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="daily-route" title="A practical route for every login">

Use this order when the menus start feeling like chores:

1. Claim mail, check-ins, pass rewards, collection bonuses, Shelter notifications, and guild gifts.
2. Spend Daily Dungeon tickets while pushing the highest clearable floor.
3. Use Arena attempts before they cap and check the defense lineup.
4. Follow the repeating quest chain until it asks for progress you cannot make yet.
5. Spend Cookie pickup pulls and free Pet tickets, then claim new Gacha level rewards.
6. Equip higher power Oven gear, sell leftovers, and stoke the Oven.
7. Cap the main lineup, unlock missing Sugar Runes, and spend Resolve coins with the current wall in mind.
8. Check Laboratory research, Stellar Links, the guild shop, and Plaque Tower milestones.
9. Push campaign stages. Reposition the team manually when enemies spawn apart.
10. When the next wall is numerical, let Auto Hunt build the next upgrade batch.

This order keeps limited attempts moving and gives premium currency one job. It also tells you why the account is stuck. Fix the missing stat, ignored mode, weak formation, or bad position. Throwing crystals at all four turns a small wall into an expensive one.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="beginner-faq" title="CookieRun: Crumble beginner FAQ">

### Should beginners spend crystals on the regular Cookie banner?

Pickup banners are usually the better crystal target because their pull milestones can add rewards and extra copies. Pulls there still raise Cookie Gacha EXP. Save Pet pulls for tickets earned through quests and other free rewards.

### What should I upgrade first when I get stuck?

Raise the main lineup to its current cap, spend available Resolve coins with attack first, equip higher power Oven gear, unlock the main Sugar Rune on each active Cookie, and claim collection bonuses. Try the stage again before replacing half the team.

### Should I farm an easy Daily Dungeon stage?

Push the highest new stage you can clear before repeating an older one. First clears and milestone floors pay extra rewards, and every fifth level can add summons. Farm lower stages after the next push stops working.

### How many tanks and supports should a beginner team use?

Start with one Defense Cookie if the team survives comfortably. Move toward two when enemies delete the front line. Two Supports is a dependable baseline, while the remaining slots can carry damage and complete useful Synergy matches.

### Why do Auto Hunt rewards look empty while I am online?

Online Auto Hunt income goes directly into the inventory instead of building in the offline claim window. Offline rewards store for up to eight hours before research upgrades extend that cap.

</GuideSection>
