New levels carry first-clear rewards, and milestone rewards add another layer on top. Every fifth level can pay summons. EXP stages also hand out a large burst when you push their first clears.

Coin Dungeon matters because its rewards feed Resolve upgrades. Other Daily Dungeons provide research materials and the account currencies that unlock permanent power. If the next floor is close, improve the team and try it. Repeating the comfortable floor first means giving up the exact first-clear reward that might have pushed the account forward.

Crumble Dungeon scores the wider roster rather than only your usual lineup. Keep the main team capped, then spread spare Cookie EXP across units that will join the attempt. Broad leveling pays back immediately here.

In Arena, set both attack and defense lineups. Spend attacks on opponents below your displayed power while the account is young. Losing one match is not a disaster, but allowing attempts to sit at the cap throws away Fame currency and rank rewards.

Plaque Tower is worth climbing until the next floor refuses to move. Floor 21 can secure Cheesecake Cookie if your pulls missed her, and later floors award useful SR Cookies such as Orange Cookie. A wall around floor 100 is normal for an early account. Take the rewards below it, improve elsewhere, and come back.
Push dungeons before farming old floors
segments.name: title

segments.text: Resolve turns ordinary coins into stats that apply across the account. Put early points into attack, then fill defensive stats. Many campaign walls are timer failures, so more damage usually changes the result sooner than extra durability. If Cookies are dying well before the timer, adjust that order and buy the defense you are missing.
Arena feeds Fame, another permanent damage upgrade. This is why Arena attempts should not sit unused. You are building a stat layer that follows the account back into other modes.

Gnome Laboratory research works the same way. Follow the damage path while normal progress is cheap. For special research choices, research speed is a strong first pick because time becomes the gate before materials do. Extra Daily Dungeon entries are also useful, but a faster laboratory keeps every later project moving.

Stellar Links adds stats through constellation coverage. Shuffle until an early layout reaches roughly 60% area or better. Lock a strong section if the rest needs rerolling, but watch the rising cost. A perfect day-one board can consume currency that would have produced several good boards. Constellation points come from check-ins, pass rewards, and unlocked exchanges.
Build permanent account power before blaming the team
segments.name: title

segments.text: You can drag the whole Cookie group during combat with a finger or mouse. The team stops attacking while it moves, so random shuffling loses damage. One deliberate move can save far more time than it costs.

Bosses sometimes spawn away from your starting position or arrive with enemies spread around them. Drag the team into the middle of the pack as soon as the targets appear. Area attacks begin connecting with more enemies, short-range Cookies spend less time walking, and the 30-second timer starts producing damage instead of travel time.

Try this before spending another pile of upgrades on a stage that ends at 2% boss health. If the same lineup clears after one clean reposition, the account was strong enough. It was standing in the wrong place.
Move your Cookies when the timer is the enemy
segments.name: title

segments.text: Keep the active lineup at its current level cap. Level reset is free while the reset screen shows no cost, so a new pull does not force you to abandon all the EXP invested in the old slot. Check the confirmation screen before every reset in case the rule changes, reclaim the materials, and move them to the replacement.

Start with one Defense Cookie. Move to two when the front line collapses, and use a third only when a mode keeps deleting the team. Two Supports is a dependable baseline. Attack buffs, defense reduction, or healing can add more than another mediocre attacker. Fill the rest with damage dealers that connect to your Synergy setup.

Hold a Cookie in the lineup screen to inspect its Synergy. Granted effects need matching receivers. Duration, for example, increases skill duration for allies that receive that Synergy. A row of impressive Granted icons does nothing for Cookies that cannot receive them. Use the
Team Builder
to check which matches become active before spending EXP on a replacement.

Sugar Runes unlock early. Put the main Rune effect on every Cookie in the working lineup before chasing ideal rolls. More slots open with promotion stars, so heavy rerolling makes more sense after those slots exist.

You do not need twelve SSR Cookies to start. Popcorn Cookie brings strong area damage. Orange Cookie adds CRIT Chance Up and grants Multi-strike. Cheesecake Cookie supplies ATK Up. Poison Mushroom Cookie is an accessible R option for area damage over time, while Blackberry Cookie and Dark Cherry Cookie can fill early damage slots. Browse their exact Role, Element, Buff, and Synergy data in the
Cookie index
, then use the units your account can level now.
Before committing rare materials, check the current
Tier List
for long-term value and the
recommended teams
for complete lineups. Those pages are a filter, not a shopping list: keep the cheaper Cookie when it already fills the same role and Synergy on your account.
Build a lineup that works with your account
segments.name: title

segments.text: Damage Pets are the default because the timer causes more early failures than survival. CRIT damage and Element-specific bonuses become better when the lineup already leans into those stats. If a team uses several Fire Cookies, a Pet that buffs Fire allies has a real job. Adding it to a mixed roster because its rarity is high does not create the same payoff.

Sweet and Sour is a CRIT damage option tied to the referral menu. It accepts another player's MID once. Your own reward progresses when invited players clear Chapter 1, and five successful referrals can complete the duplicate track if that reward is still listed. Check the in-game panel because referral rewards can rotate.
Do not force damage if Cookies are dying. Swap one Pet for recovery or defense and run the same stage again. The searchable
Pets page
includes full effect text, which makes this comparison much faster than opening every shelter portrait.
Visit the Shelter whenever it shows a claim notification. Pet levels, promotions, and collection bonuses are small alone, but ignoring all of them creates a surprisingly large stat hole.
Pick Pets for the problem you can see
segments.name: title

segments.text: A guild gives you gift boxes, research buffs, a help system, and its own shop. Ask for help on long Gnome Laboratory timers. Return the favor when other members request it. This costs very little and cuts one of the slowest early gates.

Donate, but do not empty your crystal balance to prove that you are friendly. Normal play produces guild currency, and that currency is the part you care about. Sugar Flame is a strong first shop purchase while Oven levels are cheap. Its value drops once a single Oven level costs hundreds of thousands, so switch priorities instead of buying it forever.

Dungeon keys, Sugar Rune materials, constellation points, and random SSR boxes become reasonable later purchases. Buy what opens the next useful action. A key you can spend today beats a material for a system you have not developed.
Join a guild before you feel ready
segments.name: title

segments.text: Offline Auto Hunt stores up to eight hours by default. Research can extend the cap. Claim before the timer fills, use the lucky rolls available each day, and convert the haul into levels, Resolve, gear, and research before attempting the wall again.
While you are online, the offline box does not appear to fill because income goes straight into your inventory. Watch the gold counter and item totals instead. The system is still working.

At some point, strategy stops fixing the numbers. The boss survives too long and every sensible upgrade is spent. Close the game. The idle system turns time away into stats for the next attempt. Logging off can be faster than rearranging a team that already makes sense.
Use idle rewards correctly when progress stops
segments.name: title

segments.text: Use this order when the menus start feeling like chores:
Claim mail, check-ins, pass rewards, collection bonuses, Shelter notifications, and guild gifts.
Spend Daily Dungeon tickets while pushing the highest clearable floor.
Use Arena attempts before they cap and check the defense lineup.
Follow the repeating quest chain until it asks for progress you cannot make yet.
Spend Cookie pickup pulls and free Pet tickets, then claim new Gacha level rewards.
Equip higher power Oven gear, sell leftovers, and stoke the Oven.
Cap the main lineup, unlock missing Sugar Runes, and spend Resolve coins with the current wall in mind.
Check Laboratory research, Stellar Links, the guild shop, and Plaque Tower milestones.
Push campaign stages. Reposition the team manually when enemies spawn apart.
When the next wall is numerical, let Auto Hunt build the next upgrade batch.

This order keeps limited attempts moving and gives premium currency one job. It also tells you why the account is stuck. Fix the missing stat, ignored mode, weak formation, or bad position. Throwing crystals at all four turns a small wall into an expensive one.
A practical route for every login
segments.name: title

segments.text: Should beginners spend crystals on the regular Cookie banner?

Pickup banners are usually the better crystal target because their pull milestones can add rewards and extra copies. Pulls there still raise Cookie Gacha EXP. Save Pet pulls for tickets earned through quests and other free rewards.
What should I upgrade first when I get stuck?

Raise the main lineup to its current cap, spend available Resolve coins with attack first, equip higher power Oven gear, unlock the main Sugar Rune on each active Cookie, and claim collection bonuses. Try the stage again before replacing half the team.
Should I farm an easy Daily Dungeon stage?

Push the highest new stage you can clear before repeating an older one. First clears and milestone floors pay extra rewards, and every fifth level can add summons. Farm lower stages after the next push stops working.
How many tanks and supports should a beginner team use?

Start with one Defense Cookie if the team survives comfortably. Move toward two when enemies delete the front line. Two Supports is a dependable baseline, while the remaining slots can carry damage and complete useful Synergy matches.
Why do Auto Hunt rewards look empty while I am online?
Online Auto Hunt income goes directly into the inventory instead of building in the offline claim window. Offline rewards store for up to eight hours before research upgrades extend that cap.
CookieRun: Crumble beginner FAQ
segments.name: title

cookie-run-crumble-brightseeker-cookie-b.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Brightseeker Cookie offers something raw damage charts rarely measure: fewer ruined runs. Scorpion Cookie can still post the bigger number, but only when her Venom Sting stacks land, the team survives, and you steer the fight correctly. Brightseeker trades some of that ceiling for a cleaner auto setup that works across stages, daily dungeons, tower floors, and guild bosses.

The catch is price. Brightseeker becomes much more convincing at five stars, when the extra drone joins the skill. If your Scorpion is already promoted and wearing excellent Sugar Runes, changing immediately can waste a painful amount of EXP and promotion material. This guide shows where Brightseeker earns that cost, how Pinot Noir supports the build, and which of the two complete lineups fits each mode.

<GuideSection id="brightseeker-vs-scorpion" title="Brightseeker or Scorpion: pick the problem you want">

Scorpion remains the damage-ceiling choice. Her best runs reward strong Sugar Runes, clean debuff stacks, and active positioning. If you enjoy retrying a stage until every cast lines up, she can push faster than Brightseeker.

Brightseeker is the consistency choice. The drone damage does not ask you to watch Venom Sting counters every few seconds. Movement can improve a run, but most fights do not collapse because you left the team in its starting position. That makes Brightseeker especially useful for players who want to clear while doing something more exciting than supervising an orange stack icon.

Do not call this a universal upgrade. Keep Scorpion when she has better promotion and carefully rolled Runes. Consider Brightseeker when your Scorpion build is weak, her stack routine keeps failing, or you value repeatable auto clears over the fastest possible push. The [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/) gives useful context, but your promotion gap matters more than one letter beside a name.

<GuideTip title="Short version">
Use Scorpion for the highest manual ceiling. Use Brightseeker when you want a steadier run with less stack management.
</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="five-star-breakpoint" title="Why five stars changes the decision">

At five stars, Brightseeker adds another drone to the skill. This is not a tiny stat bump hidden behind a prettier border. The extra summon raises the amount of work each cast can do and makes Brightseeker credible as the main replacement for Scorpion in a developed account.

That breakpoint is also expensive. A player with a strong five-star Scorpion should not drain every reserve just to field a two-star Brightseeker. Test the lower-promotion version with your current gear first. If the team becomes easier to run but loses too much damage, keep saving. If Scorpion's weak Runes already leave her below expectations, Brightseeker can win the practical comparison before five stars simply by finishing more attempts.

For a spending account that can reach five stars without starving the rest of the roster, Brightseeker is a reasonable main-team project. For everyone else, five stars is the target, not permission to empty the account today.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="general-pve-team" title="General PvE auto team">

This is the broad-use formation for story stages, daily dungeons, and many boss encounters. Pinot Noir grants Multi-strike, while Chargemellow adds another Multi-strike point and raises ATK for receivers. Licorice gives the lineup breathing room when incoming damage becomes messy. Holy Baby Drop supplies teamwide ATK, and Hot Doggie adds Skill Amp.

The formation reached the Stage 200 range without needing a complete rebuild. It also asks for less constant steering than the Scorpion version. That does not mean every stage is hands-free. Rowdy Truck can still delete Cookies early unless you move the formation toward the 7 o'clock side.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Brightseeker and Pinot Noir general PvE team"
  description="Use this as the default auto shell for stages and daily dungeons. Chargemellow completes the Multi-strike package while Licorice keeps difficult openings stable."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0515", "cookie3001", "cookie0126", "cookie4019", "cookie0518", "cookie4013", "cookie0503", "cookie4010", "cookie0018", "cookie4024", "cookie0063"]}
  petIds={["pet4001", "pet0111", "pet4005"]}
/>

Pinot Noir deserves more than the label of synergy switch. Healing Received Down matters when enemies erase your progress, and the resistance utility can keep the formation from being scattered. If you are still deciding how far to promote Pinot Noir, the [Pinot Noir build guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-pinot-noir-cookie-build/) explains the five-star stopping point.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-team" title="Arena and high-floor benchmark team">

Brightseeker is less dominant in Arena than in PvE. Espresso remains excellent because control and immediate pressure matter more when the opponent can end the fight quickly. Do not replace a trained Espresso merely because Brightseeker performs well in stages.

The lineup below uses Espresso, Wind Archer, and a sturdier Majestic King Choco Drop pet package. Pinot Noir stays because anti-heal and team utility remain useful against recovery-heavy opponents. Melon Soda appears in the tested formation, but Milky Way is the stronger Arena upgrade if you have enough EXP to train her properly.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Pinot Noir Arena and tower team"
  description="This version keeps Espresso for Arena pressure and uses Majestic King Choco Drop for more durability. Brightseeker can replace Espresso for easier medal farming when conserving EXP matters more than rank."
  cookieIds={["cookie0070", "cookie0515", "cookie3001", "cookie0037", "cookie0513", "cookie4024", "cookie0059", "cookie4018", "cookie4010", "cookie0126", "cookie4019", "cookie0063"]}
  petIds={["pet4001", "pet0111", "pet4003"]}
/>

Players farming medals against lower-power opponents can make a cheaper compromise. Replace Espresso with Brightseeker and reuse the investment already made for PvE. You give up some Arena sharpness, but you avoid feeding another expensive Cookie simply to beat matches you were likely to win anyway.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="mode-swaps" title="Small swaps for tower, bosses, and dungeons">

The useful part of this build is not that one formation solves everything. It is that the same shell needs only small changes.

- **Plaque Tower:** Try Wind Archer in Licorice's slot when survival is comfortable but damage has stalled. That one change turned a floor 500 wall into a climb toward floor 850 in testing.
- **Daily dungeons:** Start with the general PvE lineup. Its stable opening and Multi-strike package fit most daily fights without a special preset.
- **Split or awkward bosses:** Chargemellow is normally correct, but Panda Dumpling can perform better when a boss pattern values the alternative pet effect more than another Multi-strike point.
- **Rowdy Truck:** Move toward 7 o'clock before the opening burst. This fight can punish a stationary auto team even when the rest of the chapter does not.
- **Guild boss:** Brightseeker works here too, especially when consistent cycles matter more than chasing Scorpion's perfect attempt.

Save the original formation before experimenting. One bad replacement should not turn a useful preset into a memory test.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="sugar-runes" title="Best Sugar Rune stats">

Brightseeker wants stats that improve the drone cycle directly. Prioritize **ATK**, **Skill Amp**, **CRIT DMG**, and **CRIT Chance**. Do not force a beautiful-looking Rune if half its value lands on a stat the kit barely uses. A plain ATK roll can beat an expensive reroll full of decorative nonsense.

Pinot Noir has a different job. **Focus** is the first priority when enemies resist important effects. For Arena, add **Damage Reduction** so Pinot survives long enough to matter, then **Skill Haste** when faster cycling improves the matchup. The [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) explains why a useful substat can beat a larger Power number.

Keep separate Rune presets if you use Pinot Noir in both Arena and PvE. Rebuilding the same set before every session saves materials only in theory. In practice, it mostly saves you from playing.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="who-should-build" title="Who should spend on Brightseeker">

Build Brightseeker now if you can reach five stars without delaying the whole account, you dislike managing Scorpion stacks, or you want one ranged damage option that travels well between PvE modes. Wait if Scorpion is already far ahead, your promotion materials are thin, or Arena is your only serious goal.

Pinot Noir is the connective piece for players leaning into Multi-strike. Brightseeker does not replace the need for frontline, healing, and mode-specific control. Copy the full PvE formation first, run the stage that currently blocks you, then change one slot at a time. The site's [recommended teams](/teams/) can show which established formation matches the mode, and the [Team Builder](/tools/team-builder/) lets you save the exact version your account can field.

The best decision is pleasantly unglamorous. Keep Scorpion when you can support the high ceiling. Choose Brightseeker when reliable auto clears save more progress than another evening of retries.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="brightseeker-faq" title="Brightseeker Cookie FAQ">

### Is Brightseeker Cookie better than Scorpion Cookie?

Scorpion has the higher damage ceiling with strong Sugar Runes, clean Venom Sting stacks, and active control. Brightseeker is easier to run on auto and produces steadier results across PvE modes, so the better choice depends on promotion, Runes, and how much control you want to use.

### Does Brightseeker Cookie need five stars?

Brightseeker works below five stars, especially when your Scorpion build is weak, but five stars adds another drone and is the promotion breakpoint that makes a full replacement much easier to justify.

### What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Brightseeker Cookie?

Prioritize ATK, Skill Amp, CRIT DMG, and CRIT Chance for Brightseeker. These stats improve the damage cycle directly without asking the Cookie to fill a control or survival role.

### Which team should I use with Brightseeker and Pinot Noir?

Start with the general PvE lineup shown above: Macaron, Rye, Melon Soda, Pomegranate, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, Strawberry Crepe, Brightseeker, Licorice, Pinot Noir, Skating Queen, Nameless Cake Hound, and Herb, with Holy Baby Drop, Hot Doggie, and Chargemellow.

### Is Brightseeker Cookie good in Arena?

Brightseeker is usable in Arena, but Espresso usually brings stronger pressure in serious matches. Brightseeker makes more sense as an EXP-saving replacement when you farm medals against weaker opponents and do not care about pushing the highest rank.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-chardonnay-auto-story.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

An auto team loses its appeal when you have to drag it back onto the boss every few stages. Bari and Cherry Cola now have a better chance of staying on the right target, and Chardonnay takes the support slot that Macaron held in earlier story setups. That gives this formation a useful job: push ordinary stages with fewer interruptions, then change the part that caused a difficult boss attempt to fail.

Start with the full twelve-Cookie lineup below. Keep a second Pet setup ready for knock-ups, and resist the urge to replace half the team after one loss. This is a developed roster, so the names alone will not reproduce its progress on a fresh account.

<GuideSection id="chardonnay-story-lineup" title="Copy the Chardonnay story preset">

The first row, from left to right, is Brightseeker, Rye, Cheesecake, Skating Queen, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, and Cherry Cola.

The second row is Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pomegranate, Princess Bari, Strawberry Crepe, and Dark Choco. Use Hot Doggie, Holy Baby Drop, and Chargemellow in that order. Milk carries the captain marker in this setup.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Chardonnay, Bari and Cherry Cola story team"
  description="Copy both rows in order, keep Milk as captain, and start with Hot Doggie, Holy Baby Drop, and Chargemellow."
  cookieIds={["cookie4013", "cookie0515", "cookie0037", "cookie0018", "cookie4019", "cookie0250", "chardonnay", "cookie4010", "cookie0126", "cookie0081", "cookie0518", "cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet0111", "pet4001", "pet4005"]}
/>

Chardonnay occupies Macaron's former place in this story formation. Keep the rest of the support group while you establish a baseline. Adding Chardonnay and changing several damage dealers at once makes it harder to tell which adjustment helped.

Save the preset before trying replacements. The same formation is available on the [Teams page](/teams/), with its twelve Cookies and three Pets together. Match the members and Pet order first. Lower promotions can still justify the replacements below.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="boss-targeting" title="Why Bari and Cherry Cola chase the boss more reliably">

Bari and Cherry Cola prioritize high-ATK enemies. Earlier boss encounters could send them after the extra enemies instead, leaving the boss alive while your strongest melee attackers worked through the wrong targets.

The targeting rule still favors high ATK. In the adjusted story encounters, bosses have higher ATK than their accompanying enemies. That gives these two Cookies a clearer route to the boss. That matters because another damage upgrade cannot help much when the attacker keeps hitting something else.

Try the updated formation on auto before carrying over an old positioning workaround. Watch where Bari and Cherry Cola go once the boss and extra enemies appear. If they reach the boss but the team still loses, check survival, interruptions, or overall damage next.

This improvement does not remove every obstacle from automatic progression. A Cookie can select the right target and still spend the fight airborne. That is where the Pet change earns its place.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="knock-up-pet-swap" title="Replace Chargemellow when knock-ups stop the team">

The default Pets cover three jobs. Hot Doggie adds Skill Amp, Holy Baby Drop raises allied ATK, and Chargemellow supports Multi-strike users. Keep this setup for ordinary stages and bosses that let the team keep attacking.

**Against a knock-up boss, replace Chargemellow with Candy Shade Pouch.** Keep Hot Doggie and Holy Baby Drop. The pouch gives the squad Knock-up Resistance and additional HP. Cool Mint and the hammer-wielding Choco Werehound boss are examples where this adjustment deserves an early test.

You give up Chargemellow's Multi-strike contribution in exchange for more time spent attacking, buffing, and recovering. Compare the whole attempt. A smaller damage bonus can produce a better clear when the alternative leaves your support Cookies unable to cast.

Chardonnay's Knockback Resistance and the pouch's Knock-up Resistance address different disruptions. Do not assume that adding Chardonnay makes every control-focused Pet unnecessary. Keep the pouch preset ready and switch when the boss repeatedly lifts your team.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-replacements" title="Replace Bari according to the reason you are stuck">

A low-promotion Bari can feel weaker than the name suggests. You can still test the team while building her, but you also have three practical replacement paths.

Scorpion is a damage alternative when Bari is missing or underbuilt. Make that swap in Bari's slot and leave the rest of the preset alone for the first comparison. It gives you a manageable test instead of a completely different lineup.

Wind Archer is another option when your copy has much stronger promotion. A highly promoted TSSR can contribute substantial team Power. Story damage depends partly on the team's Power relative to the stage, so the replacement can help beyond its own attacks. The [story Power guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-power-guide-stage-damage/) explains why that comparison matters.

Choose Moon Rabbit when staying alive is the problem. If Bari is unavailable, Moon Rabbit can take her place. If Bari is already working, replace Dark Choco instead. That second swap removes a DEF Down slot, so judge whether the extra protection makes up for the lost damage support.

Do not make all three changes together. A surviving team that times out needs a different response from one that collapses before its first recovery cycle.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="chardonnay-runes" title="Build Chardonnay for the support slot">

Chardonnay is the default support choice in this preset, replacing Macaron rather than joining alongside her. Chardonnay brings a CRIT Chance buff, Knockback Resistance, and Multi-shot synergy support. Use this slot to support the rest of the formation, including the attackers who need help staying on the boss.

Skill Amp is the recommended Sugar Rune direction for Chardonnay. Keep the focus on the support contribution before chasing a set of personal damage stats. A usable build lets you test the formation sooner; the team does not require a perfect collection of SSR rolls before its first attempt.

Use the [Sugar Rune stat guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) when the rest of the roster needs work. Copying the Cookie list should not mean giving every Cookie the same Rune set. A fragile Charge attacker and a support buffer have different reasons for failing.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="promotion-crystal-priorities" title="Set promotion targets before spending crystals">

Higher promotions help, but you do not need to wait until every slot matches a finished account. Try the formation at your current investment, identify the weak point, and work toward useful milestones.

Chardonnay and Moon Rabbit have five-star targets in this progression route. After those initial goals, further Chardonnay investment toward ten stars becomes a longer project if your budget allows it. Continue building Bari when she is part of your story plan, without treating a poorly performing low-star copy as the only available choice.

The [tier list](/tier-list/) helps compare these investments with the rest of your roster. Check where a Cookie fits, then ask whether more copies will improve the team you actually use. Another promotion on a useful support may solve more fights than raising a specialist you rarely field.

Favor the relevant Cookie pickup banners for crystal spending. Regular premium pulls miss the pickup-event benefits, while Pet pulls do not advance the Cookie-promotion requirements behind Stellar Link. Cookie promotions feed that account progression, which gives the choice a benefit beyond one lineup.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="dimensional-rift-goal" title="Finish story with the Dimensional Rift in mind">

Reaching the end of the current story opens the route into Dimensional Rift. Its seasonal exchange and progression rewards add a reason to push rather than leave an almost-finished chapter sitting untouched.

Check the current exchange and milestone rewards when you arrive. If you cannot reach the content before the season ends, finishing more story still prepares the account for the next opening. Do not turn a closing season into an excuse to empty every crystal balance.

Keep both Pet setups saved as you work through the remaining stages. If a Cookie replacement gets you past a wall, note which problem it solved before carrying that change into every later fight.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="auto-stage-checklist" title="Test one difficult stage before leaving auto running">

1. Copy all twelve Cookies and the default three Pets. Keep Milk as captain for the initial test.
2. Watch Bari and Cherry Cola when the boss appears. Confirm that they engage the boss instead of spending the attempt on accompanying enemies.
3. If repeated knock-ups interrupt the team, swap Chargemellow for Candy Shade Pouch and repeat that stage.
4. If the team still dies, try Moon Rabbit in Dark Choco's slot, or in Bari's slot when Bari is missing or underbuilt.
5. If everyone survives but the timer runs out, compare Scorpion or your better-promoted Wind Archer with Bari before buying another upgrade.

Once the changed setup clears the problem stage, return to auto and watch the next boss transition. Save the successful variant so the next interruption takes one preset change instead of another round of rebuilding.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="chardonnay-story-faq" title="Chardonnay auto story team FAQ">

### Can this team clear every story boss automatically?

Treat it as a story baseline. Promotion, Runes, team Power, and the boss mechanic still affect the result. Candy Shade Pouch helps with knock-ups, and Moon Rabbit offers a survival alternative when the default formation fails.

### Who replaces Bari if I do not own her?

Try Scorpion for damage, a strongly promoted Wind Archer for damage and team Power, or Moon Rabbit when you need protection. Keep the other eleven slots steady while comparing the replacement.

### Does Chardonnay replace Macaron in this formation?

Yes. Chardonnay takes Macaron's support slot in this preset. Favor Skill Amp for Chardonnay, keep the remaining support group, and test the team before changing more members.

### Which Pet should I remove for Candy Shade Pouch?

Remove Chargemellow. Keep Hot Doggie and Holy Baby Drop, then test Candy Shade Pouch against repeated knock-ups. Return to the default trio when that protection no longer helps the fight.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-cherry-cola-auto-stag.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Cherry Cola dying during an Arena dive can make the Cookie look like a wasted investment. Story stages give that same attacker a much better job. Pair Cherry Cola with Pinot Noir, keep the support core intact, and fix the survival Runes before judging the damage. This setup aims to clear ordinary stages on auto without making you steer every fight.

**Start Cherry Cola with two Damage Reduction lines, then favor Skill Amp for the remaining Rune choices.** A little protection keeps the Cookie attacking. Stacking damage while the attacker falls over early gets you another retry screen.

This is a developed roster, so copying the twelve names does not promise identical progress. It does give you a specific team to test, clear substitutions when it fails, and a reason to leave some tempting damage upgrades alone.

<GuideSection id="story-lineup" title="Copy the full story team first">

Use the following formation as the starting preset. The order follows the two rows of the lineup, left to right. The upper row contains Macaron Cookie, Rye Cookie, Pomegranate Cookie, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, Strawberry Crepe Cookie, and Herb Cookie.

The lower row contains Brightseeker Cookie, Pinot Noir Cookie, Skating Queen Cookie, Nameless Cake Hound, Cherry Cola Cookie, and Dark Choco Cookie. Milk carries the captain marker in this setup. Keep that choice when checking how the team's ATK-based effects behave.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Cherry Cola auto story team"
  description="Copy the two rows in order. Keep Milk as captain and use Chargemellow, Hot Doggie, and Holy Baby Drop as the starting Pet setup."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0515", "cookie0126", "cookie4019", "cookie0518", "cookie0063", "cookie4013", "cookie4010", "cookie0018", "cookie4024", "cookie0250", "cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet4005", "pet0111", "pet4001"]}
/>

The three Pets are Chargemellow, Hot Doggie, and Holy Baby Drop, in that order. Chargemellow supports Multi-strike receivers, Hot Doggie adds Skill Amp, and Holy Baby Drop raises team ATK. Copy the Pet slots as well as the Cookies before deciding that the formation does not work.

You can also find this preset on the [recommended teams page](/teams/). Keep a saved copy before experimenting. Returning to a known lineup is much easier than remembering which of five swaps broke the run.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="cherry-cola-runes" title="Give Cherry Cola enough time to deal damage">

Two Damage Reduction Rune lines are the recommended starting point because Cherry Cola dies easily. Favor Skill Amp with the remaining choices. The purpose is to keep the attacker alive through the dangerous opening while retaining enough damage to move through the stage.

ATK Amp is still usable. A good roll does not need to go straight into the bin. The concern is piling on so much ATK that Cherry Cola starts taking effects intended for Milk, especially after further promotions raise Cherry Cola's stats.

Milk's ATK build and captain effects help determine who receives benefits aimed at the highest-ATK ally. If Milk has unfinished ATK Runes, an aggressively built Cherry Cola can overtake that position. A stronger-looking attacker can therefore disturb the support setup you were relying on.

Check the relevant ATK order after promotions or major Rune changes. Keep useful ATK rolls when they fit, but do not chase an all-ATK Cherry Cola build by habit. Once survival improves, compare actual stage clears before spending more on small damage gains.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="support-runes" title="Keep the support buffs on the intended Cookies">

Macaron uses extra ATK Amp here to compete for Pomegranate's buff targeting. That is a deliberate setup choice, so a high ATK number on a support Cookie is not automatically a mistake. Watch the intended recipients when you change equipment elsewhere in the team.

Build Pomegranate mainly around Skill Amp. One Skill Haste line can fit; every slot does not have to match. Milk leans heavily toward ATK Amp, with room for a Skill Amp or Skill Haste line. The important part is maintaining the ATK order that the formation needs.

Strawberry Crepe favors Skill Amp over a heavy Skill Haste build. Herb benefits from some Damage Reduction because losing a healer early hurts the whole attempt. Skill Amp and Skill Haste remain useful options around that survival choice.

For Dark Choco, mix Skill Haste and Focus rather than forcing every line into one stat. A Damage Reduction line is also a sensible choice for this setup. Rye can carry some ATK Amp, but this setup does not prescribe every Rune slot on every Cookie.

Nameless Cake Hound's cluster of CRIT DMG rolls came from the rolls available, not a recommendation to chase that stat. Copy the formation's purpose without assuming every incidental Rune is essential. For the wider relationship between these stats, use the [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/).

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rye-or-melon" title="Use Rye when you want to leave auto running">

Melon Soda can take Rye's place. The tradeoff is how much attention you want to give the fight. Melon Soda can deliver strong damage when you bring the Cookie close to a boss, where more of the missiles reach the target.

At longer range, that spread can waste hits. A large number of attacks looks encouraging until too many of them miss the enemy you need to kill. Manual positioning makes Melon Soda easier to use well, but repeated adjustments defeat the purpose if you want a quiet stretch of automatic clears.

Rye has fewer hits and tends to land them more consistently at a distance in this setup. That makes Rye the more comfortable default for unattended progression. Choose Melon Soda when you are willing to move close and manage the fight; keep Rye when you want fewer interruptions.

Scorpion is another tempting addition, but the tested variation worked better without forcing Scorpion into this particular formation. That does not erase Scorpion's uses elsewhere. It means this preset should get a fair run as a focused Cherry Cola and Pinot Noir team before you blend it with another damage plan.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="defensive-swaps" title="Change protection before replacing the whole team">

When a hard-hitting stage keeps killing Cookies, try replacing Chargemellow with Icy Birdie for incoming damage reduction. You give up Multi-strike support to buy survival, so watch whether the extra time compensates for the lost offense. Keep the original Pet preset for stages where it still clears comfortably.

If you own Majestic King Choco Drop and need more protection, consider replacing Holy Baby Drop's team ATK benefit with that Pet's HP support. This is an optional defensive adjustment, not a requirement to obtain another premium Pet before trying the team.

Strawberry Crepe's slot is the Cookie swap to examine when the team still collapses. Ion Cookie Robot can provide a more defensive alternative. Change one slot, run the same problem stage again, and check whether the team survives long enough to finish.

Knock-ups need a more specific answer. Against hammer-style attacks that repeatedly throw the team into the air, try Panda Dumpling for Lift Resistance in a Pet slot. Diagnose the interruption before cutting another attacker. A team that spends the fight airborne loses opportunities to heal as well as to deal damage.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="boss-positioning" title="Rescue a stuck boss with one positioning change">

Auto can stall against Cool Mint when smaller enemies pull attention away and spread the team's damage. The formation may have enough damage overall while failing to concentrate it on the boss. Another expensive Rune roll is a poor first response to that problem.

Try moving the team close to the boss manually. If that does not settle the fight, pull the group toward the lower-left corner, roughly the seven o'clock position. Gathering the fight there can help with the scattered targeting that stopped the automatic attempt.

Treat this as a recovery tactic for a stubborn stage. Once it clears, return to auto and see how far the team progresses before the next interruption. You do not need to turn every ordinary stage into a manual fight just because one boss needed help.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="story-and-arena" title="Judge story progress separately from Arena">

Cherry Cola's S-tier placement reflects the strong story performance of a properly supported build. The [current tier list](/tier-list/) compares the full roster; this formation explains the survival choices behind the recommendation.

The earlier Arena attempts exposed weak survival and unfinished Rune work. Further investment may improve that matchup, but successful story clears do not prove that Cherry Cola now kills every enemy Milk. Test that claim in Arena before changing an established PvP team.

Brightseeker does not need five stars just to try this story preset. Promotion still affects performance, but five stars is not an entry requirement. Start with what your account has, protect Cherry Cola and the healers, then use the failed stage to decide the next adjustment.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="auto-team-faq" title="Cherry Cola auto team FAQ">

### Which Sugar Runes should Cherry Cola use for story stages?

Start with two Damage Reduction lines and favor Skill Amp for the remaining choices. Some ATK Amp is usable, but check that Cherry Cola does not take highest-ATK benefits intended for Milk.

### Can Melon Soda replace Rye in this team?

Yes. Melon Soda works better when you move close enough for the missiles to connect. Rye is the more comfortable default when you want to leave ordinary story stages on auto.

### What should I change if the team dies too quickly?

Try Icy Birdie instead of Chargemellow for damage reduction. If necessary, consider Majestic King Choco Drop instead of Holy Baby Drop, or Ion Cookie Robot instead of Strawberry Crepe. Test each change separately.

### Does Brightseeker need five stars for this formation?

No. Five stars is not required to try the formation. Your promotions, Runes, and overall stats still affect how far the team can progress.

</GuideSection>

At longer range, that spread can waste hits. A large number of attacks looks encouraging until too many of them miss the enemy you need to kill. Manual positioning makes Melon Soda easier to use well, but repeated adjustments defeat the purpose if you want a quiet stretch of automatic clears.

Rye has fewer hits and tends to land them more consistently at a distance in this setup. That makes Rye the more comfortable default for unattended progression. Choose Melon Soda when you are willing to move close and manage the fight; keep Rye when you want fewer interruptions.

Scorpion is another tempting addition, but the tested variation worked better without forcing Scorpion into this particular formation. That does not erase Scorpion's uses elsewhere. It means this preset should get a fair run as a focused Cherry Cola and Pinot Noir team before you blend it with another damage plan.
Use Rye when you want to leave auto running
segments.name: title

segments.text: When a hard-hitting stage keeps killing Cookies, try replacing Chargemellow with Icy Birdie for incoming damage reduction. You give up Multi-strike support to buy survival, so watch whether the extra time compensates for the lost offense. Keep the original Pet preset for stages where it still clears comfortably.

If you own Majestic King Choco Drop and need more protection, consider replacing Holy Baby Drop's team ATK benefit with that Pet's HP support. This is an optional defensive adjustment, not a requirement to obtain another premium Pet before trying the team.

Strawberry Crepe's slot is the Cookie swap to examine when the team still collapses. Ion Cookie Robot can provide a more defensive alternative. Change one slot, run the same problem stage again, and check whether the team survives long enough to finish.

Knock-ups need a more specific answer. Against hammer-style attacks that repeatedly throw the team into the air, try Panda Dumpling for Lift Resistance in a Pet slot. Diagnose the interruption before cutting another attacker. A team that spends the fight airborne loses opportunities to heal as well as to deal damage.
Change protection before replacing the whole team
segments.name: title

segments.text: Auto can stall against Cool Mint when smaller enemies pull attention away and spread the team's damage. The formation may have enough damage overall while failing to concentrate it on the boss. Another expensive Rune roll is a poor first response to that problem.

Try moving the team close to the boss manually. If that does not settle the fight, pull the group toward the lower-left corner, roughly the seven o'clock position. Gathering the fight there can help with the scattered targeting that stopped the automatic attempt.

Treat this as a recovery tactic for a stubborn stage. Once it clears, return to auto and see how far the team progresses before the next interruption. You do not need to turn every ordinary stage into a manual fight just because one boss needed help.
Rescue a stuck boss with one positioning change
segments.name: title

segments.text: Cherry Cola's S-tier placement reflects the strong story performance of a properly supported build. The
current tier list
compares the full roster; this formation explains the survival choices behind the recommendation.

The earlier Arena attempts exposed weak survival and unfinished Rune work. Further investment may improve that matchup, but successful story clears do not prove that Cherry Cola now kills every enemy Milk. Test that claim in Arena before changing an established PvP team.

Brightseeker does not need five stars just to try this story preset. Promotion still affects performance, but five stars is not an entry requirement. Start with what your account has, protect Cherry Cola and the healers, then use the failed stage to decide the next adjustment.
Judge story progress separately from Arena
segments.name: title

segments.text: Which Sugar Runes should Cherry Cola use for story stages?
Start with two Damage Reduction lines and favor Skill Amp for the remaining choices. Some ATK Amp is usable, but check that Cherry Cola does not take highest-ATK benefits intended for Milk.
Can Melon Soda replace Rye in this team?
Yes. Melon Soda works better when you move close enough for the missiles to connect. Rye is the more comfortable default when you want to leave ordinary story stages on auto.
What should I change if the team dies too quickly?

Try Icy Birdie instead of Chargemellow for damage reduction. If necessary, consider Majestic King Choco Drop instead of Holy Baby Drop, or Ion Cookie Robot instead of Strawberry Crepe. Test each change separately.
Does Brightseeker need five stars for this formation?
No. Five stars is not required to try the formation. Your promotions, Runes, and overall stats still affect how far the team can progress.
Cherry Cola auto team FAQ

cookie-run-crumble-cherry-cola-cookie-gu.text:
import { GuideSection } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Cherry Cola Cookie looks like an answer to a very annoying Arena problem: Milk stays alive, keeps the enemy team going, and watches your damage disappear into another heal. A Cookie who charges toward the highest-ATK enemy sounds perfect for that matchup. Then the fight starts, Cherry Cola drops, and Milk is still standing.

**Five stars is a reasonable stopping point for Stellar Link progress. It does not guarantee a working Milk counter.** If Pinot Noir still needs seven stars, that is the stronger combat investment to finish before pushing Cherry Cola further. You can want the promotions without handing the new Cookie a permanent Arena slot.

<GuideSection id="pull-budget" title="Decide what you are buying before you pull">

The five-star recommendation comes from account growth. Stellar Link counts Cookie promotions, so progress there has value even if Cherry Cola spends some time on the bench. A newer account has more room to benefit from that progression, which can make additional promotions worth considering.

That still leaves a budget decision. Five stars is a target to weigh against your available Cutters and Crystals, not a reason to empty every reserve. Pick the stopping point before opening the banner. Once you reach it, check what the next promotion would cost and which existing Cookie would lose those resources.

One large pull session started with about 500,000 Crystals and 2,700 Cutters and still fell short of full promotion. That result is not an average cost calculation. It is a useful warning against assuming that a huge stash guarantees a finished Cookie. Rare bonus pulls can make the session feel successful while your intended promotion remains unfinished.

For combat priorities, compare the rest of your roster with the [Cookie tier list](/tier-list/). A promotion that helps account growth and a Cookie who improves today's Arena team can be different purchases. Decide which benefit you need before spending another batch of Crystals.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="milk-targeting" title="Why Cherry Cola goes after Milk">

Cherry Cola is an SSR Water Charge Cookie who receives Multi-strike and Multi-shot synergies. The attraction in Arena is the highest-ATK targeting: an enemy who builds Milk around ATK and stacks the relevant captain effects can put Milk at the top of that check.

That creates an opportunity to reach the healer instead of spending the whole fight hitting something else. But the skill does not select an enemy because their name is Milk. If another Cookie has the highest ATK, the targeting logic points elsewhere. Check the opponent's setup before blaming the skill for chasing the wrong unit.

The displayed skill interval in the initial assessment was 1.75 seconds, alongside a large damage multiplier. Those numbers explain the appeal of a fast burst attacker. They do not tell you how many attacks Cherry Cola will finish after diving into danger.

There is another ATK check on your own side. In the setup under review, Cherry Cola's ATK sat below Milk's, so effects that favored the highest-ATK ally did not automatically prioritize Cherry Cola. Adding the new attacker does not mean your existing buff package suddenly belongs to them. Watch who receives it.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-survival" title="The first problem is staying alive">

Cherry Cola's early Arena weakness was painfully simple: the Cookie moved out alone and died too easily. Against a strong defense, the expected healer assassination became a quick loss of your own attacker. A short skill interval cannot help much after that.

The initial swap removed the SSR Royal Excellence version of Space Doughnut. It kept the team's defensive support, including Nameless Cake Hound. That is a useful starting principle for your own experiments: remove a flexible slot before cutting the protection that gives Cherry Cola a chance to act.

A later attempt used a more defensive Pet setup. It did not turn Milk into a reliable early kill. Defensive Pets can give Cherry Cola more time. The Cookie still has to deal enough damage to finish Milk before that protection runs out.

Start with an established formation from the [team lineup guide](/teams/) and make one swap. If you change the frontline, Pets, captain setup, and damage core together, you will have trouble telling whether Cherry Cola improved anything. A familiar team makes a disappointing result much easier to diagnose.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="kill-check" title="A win can hide a failed assassination">

Watch Milk's health during the opening exchange. Does Cherry Cola take a meaningful chunk out of it? Does the target recover? Does Cherry Cola survive long enough to finish? The final victory screen skips the detail you need to judge this particular slot.

In the early attempts, Milk kept surviving even when the overall fight looked winnable. Cherry Cola could fall while the remaining team still had enough damage to win. Calling that a successful counter gives the new Cookie credit for work the rest of the lineup did.

The promising case is narrower: enough offensive investment, with a favorable stat matchup, may let Cherry Cola finish Milk quickly. Treat that as a condition to test. The early results do not establish a reliable answer against equally strong or stronger defenses.

For a useful comparison, repeat the same opponent with your original lineup and the Cherry Cola swap. Keep the other settings fixed. Record whether Milk dies early and whether your team wins. If the original team wins just as comfortably, Cherry Cola has not yet earned the slot, even if the damage number looks respectable.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rune-spending" title="Avoid expensive rune guesses">

There is not enough here to name a settled best Sugar Rune build. The initial assessment explicitly left that decision open, and the Arena attempts exposed a survival problem before they established an ideal damage setup. Spending heavily on a supposed perfect roll would get ahead of the evidence.

The short displayed skill interval makes Skill Haste a less obvious first expense. It does not prove that Haste has zero value. First check whether Cherry Cola lives to use repeated skills at all. If the Cookie dies during the opening dive, shaving time off later casts misses the immediate problem.

Use the gear you already own for the first comparison. Then change one part of the setup to address what happened in battle: an attacker who survives but cannot finish Milk needs a different adjustment from one who disappears immediately. Avoid paying for several speculative fixes at once.

Also check which ally receives ATK-based support effects after any gear changes. Raising Cherry Cola's stats can alter that order. You want to know whether an apparent improvement came from the gear itself or from moving an important buff away from another Cookie.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pinot-priority" title="Finish Pinot Noir before chasing more stars">

If you need a firm investment order, prioritize seven-star Pinot Noir before taking Cherry Cola beyond the five-star Stellar Link plan. Pinot Noir was the more dependable investment in this comparison. Cherry Cola still needed a formation that could turn the targeting idea into repeatable kills.

That recommendation concerns which upgrade to finish first. It does not mean five-star Cherry Cola is useless, or that every account needs to stop at the same point forever. A newer roster may still gain useful account progress from more promotions. An Arena-focused account needs evidence that those extra stars fix its actual matchup.

Once Cherry Cola reaches your planned target, benching the Cookie is an acceptable result. Test again when your setup changes enough to address the failed dive. You do not have to keep a fragile attacker in the lineup just because the banner consumed a lot of Crystals.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="cherry-cola-faq" title="Cherry Cola pull and Arena FAQ">

### Should I stop Cherry Cola Cookie at five stars?

Five stars is a reasonable Stellar Link target. Reassess before going further, especially if Pinot Noir still needs seven stars. Extra promotions do not guarantee that Cherry Cola will survive an Arena dive or finish Milk.

### Does Cherry Cola always target Milk?

No. The relevant targeting rule checks the enemy with the highest ATK. Milk becomes the target when the opponent's ATK investment and captain setup put Milk first.

### What is the best Sugar Rune for Cherry Cola?

This early assessment does not establish a best Sugar Rune. Test with existing gear, watch survival and target damage, and avoid expensive rolls until you know what your lineup needs.

### Is Cherry Cola already a reliable Arena counter?

The early attempts do not support that claim. Milk survived several dives, and some wins came from the remaining team's damage after Cherry Cola fell. Judge the opening kill and the match result separately.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-cool-mint-cookie-buil.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Cool Mint Cookie is easy to write off because her failed casts are impossible to miss. She steps into melee range, starts her drill, then a knockback or stun cancels the hit. Her summons can also disappear before they do enough to justify the slot.

She works best in a summon team with Licorice and Witchberry. The trio is built for split targets and crowded stages, where extra bodies can pin enemies in place and soak attacks. Against one boss with constant area damage, use a more focused team.

<GuideSection id="why-cool-mint-fails" title="Why Cool Mint feels weak alone">

Cool Mint is an SSR Water Charge Cookie, so she has to drill from close range without crowd-control immunity. One clean cast looks excellent. The next can be interrupted before it does anything.

Do not judge her from one lucky damage screen. Give enemy skills more targets, activate both of her synergies, and use fights where her wide attacks can hit more than one target.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="summon-core" title="The three-Cookie summon core">

- Cool Mint Cookie supplies the main summons, area pressure, and crowd control.
- Licorice Cookie adds another group of summons that can absorb attacks and share the pressure.
- Witchberry Cookie covers split enemies with large block attacks and becomes the main wide-damage threat.

Licorice makes the setup work. His summons scale with ATK and deal respectable damage, but their main job is sharing hits with Cool Mint's summons. That buys her enough time to finish the drill and cycle again.

Witchberry handles the enemies that refuse to stand together. Her blocks stay active for 5.5 seconds while the skill has a 4-second cooldown. She already has continuous coverage without Skill Haste. Extra Haste can create overlap, but it is not the first stat I would chase.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="synergy-providers" title="Activate Cool Mint's two synergies">

Cool Mint receives Multi-shot and Duration. The core feels incomplete when either one is missing, so reserve provider slots before filling the lineup with extra damage dealers.

Herb is the Multi-shot provider in the lineup below, and his healing patches Cool Mint's melee risk. Cheesecake Cookie or Tiger Lily Cookie can fill the same synergy slot when the team can afford to trade healing for more pressure.

Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician provides Duration plus ATK Up and healing. That is an easy fit because longer summon uptime and better survival solve the same problem from different sides.

Witchberry receives Pierce, but I treat that as optional. Rockstar Cookie can provide it and brings a shield, yet the slot may be worth more as healing, defense, or focused boss damage. Finish Cool Mint's two synergies first. Add Pierce only when the team already stays alive.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="recommended-team" title="Recommended Cool Mint team">

Start with this full 12-Cookie lineup. If a stage asks for more single-target damage or defense, compare it with the [recommended teams](/teams/) before changing the summon core.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="12-Cookie summon lineup"
  description="Herb activates Multi-shot, Milk activates Duration, and Licorice plus Ion keep the summon core alive through another cycle."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0503", "cookie0126", "cookie2006", "cookie4024", "cookie4006", "cookie0181", "cookie0037", "cookie4003", "cookie4019", "cookie0136", "cookie0063"]}
  petIds={["pet4004", "pet4001", "pet0111"]}
/>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="sugar-rune-stats" title="Best Sugar Rune stats">

Use these priorities when you sort Sugar Runes:

- Cool Mint Cookie: ATK%, Skill Amp, Skill Haste, then a survival stat if needed.
- Licorice Cookie: ATK% first, followed by Skill Amp or Skill Haste.
- Witchberry Cookie: ATK%, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, and Skill Amp.

Skill Haste is acceptable on Witchberry, especially if it makes the blocks overlap, but her base timing already works. I would keep a strong Haste roll rather than throw materials away. I would not lock it ahead of a good offensive stat.

A useful SR ATK roll beats an SSR line that does nothing for the Cookie. The letters look expensive. The fight does not care.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="best-content" title="Where this team earns its slots">

Rowdy Bikers is the best example. Three bosses split up and ride toward different corners, which can leave ordinary damage dealers swinging at empty space. Cool Mint and Licorice put extra bodies on the field, so the bikers stop moving long enough for Witchberry's wide blocks to connect. The core also works against Rowdy Truck and can handle the Twisted boss with the right support slots.

Plaque Tower gives the trio another good job. The summons appear late enough that enemies can group before the extra bodies arrive, then soak damage once the floor gets busy. That can reduce the amount of healing the lineup needs. Milk and Grapevine Cookie may be enough on floors where the summons catch most of the pressure.

PvP is less consistent, but the summons can bait enemy skills and keep melee targets busy. Cool Mint may not top the damage chart immediately. Longer fights give her more summon cycles, and that is when her total can pass much more obvious carries.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bad-matchups" title="When to bench the summon core">

Frequent area damage is the cleanest counter. A boss that wipes every summon every few seconds removes the reason to run both Cool Mint and Licorice. Pure single-target fights can also favor Scorpion Cookie, Rye Cookie, or another focused attacker.

GingerBrave at higher boss stages exposes the problem. The opener can nearly remove the team, and the summons do not solve that by themselves. The setup can still win after defensive adjustments, but that does not make it the best answer. If Cool Mint dies before cycling, replace one greedy slot with Ion Cookie Robot, Herb Cookie, or another protector.

The [Tier List](/tier-list/) helps compare Cool Mint with focused carries at the same investment level. Read the rank together with the matchup, because a lower general rank can still win when split targets give summons a real job.

<GuideTip title="Use the matchup, not the hype">

Run the trio when targets split, waves stay crowded, or enemy skills can be wasted on summons. Bench it when frequent area damage deletes the whole gimmick.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="quick-build" title="Quick Cool Mint build">

1. Lock Cool Mint, Licorice, and Witchberry as the core.
2. Activate Multi-shot and Duration. The displayed lineup uses Herb and Milk.
3. Keep Scorpion for boss damage, then add defense if Cool Mint cannot reach her second skill cycle.
4. Test the team on Rowdy Bikers, packed Tower floors, or PvP before spending more Rune materials.

Check each unit in the [Cookie list](/cookies/) and arrange your exact roster in the [Team Builder](/tools/team-builder/). If your Rune rolls are the weak point, use the [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) before locking another expensive stat.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="cool-mint-faq" title="Cool Mint Cookie FAQ">

### What is the best Cool Mint Cookie team core?

Use Cool Mint Cookie, Licorice Cookie, and Witchberry Cookie. Licorice adds summons that absorb pressure, while Witchberry punishes split or grouped enemies with wide block damage.

### Which synergies does Cool Mint need?

Cool Mint receives Multi-shot and Duration. Use Cheesecake, Herb, or Tiger Lily for Multi-shot, then add Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician for Duration.

### What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Cool Mint?

Start with ATK% because her summons scale with ATK. Skill Amp and Skill Haste are good follow-ups. Keep a defensive stat when she dies before getting another summon cycle.

### Is Skill Haste good on Witchberry Cookie?

It is usable, but her blocks already last 5.5 seconds on a 4-second cooldown. ATK, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, and Skill Amp usually deserve priority.

### Is Cool Mint Cookie good for every boss?

No. She performs best against split targets, crowded waves, and enemies that waste attacks on summons. Frequent area damage and strict single-target checks can make a focused damage team safer.

</GuideSection>

Plaque Tower gives the trio another good job. The summons appear late enough that enemies can group before the extra bodies arrive, then soak damage once the floor gets busy. That can reduce the amount of healing the lineup needs. Milk and Grapevine Cookie may be enough on floors where the summons catch most of the pressure.

PvP is less consistent, but the summons can bait enemy skills and keep melee targets busy. Cool Mint may not top the damage chart immediately. Longer fights give her more summon cycles, and that is when her total can pass much more obvious carries.
Where this team earns its slots

segments.text: Frequent area damage is the cleanest counter. A boss that wipes every summon every few seconds removes the reason to run both Cool Mint and Licorice. Pure single-target fights can also favor Scorpion Cookie, Rye Cookie, or another focused attacker.

GingerBrave at higher boss stages exposes the problem. The opener can nearly remove the team, and the summons do not solve that by themselves. The setup can still win after defensive adjustments, but that does not make it the best answer. If Cool Mint dies before cycling, replace one greedy slot with Ion Cookie Robot, Herb Cookie, or another protector.
The
Tier List

helps compare Cool Mint with focused carries at the same investment level. Read the rank together with the matchup, because a lower general rank can still win when split targets give summons a real job.
Run the trio when targets split, waves stay crowded, or enemy skills can be wasted on summons. Bench it when frequent area damage deletes the whole gimmick.
Use the matchup, not the hype

Activate Multi-shot and Duration. The displayed lineup uses Herb and Milk.
Keep Scorpion for boss damage, then add defense if Cool Mint cannot reach her second skill cycle.
Test the team on Rowdy Bikers, packed Tower floors, or PvP before spending more Rune materials.
Check each unit in the
Cookie list
and arrange your exact roster in the
Team Builder
. If your Rune rolls are the weak point, use the
gear and Sugar Rune guide
before locking another expensive stat.
Quick Cool Mint build

segments.text: What is the best Cool Mint Cookie team core?
Use Cool Mint Cookie, Licorice Cookie, and Witchberry Cookie. Licorice adds summons that absorb pressure, while Witchberry punishes split or grouped enemies with wide block damage.
Which synergies does Cool Mint need?
Cool Mint receives Multi-shot and Duration. Use Cheesecake, Herb, or Tiger Lily for Multi-shot, then add Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician for Duration.
What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Cool Mint?
Start with ATK% because her summons scale with ATK. Skill Amp and Skill Haste are good follow-ups. Keep a defensive stat when she dies before getting another summon cycle.
Is Skill Haste good on Witchberry Cookie?
It is usable, but her blocks already last 5.5 seconds on a 4-second cooldown. ATK, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, and Skill Amp usually deserve priority.
Is Cool Mint Cookie good for every boss?
No. She performs best against split targets, crowded waves, and enemies that waste attacks on summons. Frequent area damage and strict single-target checks can make a focused damage team safer.

cookie-run-crumble-dungeon-milk-buff-gui.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Your Crumble Dungeon score can suffer even when you bring stronger Cookies. A roaming attacker can pull the formation apart. A support can take a buff you meant for Milk. Another ATK buff can interrupt the stacks you spent the fight building.

For a push toward 50G, start with Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician as leader, keep the group together, and check who receives the important buffs. The setup behind this approach reached roughly 52G, or 52 billion damage. That is a reference result, not a promise for every account.

Check Combat Power to see who enters, then compare ATK to see who gets the targeted effects. Milk can make the initial group and still lose an ATK-based buff to a carry.

<GuideSection id="entry-and-position" title="Check who enters and where they move">

Crumble Dungeon starts with 40 Cookies, with entry priority based on individual Combat Power. Levels change that ranking, so lowering or raising a Cookie can change who joins the initial group. Inspect the entry display after every adjustment instead of assuming a level reset guarantees exclusion.

The goal is a compact formation near the center. Buffs and synergies have ranges; a Cookie fighting away from the group can miss effects that make the whole setup work.

Oven Wanderer is a poor fit for this particular approach because movement around the boss can draw attention and disturb the formation. Summons can create similar positioning problems. Watch where the group goes before deciding that another personal damage dealer improves the run.

This is not a blanket ban on every Charge Cookie or summoner in every mode. Skating Queen can still have a role here. The useful question is whether a specific Cookie disrupts the cluster during this fight.

The [recommended Teams](/teams/) page can help you identify familiar damage and support combinations, but its standard formations are not complete 40-Cookie dungeon rosters. Entry control needs its own check.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="milk-leader" title="Make Milk receive the leader and Welfare benefits">

Choose Milk as leader. If your mercenary level is at least 4, the demonstrated setup uses the Welfare option labeled 열정페이, alongside 초고속 승진 as the second choice. Check those options in your client and aim their benefits at Milk. The first depends on your highest-ATK ally; selecting Milk's portrait alone does not guarantee the result.

Include the leader effect's 10% ATK increase when comparing candidates. Do not simply sort the unadjusted numbers on the roster screen. Apply the relevant leader bonus, then check whether Milk remains first. Avoid adding the bonus twice if the screen you use already includes it.

If a carry still wins the comparison, lowering that carry's level is one way to move Milk ahead. Record the original level and ATK first. Rebuild only as far as the intended ranking allows, then check the other competing Cookies too.

The [level 100 EXP priority guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-level-100-exp-priority-guide/) explains why entry power and Welfare targeting need separate calculations. Keep enough investment for the intended Cookies to enter, while preserving Milk's priority.

<GuideTip title="A lower carry level has a cost">

You are trading some personal damage for stronger support effects. If the final score drops, revisit that trade instead of continuing to lower every attacker just to make the ATK ranking look neat.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pomegranate-targets" title="Remove competition for Pomegranate's red beam">

In the targeting tests behind this setup, Pomegranate appeared to prioritize Cookies that receive Projectile Speed synergy. Among the remaining candidates, higher ATK then mattered. Treat that as observed targeting behavior to verify in your own attempt, not a fully proven rule for every possible lineup.

Milk receives Projectile Speed and must stay in the group. The following Cookies also receive it in the roster data, so they create competition for the intended beam targets:

- Zombie Cookie
- Cocoa Cookie
- Blackberry Cookie
- Lemon Cookie
- Strawberry Shortcake Cookie
- Madeleine Cookie

The exclusion method is to reset these Cookies to level 1 so their power drops below the initial entry group. Confirm the result in the entry display. A level number is only useful if it produces the roster you intended.

Read the reset confirmation before applying it, and note any teams that currently use those Cookies. This is a dungeon-specific adjustment, not an instruction to permanently abandon them. The [Cookie Tier List](/tier-list/) describes broader roster value; a useful Cookie elsewhere can still interfere with this specialized setup.

Do not confuse Strawberry Shortcake with Strawberry Crepe. They are different Cookies, and the exclusion list names Shortcake.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="cheesecake-conflict" title="Leave Cheesecake out of this Milk-focused setup">

Cheesecake needs a separate explanation. She does not belong to the Projectile Speed exclusion group, but her ATK buff can interfere with Milk's accumulated ATK buff.

The reported interaction is order-sensitive. Milk can build stacks while Cheesecake's ATK buff is already present. If Cheesecake applies her buff after Milk has built his stacks, those stacks disappear and Milk starts building again.

That means "both give ATK" is not enough reason to use both. In a run built around maximizing Milk, repeatedly losing accumulated stacks can undermine the investment you made to direct other effects toward him.

For this approach, lower Cheesecake to level 1 and verify that she stays out of the initial group. Judge that choice within Crumble Dungeon. It does not mean her buff has no use in an early team or another formation.

If you change several support slots at once, you will struggle to tell whether an improvement came from removing Cheesecake, changing beam targets, or fixing movement. Establish the exclusions first, then adjust the remaining targets.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="two-target-plans" title="Choose between support targets and damage targets">

There are two practical ways to distribute Pomegranate's remaining attention once Milk is secure.

The more demanding option raises Macaron and Skating Queen to the top ATK positions among the other eligible candidates. Lower the competing damage dealers beneath them. Giving the beam to these buffers produced better damage in the comparison behind this setup.

Making that ranking happen can be awkward. A less-promoted Macaron may have much lower ATK than your carries. Chasing ATK through Sugar Runes solely to force the result can also cost resources you wanted for other builds.

The simpler option leaves the beam with Milk and two main damage dealers, such as Scorpion and another invested carry. You can still get a strong result without forcing both support targets. Keep Milk's leader and Welfare setup correct even if you choose this route.

I would test the simpler option first if Macaron needs substantial new investment just to compete. Record the result before trying the support-target version. Otherwise, you have no useful baseline for deciding whether the extra work helped.

For both options, spend remaining EXP on the active damage dealers only within the ATK limits your chosen plan requires. You do not need every supporting Cookie at level 100. Some only need enough power to make the entry group.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="attempt-checklist" title="Use each ticket to answer one question">

Before the next attempt, work through these checks:

1. Confirm Milk is leader and receives the intended Welfare effects.
2. Recalculate the relevant ATK ranking with the leader bonus.
3. Check the initial 40, including the seven named exclusions.
4. Watch whether the group stays together around the boss.
5. Verify the beam recipients before comparing final damage.

Keep Pets and unrelated builds unchanged while testing the two target plans. Record the score alongside the actual recipients. A higher result tells you less if you do not know which setup produced it.

Make at least one daily attempt when you can, even if you are far below 50G. Participation, score milestones, and ranking rewards give this mode value before a record run. Check the reward screen for the tiers your account can reach rather than postponing participation until the build feels perfect.

Save a note of any reduced levels so you can restore another mode's lineup afterward. If Milk gets the right effects but the score still disappoints, look at lost carry stats and positioning before spending more on a target you already fixed.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="dungeon-faq" title="Crumble Dungeon buff setup FAQ">

### Does choosing Milk as leader guarantee the Welfare target?

No. The highest-ATK check still matters. Include the relevant 10% leader bonus in the comparison and verify the actual recipient.

### Which Cookies should stay out of this setup?

Exclude Zombie, Cocoa, Blackberry, Lemon, Strawberry Shortcake, and Madeleine to reduce Projectile Speed target competition. Exclude Cheesecake separately because her ATK buff can interrupt Milk's stacks.

### Do Macaron and Skating Queen have to receive the beam?

No. They are the more demanding support-target option. Milk and two invested damage dealers offer a simpler alternative when forcing the supports' ATK rankings costs too much.

### Will this setup guarantee 50G damage?

No. Roughly 52G is the reference result. Your levels, promotions, stats, positioning, and actual buff recipients affect the score.

</GuideSection>
