cookie-run-crumble-endgame-grind-guide.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

You change a Cookie, wait through another stage attempt, and still cannot tell whether the swap helped. Meanwhile, Arena tickets pile up and the next level eats millions of EXP. CookieRun: Crumble can ask for a surprising amount of attention once your account gets past the easy upgrades.

I would put faster retries and cheaper team experiments ahead of another long upgrade track. Battle reports could explain a failed swap; level synchronization and saved Sugar Rune builds could make the next one less work.

You can reduce some of that friction now by keeping a stable core and testing one change at a time. Other problems need changes to the game itself.

<GuideTip title="Suggestions, not an update announcement">

Level synchronization, summon wishlists, elemental towers, and the other proposed features below are design ideas. This guide does not announce a release date or confirm that the developers plan to add them.

</GuideTip>

<GuideSection id="slow-stage-attempts" title="The wait between useful attempts adds up">

A push from around stage 140 to 171 took roughly 15 hours in one account's experience. That is an example of the time commitment, not a clear-time target. Your roster and upgrades will change the pace.

At higher stages, leaving auto-battle running does not solve every wall. Around the 160 range, repeated lineup adjustments can become part of the push. Each failed experiment feels worse when you must wait before reaching the boss again.

A manual boss shortcut would help. Players could still choose when to attempt the fight, but would spend less time filling the gauge between meaningful decisions. Faster progression or a 2x option would also address the waiting. Neither idea needs to make the boss weaker.

Until your available controls solve that problem, give each attempt a purpose. Are you checking whether a tank survives the opener, whether poison stacks land, or whether the timer expires with everyone alive? Pick one. Compare an appropriate [recommended team](/teams/) with your own lineup, then change the slot connected to that failure.

If nothing changed since the last several losses, another identical attempt may tell you very little. Waiting for an upgrade is sometimes more sensible than watching the same loss again.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="battle-feedback" title="A damage report would make failed runs useful">

Skill descriptions cannot show how a Cookie moves through an actual fight. Target selection and time spent reaching enemies can make an impressive kit perform worse than its numbers suggest. Oven Wanderer is a useful example of the concern: a strong-looking kit still needs practical testing.

PvE battle reports should show damage dealt, healing, and damage taken. They would help in ordinary boss attempts, Guild Conquest, and Crumble Dungeon. A single-target fight asks different questions from a 12-Cookie Arena battle, so an Arena result cannot settle every PvE choice.

A report would not explain everything either. Low personal damage does not make a buffer useless. You would still compare the team's result with and without that Cookie. But actual battle totals would give you a better starting point than guessing from the power display.

For now, record what you can see: boss HP left, survival time, missed attacks, and important debuffs. Keep the stage and Pets unchanged during a comparison. That will not replace a proper meter, but it makes the next decision less arbitrary.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="exp-and-build-swaps" title="Level 90 makes casual experiments expensive">

The EXP example is stark: a level 97 Scorpion needed about 10 million EXP for the next level, compared with roughly 2 to 2.5 million near level 88. Those figures describe the example account, not every entry in an EXP table. They explain why raising several alternatives can feel slow.

A proposed level-sync system could use the lowest level among 12 invested Cookies. If the lowest were level 88, eligible lower-level Cookies could temporarily match 88. That would let players test a new formation without funding every candidate separately. This is a suggested rule, not an existing unlock instruction.

Resetting levels can help move investment, but repeatedly resetting and rebuilding takes time. It can also leave your Arena defense weaker if it uses a Cookie you just reset. Check that lineup before finishing the session.

Keep most of your EXP in the Cookies you regularly field. Use the [level 100 EXP priority guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-level-100-exp-priority-guide/) when choosing the next recipient, rather than leveling every possible replacement equally.

Sugar Rune presets would solve a related problem. A Cookie might need different stats for PvP and a boss, yet testing both should not mean repeatedly rebuilding the same setup. Saved builds would make those comparisons easier. Equipment presets and proposed Rune presets are separate features; do not assume one provides the other.

Until you have a switching option that suits the job, keep a note of your working rolls before experimenting. The [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) can help narrow the stats worth testing so you make fewer speculative changes.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="mileage-and-wishlists" title="Duplicates need somewhere useful to go">

Mileage can lose its appeal when you already bought the items you want and must wait for a shop reset. Extra tickets or keys do not solve that for an account that already struggles to use its existing supply.

A useful shop refresh would give those accounts more choices. That does not make every random SSR purchase worthless. A newer roster may still benefit, while an account with many promoted SSR Cookies may get little from another random copy. Check your inventory before treating a cheap item as a good purchase.

A summon wishlist would address the other side of that problem: getting the Cookie you need. Pomegranate, Scorpion, and Milk are examples of targets that could help a developing account. A wishlist could give players more direction as the pool grows, but its value would depend on the actual rules and rates.

Use the [Cookie Tier List](/tier-list/) to identify useful targets in your roster planning. That is different from assuming a wishlist will arrive soon or guarantee those targets. Do not plan a spending decision around an unannounced system.

Underperforming Cookies also deserve attention. Cream Puff is one damage-role example worth examining in balance discussions. More buffs could create useful alternatives, rather than leave players collecting Cookies they rarely bring to battle.

An awakening system or more promotion levels might give developed accounts another goal. I would still want better uses for the roster alongside it. Extending the grind without changing the choices could leave the same boredom waiting a little further ahead.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="better-modes" title="New modes should give neglected Cookies a job">

Element-restricted towers could make players build beyond their usual formation. An account that normally picks by skill strength would have a reason to examine the rest of its Grass, Water, or Fire roster. The restriction should create interesting choices, not just demand another expensive team before you can participate.

A roguelike PvE mode could offer temporary upgrades between fights. One run might favor an element; another might improve a class or attack style. A proposed bonus such as one second of invulnerability after a Charge Cookie uses a skill could change how you approach a wave. It is a design example, not a Cookie ability to build around today.

A run like that could work as solo or guild content, with rewards for the fights you clear. I would rather try a strange temporary build than repeat a familiar encounter with a larger HP bar.

Arena needs attention to time costs too. The feedback describes long fights before Pinot Noir reduced the effectiveness of healing-heavy teams, plus delays while choosing opponents and loading battles. Faster fights help, but an optional sweep could reduce the routine further. Players testing a lineup should still have a way to watch it fight.

Guild competition or another PvP format could add variety. It should offer a reason to make different decisions, rather than simply add another queue of tickets to clear. None of these ideas establishes a release schedule, and empty menu space does not confirm future content.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="shorter-session" title="Give the next session a stopping point">

You do not need to fix the entire account in one sitting. A smaller plan makes it easier to tell whether the time helped:

1. Pick one wall and note what ends the attempt.
2. Test one relevant lineup or stat change with the rest unchanged.
3. Check Arena defense after moving levels around.
4. Stop repeating the test when you need more EXP or another upgrade to learn anything new.

Keep Mileage purchases tied to something you will use. Leave hypothetical towers and awakening systems out of today's investment plan. If you have a working team and no useful adjustment left to test, collect what you need and come back later.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="endgame-faq" title="Late-game progression FAQ">

### Does this guide confirm level synchronization or a wishlist?

No. Both are proposed improvements, not confirmed additions. The level 88 synchronization example illustrates a possible design rather than a feature you can unlock.

### Should I reset Cookies whenever I get stuck?

Only when you have a specific replacement to test. Repeated resets add work and can weaken your Arena defense. Keep a stable core and check affected lineups after moving levels.

### Should I buy random SSR Cookies with Mileage?

Judge the purchase against your roster. A developing account may benefit more than one with many promoted SSR Cookies. Extra stock is not automatically useful just because it is cheap.

</GuideSection>

A proposed level-sync system could use the lowest level among 12 invested Cookies. If the lowest were level 88, eligible lower-level Cookies could temporarily match 88. That would let players test a new formation without funding every candidate separately. This is a suggested rule, not an existing unlock instruction.

Resetting levels can help move investment, but repeatedly resetting and rebuilding takes time. It can also leave your Arena defense weaker if it uses a Cookie you just reset. Check that lineup before finishing the session.
Keep most of your EXP in the Cookies you regularly field. Use the
level 100 EXP priority guide
when choosing the next recipient, rather than leveling every possible replacement equally.

Sugar Rune presets would solve a related problem. A Cookie might need different stats for PvP and a boss, yet testing both should not mean repeatedly rebuilding the same setup. Saved builds would make those comparisons easier. Equipment presets and proposed Rune presets are separate features; do not assume one provides the other.
Until you have a switching option that suits the job, keep a note of your working rolls before experimenting. The
gear and Sugar Rune guide
can help narrow the stats worth testing so you make fewer speculative changes.
Level 90 makes casual experiments expensive
segments.name: title

segments.text: Mileage can lose its appeal when you already bought the items you want and must wait for a shop reset. Extra tickets or keys do not solve that for an account that already struggles to use its existing supply.

A useful shop refresh would give those accounts more choices. That does not make every random SSR purchase worthless. A newer roster may still benefit, while an account with many promoted SSR Cookies may get little from another random copy. Check your inventory before treating a cheap item as a good purchase.

A summon wishlist would address the other side of that problem: getting the Cookie you need. Pomegranate, Scorpion, and Milk are examples of targets that could help a developing account. A wishlist could give players more direction as the pool grows, but its value would depend on the actual rules and rates.
Use the
Cookie Tier List

to identify useful targets in your roster planning. That is different from assuming a wishlist will arrive soon or guarantee those targets. Do not plan a spending decision around an unannounced system.

Underperforming Cookies also deserve attention. Cream Puff is one damage-role example worth examining in balance discussions. More buffs could create useful alternatives, rather than leave players collecting Cookies they rarely bring to battle.

An awakening system or more promotion levels might give developed accounts another goal. I would still want better uses for the roster alongside it. Extending the grind without changing the choices could leave the same boredom waiting a little further ahead.
Duplicates need somewhere useful to go
segments.name: title

segments.text: Element-restricted towers could make players build beyond their usual formation. An account that normally picks by skill strength would have a reason to examine the rest of its Grass, Water, or Fire roster. The restriction should create interesting choices, not just demand another expensive team before you can participate.

A roguelike PvE mode could offer temporary upgrades between fights. One run might favor an element; another might improve a class or attack style. A proposed bonus such as one second of invulnerability after a Charge Cookie uses a skill could change how you approach a wave. It is a design example, not a Cookie ability to build around today.
A run like that could work as solo or guild content, with rewards for the fights you clear. I would rather try a strange temporary build than repeat a familiar encounter with a larger HP bar.

Arena needs attention to time costs too. The feedback describes long fights before Pinot Noir reduced the effectiveness of healing-heavy teams, plus delays while choosing opponents and loading battles. Faster fights help, but an optional sweep could reduce the routine further. Players testing a lineup should still have a way to watch it fight.

Guild competition or another PvP format could add variety. It should offer a reason to make different decisions, rather than simply add another queue of tickets to clear. None of these ideas establishes a release schedule, and empty menu space does not confirm future content.
New modes should give neglected Cookies a job
segments.name: title

segments.text: You do not need to fix the entire account in one sitting. A smaller plan makes it easier to tell whether the time helped:
Pick one wall and note what ends the attempt.
Test one relevant lineup or stat change with the rest unchanged.
Check Arena defense after moving levels around.
Stop repeating the test when you need more EXP or another upgrade to learn anything new.

Keep Mileage purchases tied to something you will use. Leave hypothetical towers and awakening systems out of today's investment plan. If you have a working team and no useful adjustment left to test, collect what you need and come back later.
Give the next session a stopping point
segments.name: title

segments.text: Does this guide confirm level synchronization or a wishlist?
No. Both are proposed improvements, not confirmed additions. The level 88 synchronization example illustrates a possible design rather than a feature you can unlock.
Should I reset Cookies whenever I get stuck?
Only when you have a specific replacement to test. Repeated resets add work and can weaken your Arena defense. Keep a stable core and check affected lineups after moving levels.
Should I buy random SSR Cookies with Mileage?
Judge the purchase against your roster. A developing account may benefit more than one with many promoted SSR Cookies. Extra stock is not automatically useful just because it is cheap.
Late-game progression FAQ

cookie-run-crumble-equipment-choice-guid.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Two equipment rolls sit on screen. One adds Combat Power. The other keeps the Accuracy and Focus your team needs. Which one should you keep?

Before roughly Oven level 10, taking the higher-power piece is a reasonable shortcut. After that, check the size of the power gain first. When the two pieces are close, fix missing Accuracy, then consider Focus, Skill Amp, and Skill Haste. Once attacks land reliably, extra Accuracy can wait.

If you keep choosing Accuracy after misses stop, you may pass up the Focus roll that would help your poison stacks land.

<GuideSection id="left-or-right" title="Choose the piece that fixes the current problem">

Use this order for stage progression. It helps with ordinary equipment comparisons; it does not make every small power increase worth a swap.

| What you see | What to favor |
| --- | --- |
| You are still below about Oven level 10 | Higher Combat Power for quick early progress |
| One piece gives a much larger power increase | Consider the power upgrade, then check what useful stats you lose |
| Power is similar and attacks often miss | Accuracy |
| Attacks connect but important debuffs remain unreliable | Focus, alongside a check of your power deficit |
| Accuracy and debuffs already work well | Skill Amp, then Skill Haste as the stage-oriented starting order |
| Your team dies before it can work | Test Damage Reduction instead of forcing another offensive roll |

There is no fixed percentage that makes a power increase "much larger" here. Look at your current stage and the size of the loss elsewhere. A modest upgrade that removes your main Accuracy roll deserves more thought than an obvious early-game replacement.

Check the lineup too. If you are still choosing which Cookies to invest in, use the [Cookie Tier List](/tier-list/) before spending materials around a Cookie you rarely field. Equipment decisions make more sense once you know who will use the stats.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="accuracy-check" title="Fix misses before chasing more damage">

An attack that misses cannot apply its attached debuff. That makes Accuracy more than a damage concern. A missed debuff can leave the rest of the team attacking without the effect it needs.

Open a Cookie's detailed stats and scroll to Accuracy and Focus. Check those numbers, then watch the fight. Frequent "Miss" messages tell you something that the equipment comparison alone cannot.

Around chapter 200, roughly 900 Accuracy is a useful progression reference. Treat it as a place to start checking, not a universal minimum or a cap. Your stage and research affect the comparison. It also says nothing precise about the amount a much earlier account needs.

Suppose the left piece gives a little more power but drops Accuracy, while the right keeps it steady. If misses already interrupt the run, favor the right. If attacks land consistently and Accuracy is comfortably covered, compare the other stats instead. You do not need to keep choosing Accuracy forever.

The [Accuracy and Focus guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-accuracy-focus-guide/) explains the two checks in more detail if you cannot tell which one is failing.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="focus-and-power" title="Judge Focus against the stage, not another account">

Focus has no equally tidy target. Your Combat Power relative to the stage changes how difficult it is to apply debuffs. A stronger account can land them more reliably with less Focus than a weaker account has.

Poison might stall at four or six stacks when you need ten, even though you copied a stronger account's Focus total. More Focus can help, but the power gap still matters.

For a debuff-dependent team, watch the stack count or the effect you need during the same part of the fight. If attacks connect but the effect keeps failing, compare Focus rolls. Avoid judging the swap from one lucky clear. Repeat the same stage with the same lineup so you can see whether the change improves consistency.

You may accept more retries when pushing a single difficult clear. For routine farming, that becomes tiresome fast. A Focus piece that makes the run repeatable can be worth keeping even when another piece looks more aggressive.

Use the [recommended Teams](/teams/) to check whether your formation relies on poison, DEF Down, or other debuffs. A gear choice that helps that formation may matter less in a different one.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="enhancement-order" title="Spread upgrades to +10 before pushing +15">

Bring equipment slots to +10 across the set before concentrating on +15. After that, a practical stage-progression order starts with Accuracy, followed by Focus. Skill Amp is the next default choice, though upgrading the weapon first is another option when damage needs the investment.

Eventually you will work through the remaining equipment too. The question is where the next batch of materials does the most good while you cannot afford everything.

Leave DEF, HP, and Evasion toward the end of this progression order. They give relatively weak power gains in this approach. That does not mean survival never matters. If the team dies early, reassess the fight and test Damage Reduction rather than treating the upgrade list as a command to ignore incoming damage.

Keep enhancement order separate from Sugar Rune choices. They use different decisions and resources. The broader [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) covers role-specific rolls when you need to tune an individual Cookie beyond this Oven comparison.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-presets" title="Use different priorities for Arena, but check the preset">

For Arena equipment, start with Skill Amp, then Skill Haste. CRIT DMG and CRIT Chance come next, followed by Damage Reduction and CRIT Resistance. This is a practical farming order, not a promise that one stat wins every matchup.

Before spending Dough on a separate Arena setup, check which equipment preset receives the drops. The preset setup described here does not let you freely move a desirable piece from one set to the other. A rare stage upgrade landing in your PvP set can be frustrating when your main set still needs it.

I would finish a useful main set before committing scarce rolls to a second one. If you do build an Arena set, confirm the selected preset before farming and again before fighting.

<GuideTip title="Power suddenly dropped?">

Check the active equipment preset before replacing anything. Switching to a weaker set can explain a sudden power loss even when you have not changed your Cookies.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="eternal-filter" title="Do not make Eternal your only acceptable drop">

Eternal equipment can offer noticeably stronger stat values at comparable enhancement. Its rarity still makes it a poor sole target for an ordinary farming session. You can spend a large pile of Dough waiting for one piece.

Set the farming rarity threshold one grade below the highest grade you can currently obtain. That keeps the next-best drops in consideration while you wait for a better one. Recheck the setting after your Oven unlocks another grade; a filter that made sense earlier may no longer fit.

Higher equipment levels can produce higher stat values, so read the numbers before rejecting a piece by appearance. Compare enhancement levels too. You want to understand what the new roll changes, rather than mistake an enhancement gap for a better underlying piece.

Before your next roll, note your current Accuracy and Focus. If you decide to swap a piece, keep the same lineup and Pets for the next attempt. Watch whether the misses or missing debuffs improve before spending enhancement materials on it.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="equipment-faq" title="Equipment choice FAQ">

### Should I always keep the higher-power equipment?

No. It is a reasonable shortcut before roughly Oven level 10. Later, weigh large power gains against useful stats. When power is similar, fix missing Accuracy before considering Focus, Skill Amp, and Skill Haste.

### Is 900 Accuracy enough for every stage?

No. Roughly 900 Accuracy is a reference around chapter 200, not a universal requirement or cap. Check your current stage, research, and visible misses before deciding whether to add more.

### What Focus number should I aim for?

There is no single target here. Your power relative to the stage affects debuff reliability. Watch the debuff you need and compare Focus upgrades under the same battle conditions.

### Which equipment should reach +15 first?

Bring the set to +10 first. For stage progression, prioritize Accuracy, then Focus, then usually Skill Amp. Weapon-first investment is another option; leave DEF, HP, and Evasion until later unless survival needs attention.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-fast-account-growth-g.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Some CookieRun: Crumble accounts play every day and still grow like they are dragging an Oven uphill. The problem is often the order of the work. Claim a Lucky Reward before pushing a stage, repeat a comfortable dungeon floor, leave Arena tickets capped, and the account keeps buying tomorrow's upgrades at yesterday's prices.

You do not need a perfect roster to fix that. You need each daily action to make the next one pay more.

<GuideSection id="push-before-claiming" title="Push stages before claiming the good rewards">

Campaign progress improves more than the chapter number. Lucky Rewards scale with the stage milestones shown in their reward panel, so check that panel before spending the day's rolls. If the next milestone is one or two clears away, make the push first. The same roll can then land on a better reward table.

Do not get cute near reset. A saved roll that expires is worth less than an early roll on the current table. Push while the team still has a realistic clear, then collect before the daily cutoff.

This also applies to idle rewards. A boss sitting at 5% health is a reason to collect, upgrade, and retry. A boss deleting the front line in five seconds is a team problem. Start from a proven shell on the [recommended teams page](/teams/), then change the slot that is failing instead of feeding materials to all twelve Cookies at once.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="enhancement-order" title="Use +5, +10, and +15 as different jobs">

Early account enhancement does not need a grand strategy. Bring the available lines to +5, then raise them evenly toward +10. Those cheap levels spread useful stats across the roster and keep one expensive node from eating the whole coin pile.

The choice matters more at +15. Accuracy is the safest first target because a missed attack contributes nothing. Focus comes next for a lineup that depends on DEF Down, damage over time, or another debuff landing reliably. After those, choose Skill Amp or ATK based on what the active Cookies use. CRIT, Damage Reduction, and CRIT Resist can follow.

If the team dies early, move a defensive upgrade forward. If it survives and loses to the timer, stop buying comfort and add damage. The menu order is not a commandment.

<GuideTip title="A useful +15 order">

For a normal stage-pushing account, start with Accuracy, then Focus, then Skill Amp or ATK. Change that order only when repeated attempts show a specific survival problem.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="gear-tie-breakers" title="Take the Power upgrade, then read the substats">

During the first stretch, replacing gear with the higher displayed Power is fine. Those pieces will not stay forever, and crossing a stage Power band can matter more than a tidy substat on weak gear.

When two pieces are close, use Accuracy as the first tie-breaker, followed by Focus, Skill Amp, and Skill Haste. This is a progression rule, not a forever build. Once better gear has several useful rolls, match the stats to the Cookie's actual job.

Do not keep swapping blindly once the green number stops helping. The [Power and stage damage guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-power-guide-stage-damage/) explains why a higher total can rescue one run yet lose another after you break an important synergy.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="push-dungeon-floors" title="Stop farming the easy Daily Dungeon floor">

Daily Dungeon keys become much better when you push first. The gap is not small. A lower floor can show about 64 of a reward, while a late floor can reach roughly 6,000 per key. Spending today's key on the old floor also delays the permanent upgrade that could clear tomorrow's floor.

Use the first attempt on the highest uncleared stage that looks reasonable. If it nearly clears, take the cheapest available account upgrade and try again. Farm the previous floor only after the push has genuinely stopped.

Crumble Dungeon deserves at least one daily run too. Plaque Tower can wait when it hard-walls the account, but a fresh dungeon floor and its first-clear reward should not sit untouched because the older one finishes ten seconds faster.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="spend-arena-tickets" title="Turn Arena tickets into permanent stats">

New players sometimes avoid Arena until their roster looks respectable. Meanwhile the ticket counter fills and stops producing attempts. Pick opponents you are likely to beat and spend the tickets.

Fame levels raise account stats. They also build bonuses such as boss damage, elemental damage, and CRIT damage. Those gains follow you back into PvE, which makes a safe Arena win part of stage progression.

Lineup Power is the number to watch during a stage. In one simple test, Wind Archer's hit read 192 on the displayed scale. Adding a healer with no ATK buff and no new Pet moved the hit to 576. The healer did not secretly become a damage support. The larger lineup crossed into a better Power correction band.

That is why total account Power can look impressive while the selected formation still struggles. Spend Arena attempts for permanent growth, but judge the next stage with the twelve Cookies you actually brought.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="save-stellar-points" title="Accept a good Stellar Link board early">

Stellar Points are too scarce for perfection on a young account. Around 70% coverage is a sensible stopping point for a free player. Keep the board, move deeper into the system, and save the serious rerolls for later sections where the percentages are larger.

Locking a section also raises the cost of future attempts. It is easy to spend a week's currency fixing one ugly gap while gaining less Power than a cheap research node would have given immediately. The [account resource traps guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-resource-guide-account-traps/) covers the other taps that look harmless until the balance hits zero.

Cookie promotions feed Stellar Link progress, which gives featured banners a second job. Five stars is a practical baseline for a pickup Cookie you expect to use. Beyond that, read the next promotion effect and check the current [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/). Six or seven stars should solve a real roster need, not soothe the discomfort of stopping mid-banner.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="research-and-guild" title="Climb research and use the guild exchange">

Move up the research tree one required node at a time. Filling every early branch feels organized, but it delays account-wide upgrades and burns the materials needed higher up. Research speed is a strong early pick because every later timer benefits. The side chest research near Lucky Rewards can wait while supplies are tight.

Join a guild before your roster looks impressive. Guild membership works across servers, and you can find your server's S-number under Settings, then Account. Guild Conquest rewards, ranking rewards, research help, and the exchange all speed up an account that would otherwise play alone.

If you do not own Tea Knight, save guild currency for the first useful copy. His Boss DMG Up job is difficult to replace in Guild Conquest. After securing him, Stellar Points become a strong repeat purchase for free and light-spending accounts because their regular income is thin.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="daily-growth-route" title="Run this 15-minute growth route">

1. Check the next Lucky Reward milestone, then push the campaign before rolling.
2. Spend Daily Dungeon keys on first clears or the highest farmable floor.
3. Use Arena tickets on safe opponents before the counter caps.
4. Claim Fame, enhancement, collection, and other permanent account upgrades.
5. Advance one useful research path and collect guild rewards.
6. Keep a workable Stellar Link board instead of rerolling from boredom.
7. Return to the stage wall with the upgraded lineup.

One failed retry is information. A team that survives but times out needs damage or a better Power band. A formation that collapses immediately needs defense, healing, or a safer position. Once the sensible upgrades are spent, collect the remaining rewards and stop. An extra hour of menu shuffling does not create another dungeon key.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="fast-growth-faq" title="CookieRun: Crumble fast progression FAQ">

### Should I use Lucky Reward rolls before or after pushing stages?

Push first when the next reward milestone is within reach, then use the rolls on the improved table. Spend them before reset if the alternative is losing them.

### What should I enhance to +15 first?

Accuracy is the safest first choice for normal progression because missed attacks deal no damage. Follow with Focus when debuffs matter, then Skill Amp or ATK. Move defense forward only when the team dies early.

### Should I repeat an easy Daily Dungeon floor?

Try the highest uncleared floor first. Higher floors improve each key's payout, and first clears add more rewards. Repeat the previous floor only after the next one has genuinely stopped your lineup.

### How much Stellar Link coverage is enough for a beginner?

About 70% is a reasonable early stopping point for a free account. Later sections offer larger gains, while locking and rerolling the opening board can drain scarce Stellar Points.

### What should I buy first from the guild exchange?

Save for Tea Knight if you do not own him and plan to play Guild Conquest. After the first useful copy, Stellar Points are a strong recurring choice because dependable free sources are limited.

</GuideSection>

When two pieces are close, use Accuracy as the first tie-breaker, followed by Focus, Skill Amp, and Skill Haste. This is a progression rule, not a forever build. Once better gear has several useful rolls, match the stats to the Cookie's actual job.
Do not keep swapping blindly once the green number stops helping. The
Power and stage damage guide
explains why a higher total can rescue one run yet lose another after you break an important synergy.
Take the Power upgrade, then read the substats
segments.name: title

segments.text: Daily Dungeon keys become much better when you push first. The gap is not small. A lower floor can show about 64 of a reward, while a late floor can reach roughly 6,000 per key. Spending today's key on the old floor also delays the permanent upgrade that could clear tomorrow's floor.

Use the first attempt on the highest uncleared stage that looks reasonable. If it nearly clears, take the cheapest available account upgrade and try again. Farm the previous floor only after the push has genuinely stopped.

Crumble Dungeon deserves at least one daily run too. Plaque Tower can wait when it hard-walls the account, but a fresh dungeon floor and its first-clear reward should not sit untouched because the older one finishes ten seconds faster.
Stop farming the easy Daily Dungeon floor
segments.name: title

segments.text: New players sometimes avoid Arena until their roster looks respectable. Meanwhile the ticket counter fills and stops producing attempts. Pick opponents you are likely to beat and spend the tickets.

Fame levels raise account stats. They also build bonuses such as boss damage, elemental damage, and CRIT damage. Those gains follow you back into PvE, which makes a safe Arena win part of stage progression.

Lineup Power is the number to watch during a stage. In one simple test, Wind Archer's hit read 192 on the displayed scale. Adding a healer with no ATK buff and no new Pet moved the hit to 576. The healer did not secretly become a damage support. The larger lineup crossed into a better Power correction band.

That is why total account Power can look impressive while the selected formation still struggles. Spend Arena attempts for permanent growth, but judge the next stage with the twelve Cookies you actually brought.
Turn Arena tickets into permanent stats
segments.name: title

segments.text: Stellar Points are too scarce for perfection on a young account. Around 70% coverage is a sensible stopping point for a free player. Keep the board, move deeper into the system, and save the serious rerolls for later sections where the percentages are larger.

Locking a section also raises the cost of future attempts. It is easy to spend a week's currency fixing one ugly gap while gaining less Power than a cheap research node would have given immediately. The
account resource traps guide
covers the other taps that look harmless until the balance hits zero.

Cookie promotions feed Stellar Link progress, which gives featured banners a second job. Five stars is a practical baseline for a pickup Cookie you expect to use. Beyond that, read the next promotion effect and check the current
CookieRun: Crumble Tier List
. Six or seven stars should solve a real roster need, not soothe the discomfort of stopping mid-banner.
Accept a good Stellar Link board early
segments.name: title

segments.text: Move up the research tree one required node at a time. Filling every early branch feels organized, but it delays account-wide upgrades and burns the materials needed higher up. Research speed is a strong early pick because every later timer benefits. The side chest research near Lucky Rewards can wait while supplies are tight.

Join a guild before your roster looks impressive. Guild membership works across servers, and you can find your server's S-number under Settings, then Account. Guild Conquest rewards, ranking rewards, research help, and the exchange all speed up an account that would otherwise play alone.

If you do not own Tea Knight, save guild currency for the first useful copy. His Boss DMG Up job is difficult to replace in Guild Conquest. After securing him, Stellar Points become a strong repeat purchase for free and light-spending accounts because their regular income is thin.
Climb research and use the guild exchange
segments.name: title

segments.text: Check the next Lucky Reward milestone, then push the campaign before rolling.
Spend Daily Dungeon keys on first clears or the highest farmable floor.
Use Arena tickets on safe opponents before the counter caps.
Claim Fame, enhancement, collection, and other permanent account upgrades.
Advance one useful research path and collect guild rewards.
Keep a workable Stellar Link board instead of rerolling from boredom.
Return to the stage wall with the upgraded lineup.

One failed retry is information. A team that survives but times out needs damage or a better Power band. A formation that collapses immediately needs defense, healing, or a safer position. Once the sensible upgrades are spent, collect the remaining rewards and stop. An extra hour of menu shuffling does not create another dungeon key.
Run this 15-minute growth route
segments.name: title

segments.text: Should I use Lucky Reward rolls before or after pushing stages?
Push first when the next reward milestone is within reach, then use the rolls on the improved table. Spend them before reset if the alternative is losing them.
What should I enhance to +15 first?

Accuracy is the safest first choice for normal progression because missed attacks deal no damage. Follow with Focus when debuffs matter, then Skill Amp or ATK. Move defense forward only when the team dies early.
Should I repeat an easy Daily Dungeon floor?
Try the highest uncleared floor first. Higher floors improve each key's payout, and first clears add more rewards. Repeat the previous floor only after the next one has genuinely stopped your lineup.
How much Stellar Link coverage is enough for a beginner?
About 70% is a reasonable early stopping point for a free account. Later sections offer larger gains, while locking and rerolling the opening board can drain scarce Stellar Points.
What should I buy first from the guild exchange?
Save for Tea Knight if you do not own him and plan to play Guild Conquest. After the first useful copy, Stellar Points are a strong recurring choice because dependable free sources are limited.
CookieRun: Crumble fast progression FAQ

cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats.text:
import { GuideSection } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

A Cherry Cola with perfect damage rolls still contributes very little after dying in the opening exchange. Meanwhile, an ordinary SR ATK roll can improve both Milk's healing and the buff your damage dealers receive. Before another reroll, check which part of the skill the stat improves.

For CookieRun: Crumble Sugar Runes, start with the skill you need that Cookie to deliver. Pure attackers want damage multipliers. Healers need stronger recovery. Debuffers often need another cast or enough health to survive until it happens. The class icon only tells part of that story.

<GuideSection id="upgrade-budget" title="Keep a useful SR before chasing a perfect SSR">

**A suitable SR roll is a sensible stopping point for a limited budget.** Sugar Runes involve several layers of luck: the stat, its rarity, and three possible values within that rarity. Hunting the highest value of one exact SSR stat can consume materials that would improve several teammates.

Decide which stats you will accept before rolling. A damage dealer can use four strong options, so keep any useful result from that group. Save tighter locks for Cookies with narrow needs, such as a buffer that mainly wants Skill Amp.

Promotion unlocks more slots, but an unlocked slot does not need a perfect roll immediately. Use the [tier list](/tier-list/) to shortlist regular investments, then prioritize the Cookies you actually field. A specialist used once a week can wait while your everyday healer gets a workable set.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="damage-runes" title="Give damage dealers four good options">

For Milky Way, Melon Soda, Brightseeker, Rye, Wind Archer, and Espresso, aim for ATK%, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, or Skill Amp. These Cookies mainly earn their slots through damage. Vampire can follow the same general approach when you use him as an attacker.

Skill Haste remains usable, but it usually trails those four options for pure damage. Many attackers already have short cooldowns, so extra casts may offer less than stronger hits. Do not reroll a good offensive SR simply because a theoretical ranking puts another damage stat slightly ahead.

Strawberry Crepe follows this damage approach despite the Defense label. Build for the AoE damage you brought Crepe to deliver. Innate bulk gives you more room to spend Rune slots on offense, although you should still watch survival on harder stages.

Scorpion deserves a little extra attention. Skill Amp and ATK% are strong targets; CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, and Skill Haste are also usable. Keep a good offensive roll rather than burning currency to settle a tiny difference between damage options. Check team Focus separately if poison applications keep failing.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="healer-runes" title="Healers need stronger recovery, not just shorter cooldowns">

Herb, Grapevine, and Milk heal through ATK scaling, so start with **Skill Amp and ATK%**. Bigger heals matter when enemies deal damage in bursts. A slightly faster heal can still leave a Cookie in danger if it restores too little health.

Skill Haste is a reasonable fallback. It helps when you need more casts, but it should not automatically replace strong healing stats. Watch the actual failure: does the heal arrive too late, or does it land and barely move the health bar?

Milk has an extra reason to keep ATK%. The ATK buff scales with Milk's own ATK, so that Rune can help the whole damage group as well as recovery. Skill Amp and Skill Haste remain useful choices for the buffing and healing jobs.

If a healer dies before doing either job, keep a defensive result. Damage Reduction or Evasion can be practical temporary choices. Keep that working set while the rest of your lineup still needs useful rolls.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="buff-scaling" title="Read the buff before adding ATK">

Macaron's CRIT Chance buff does not scale with Macaron's own ATK. Give Macaron Skill Amp and Skill Haste instead. Pomegranate also favors those two stats, with Skill Amp a strong first target.

Cheesecake's ATK buff needs the same careful reading. An ATK increase for the recipient does not mean that raising Cheesecake's personal ATK strengthens it. Skill Amp is the main target here. Tea Knight also wants Skill Amp when you bring him for the team's damage buff.

Pinot Noir is the exception that trips people up. Skill Amp improves neither Healing Received Down nor the Lift Resistance buff. Do not reroll it expecting stronger anti-heal or knock-up protection; Focus can help when enemies resist the debuff, while Accuracy helps when attacks miss.

Haste has less urgency on Pinot Noir. The anti-heal lasts five seconds on a 3.25-second cooldown, while Shadow Vine lasts ten seconds on a 9.5-second cooldown. Those timers already overlap. Unless a particular fight exposes a timing problem, prioritize the stat that fixes missed attacks or resisted debuffs instead of paying for more Haste.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="focus-debuffers" title="Debuffers need uptime and survival">

Skill Amp no longer strengthens stat reductions such as DEF Down and ATK Down. The [Skill Amp changes guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-skill-amp-fix-rune-refund/) explains the affected effects. A debuffer may still deal more damage with Skill Amp, but that does not improve the reduction you selected it for.

Devil benefits from Skill Haste and defensive stats. Dark Choco also likes Haste because faster casts help build DEF Down stacks. HP or other survival rolls are acceptable when keeping the debuffer alive matters more than personal damage.

Moon Rabbit's ATK Down and CRIT Chance Down do not become stronger with Skill Amp. Their five-second duration and seven-second cooldown make Skill Haste useful for reducing the gap. Add Damage Reduction, HP, DEF, or Evasion when incoming damage is the problem.

Focus and Accuracy can help, but check equipment first. Gear raises those stats across the squad, and it may already cover the stage's needs. Do not spend scarce personal Rune slots solving a problem the whole team shares. The [Accuracy and Focus guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-accuracy-focus-guide/) helps separate missed attacks from resisted debuffs.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="charge-survival" title="Protect fragile Charge Cookies">

Cherry Cola can deal plenty of damage without a full offensive Rune set. Staying alive is the harder part. Favor Damage Reduction, or mix it with damage if your formation already offers enough protection. HP and DEF are usable alternatives. A full damage build becomes expensive when you keep watching Cherry Cola disappear.

Princess Bari has more room for offense because Guided Soul gives damage protection and resistance to displacement. Try the normal damage stats when Bari survives comfortably. Keep defensive rolls if charging into the enemy still gets Bari killed. Her built-in protection is helpful, not a promise that every stage is safe.

Tiger Lily usually fills a synergy and support slot. Skill Haste plus Damage Reduction can help, but avoid heavy investment in a Cookie that dies quickly and mainly needs to provide the team's synergy.

Skating Queen has a different support job: improving CRIT DMG. Favor Skill Amp for that buff. Haste can produce more frequent ice casts, though it is a secondary choice rather than the reason to rebuild the set.

Compare your protection with the [recommended teams](/teams/) before rerolling every melee Cookie. A missing healer or defensive teammate can make otherwise sensible Rune choices look terrible.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="shields-and-summons" title="Build shields and summons around their scaling">

Ion Cookie Robot needs to survive long enough to provide the shield. HP strengthens the shield, and Skill Amp can help its eligible shielding effect. Neither makes the separate Damage Reduction effect stronger. Keep enough defensive stats to survive the opening hit.

Nameless Cake Hound can use Skill Haste for a relatively long cooldown, offensive stats for damage, or defensive stats for survival. Do not select Skill Amp specifically to increase its Damage Reduction.

Licorice favors Skill Amp or ATK for summon output, with survival rolls also usable. Haste is a lower priority when the summons already remain alive and active. Cool Mint needs more caution: as a fragile Charge Cookie, prioritize survival, then consider ATK% for the summon setup.

For Space Doughnut in a crowd-control role, use Skill Haste and survival. Skill Amp does not make a stun stronger. More reliable casts offer a clearer benefit than chasing personal damage.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="check-the-failure" title="Check gear before spending another reroll">

Equipment and personal Sugar Runes solve different problems. If several Cookies miss attacks or fail debuffs together, review the squad's Accuracy and Focus through gear. If only Cherry Cola dies, a personal survival adjustment makes more sense.

Use the same stage and lineup for a comparison. Watch the opening exchange, healing recovery, and whether important effects stay active. Keep Pets unchanged so you can tell what the Rune adjustment did. A larger Power number alone does not establish that the new set performs better.

Avoid targeting Move Speed or Resistance as default Rune rolls for these builds. They rarely address the jobs described here. Stop once your active Cookies have useful stats; squeezing one perfect result out of a finished attacker can leave several teammates waiting.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="gear-rune-faq" title="Sugar Rune FAQ">

### Should free players chase SSR Sugar Runes?

Useful SR rolls are enough to build a working set. Keep a suitable SSR when it appears, but do not spend the whole budget chasing one exact stat or the highest value within its rarity.

### Is Skill Haste the best stat for every Cookie?

No. Pure damage dealers usually prefer ATK%, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, or Skill Amp. Haste becomes more useful when you need faster stacking, repeated control, or better coverage on effects such as Moon Rabbit's debuffs.

### Should every support use ATK%?

No. Herb, Grapevine, and Milk benefit through ATK-based healing, and Milk's buff also scales with personal ATK. Macaron and Cheesecake do not strengthen their buffs by stacking their own ATK. Read the scaling line first.

### Does Skill Amp improve every defensive effect?

No. Ion's shield can benefit, while the separate Damage Reduction effect does not. Nameless Cake Hound's Damage Reduction also does not scale with Skill Amp. Evaluate each effect separately before locking the stat.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-gingercraven-boss-gui.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

GingerCraven has a rude way of making a decent account look broken. You can enter with 292.71M Power, survive most of the fight, then watch the final knockback scatter the lineup and erase the attempt. Adding another damage dealer usually makes that ending arrive sooner.

The safer answer is a sustain shell built around Scorpion Cookie. Three healers keep the group upright, GingerBright cuts the boss's ATK, Dark Choco lowers DEF, and the rest of the formation turns each Scorpion cycle into useful damage. A clean opening still matters, so expect an occasional restart. Compared with a damage-heavy team, this plan gives the fight fewer ways to go wrong.

<GuideSection id="why-gingercraven-wipes-teams" title="Why GingerCraven wipes a strong team">

Two problems overlap here. First, GingerCraven hits hard enough that a normal stage team can lose one support before its healing loop settles. Second, a large gap below the stage's Recommended Power can reduce the damage your Cookies deal. That leaves the boss alive longer, so the lineup has to absorb more dangerous cycles.

This is why the Power number can feel dishonest. The formation may have the right buffs and debuffs but still need a little more account strength. Check the [CookieRun: Crumble Power guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-power-guide-stage-damage/) if your damage suddenly falls off at this stage. A small Resolve or promotion gain can matter more than replacing a Cookie that already performs the correct job.

The other trap is movement. When the team's HP is low, dragging everyone across the arena can walk the Cookies into another boss skill before Grapevine, Lime, or Herb finishes a cast. Stop. Let the green bars recover, then reposition.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="recommended-gingercraven-team" title="Copy the 12-Cookie sustain team">

Set Scorpion Cookie as leader. The slot order below matches the tested 292.71M formation, including the three Pets. Keeping the order also makes it easier to compare your run with the healing and knockback timing described later.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="GingerCraven sustain and Scorpion team"
  description="Scorpion leads the damage plan while GingerBright and Dark Choco weaken the boss. Grapevine, Lime, Herb, and the defensive supports keep the formation alive through the push."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0126", "cookie4003", "cookie0054", "cookie4024", "cookie0103", "cookie0181", "cookie0018", "cookie0040", "cookie4019", "cookie0063", "cookie0003"]}
  petIds={["pet0110", "pet4001", "pet4003"]}
/>

Save this as a boss preset. When you return to story farming, Arena, or daily stages, use the site's [recommended teams](/teams/) instead of hauling all twelve Cookies into every mode. GingerCraven rewards survival more heavily than most routine fights.

<GuideTip title="Check the ATK Down slot">
Use GingerBright in slot 12. GingerBrave cannot replace the ATK Down effect that keeps this formation stable.
</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="cookie-jobs" title="Know what each Cookie is doing">

Scorpion is the main damage dealer and should be the leader. Her damage over time becomes dependable at five stars, where the relevant trigger reaches 100%. If she is below that breakpoint, the team can still work, but failed applications create wider swings between attempts.

GingerBright and Dark Choco prepare the target. GingerBright applies ATK Down, which reduces the pressure on every healer. Dark Choco brings DEF Down now that Devil Cookie is less attractive for this job. Pomegranate adds Skill Amp Up so Scorpion and the support cycle get more value from each cast.

Grapevine, Lime, and Herb form the healing core. Grapevine is the plain, reliable healer. Lime adds healing and CRIT Chance Up, which lets the team survive without abandoning burst damage. Herb gives another steady recovery line and receives Multi-strike, so the same synergy package can improve his healing output.

Macaron and Skating Queen turn that survival time into damage. Macaron raises CRIT Chance, while Skating Queen raises CRIT DMG. Above 100% CRIT Chance, attacks can double crit; above 200%, they can triple crit. Reaching those numbers is hard, but the two buffs still make every Scorpion cycle less dependent on one lucky roll.

Tiger Lily supplies a useful low-rarity body and Multi-shot synergy. Nameless Cake Hound reduces damage taken. Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician brings healing plus ATK Up. None of these slots looks glamorous on a damage chart, which is exactly why the lineup survives long enough to finish the boss.

If you are deciding where Scorpion and the supports sit in the broader roster, use the [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/) as context. Promotion and Sugar Runes still decide whether your version can do the advertised job.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="sugar-rune-priorities" title="Build the Sugar Runes for the job">

Do not give every support the same Rune page just because Skill Amp appears on many recommendations. The recent stat changes narrowed where Skill Amp helps debuffs.

- Scorpion wants Skill Haste, Skill Amp, and ATK Amp. Keep enough Focus for her damage plan to land reliably, but do not reroll a strong set only to chase a prettier number.
- Grapevine, Lime, Tiger Lily, Macaron, Herb, Skating Queen, and Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician prefer Skill Haste and Skill Amp, followed by useful ATK or ATK Amp rolls.
- GingerBright wants Focus, Accuracy, or defensive stats. Skill Amp no longer strengthens the ATK Down effect.
- Dark Choco needs Focus for DEF Down and enough defense to stay present through the dangerous cycles.
- Nameless Cake Hound values Skill Haste plus defensive rolls. A dead damage reducer is decorative furniture.
- Pomegranate wants Skill Haste and Skill Amp so the team receives the support buff more often.

Upgrade the SR and SSR lines you can afford before chasing perfect rolls. A workable set across all twelve Cookies beats one support with museum-quality Sugar Runes and eleven underbuilt teammates.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pet-loadout" title="Use the three-Pet survival package">

Octo Wasabi grants Duration synergy and raises ATK for Cookies that receive it. Holy Baby Drop gives ATK to all allies. Majestic King Choco Drop raises Max HP, buying the extra second that often separates a recovery cast from a wipe.

You can clear without Majestic King Choco Drop. Use Kiwi Bird for DEF Up if you do not own the SSR Pet. That replacement lowers the team's HP cushion but keeps the same purpose: survive the knockback with enough Cookies alive to restart the healing loop.

Avoid swapping the defensive Pet for a pure damage option until the formation already survives consistently. Faster failure is still failure.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="fight-sequence" title="Play the knockback without panicking">

1. Make Scorpion the leader before entering. Her damage over time finishes the boss, so the other eleven slots support that cycle.
2. Collapse the group close to GingerCraven when the opening allows it. Stacking keeps the formation's movement predictable and helps the support cycle cover the same area.
3. Watch HP before dragging the leader. If several bars are low, wait for Grapevine, Lime, or Herb to cast. Moving during that gap can feed the team directly into the next skill.
4. Expect the boss to push the formation away. Survive that moment first. Once the team stabilizes, move back in and let Scorpion continue stacking damage.
5. Restart when GingerBright, Grapevine, or another core support dies before the main push. The team has enough sustain to win, but it cannot repair a broken cycle with half its parts missing.

</GuideSection>

Start with the death log in your head. If the boss survives while the team remains healthy, raise Scorpion's damage, promotion, or Power. If the boss's damage spikes because ATK Down fails, add Focus or Accuracy to GingerBright rather than piling more Skill Amp onto the wrong stat.

Use Macaron, Pomegranate, Grapevine, Lime, Nameless Cake Hound, Dark Choco, Scorpion, Skating Queen, Tiger Lily, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, Herb, and GingerBright. Pair them with Octo Wasabi, Holy Baby Drop, and Majestic King Choco Drop.

### Who should be the leader against GingerCraven?

Scorpion Cookie should lead. Her damage over time is the main finisher, and the other eleven Cookies protect or amplify that plan.

Use GingerBright. GingerBright applies the ATK Down effect used by this formation, while GingerBrave does not fill that exact role.

cookie-run-crumble-guild-conquest-team-g.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Guild Conquest can make the same account look brilliant in one run and half asleep in the next. Your first attempt might land around 250M damage, then the next jumps by 60M without a promotion or Rune change. That swing is normal. Extra-Stuffed Piñata has enough random targeting and timing variance that one result tells you very little.

Entries are unlimited, so use them. Build a sensible single-target team, keep the important buffs and debuffs, then run it several times. The two lineups below use the same core and the same three Pets. Wind Archer has the better damage ceiling in this comparison, while Milky Way gives accounts without a strong Wind Archer a practical second option.

<GuideSection id="guild-conquest-rules" title="Understand what raises your Guild Conquest score">

Extra-Stuffed Piñata is a Dark boss, which makes Light attackers useful. That does not mean you should cram every Light Cookie into the formation. The boss still asks for enough healing, damage reduction, DEF Down, Lift Resistance, and single-target damage to keep all twelve slots working.

Start by checking the jobs, not the Power total. Scorpion, Rye, and Melon Soda handle most of the direct damage in the two accessible teams. Macaron raises CRIT Chance. Skating Queen adds CRIT DMG. Pomegranate improves eligible skills with Skill Amp Up, while Dark Choco lowers the boss's DEF. If one of those jobs disappears, another damage dealer rarely covers the loss.

Save Guild Medals instead of spending them on whatever looks cheap in the exchange. Tea Knight is built for this mode because his Boss DMG Up applies to the whole plan. You can use the teams below before owning him, then add him once the exchange gives you enough copies.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="wind-archer-team" title="Use the Wind Archer damage team">

Start with this lineup when Wind Archer is close to the rest of your roster in promotion and Rune quality. He adds another focused damage slot, but promotion matters. If your copy is well below five stars and Milky Way has far better levels and Runes, test both before assuming the TSSR label wins automatically.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Wind Archer Guild Conquest team"
  description="Wind Archer joins Scorpion, Rye, and Melon Soda for the higher single-target ceiling. The remaining slots supply CRIT buffs, Skill Amp, DEF Down, healing, and Lift Resistance."
  cookieIds={["cookie0070", "cookie0181", "cookie0040", "cookie0126", "cookie3001", "cookie4024", "cookie0059", "cookie0515", "cookie4010", "cookie0018", "cookie4019", "cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet4001", "pet0111", "pet0069"]}
/>

Do not judge this preset from one attempt. Run it at least three times and keep the best score. If Wind Archer repeatedly trails the second team, the problem is probably investment rather than the formation itself.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="milky-way-team" title="Swap to the Milky Way team">

The second formation replaces Wind Archer with Milky Way Cookie. Macaron moves to slot 1 and Milky Way enters slot 7, matching the supplied setup. Every other Cookie stays the same, which makes this a clean comparison instead of a completely different experiment.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Milky Way Guild Conquest team"
  description="Use this version when Milky Way is built better than Wind Archer. It keeps the full Scorpion core, support package, and anti-lift setup intact."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0181", "cookie0040", "cookie0126", "cookie3001", "cookie4024", "cookie0573", "cookie0515", "cookie4010", "cookie0018", "cookie4019", "cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet4001", "pet0111", "pet0069"]}
/>

Wind Archer usually wins when both Cookies have comparable investment. Milky Way remains worth testing because a five-star SSR with finished Runes can beat an underbuilt TSSR on your account. Check the [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/) before investing, then let your own score decide this slot.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="cookie-jobs" title="Keep the damage core and support jobs intact">

Scorpion is the center of the damage plan. Five stars matters because her damage over time application becomes much more dependable. Build enough Focus to land it, then add Skill Haste, Skill Amp, and ATK Amp. An all-offense page can post a bigger lucky score, but missed applications make the results messy.

Rye is the burst option. Her five-star breakpoint adds the hits that make the short cooldown worth building around. Melon Soda brings another strong single-target cycle. If one is much weaker, that Cookie becomes the first slot to remove when Tea Knight arrives.

Macaron and Skating Queen are a pair. Macaron raises CRIT Chance, and Skating Queen turns those crits into larger numbers. CRIT Chance does not become dead after 100%. Chance above 100% can produce a double crit, and chance above 200% can produce a triple crit. That is why the formation keeps stacking CRIT instead of stopping at the usual cap.

Pomegranate grants Skill Amp Up. Tiger Lily helps the synergy package. Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician heals and raises ATK. Nameless Cake Hound reduces incoming damage, which prevents an unlucky hit from deleting a damage dealer before the next cast.

Pinot Noir supplies Lift Resistance. Her Healing Received Down does nothing useful to this boss, so build for Focus, Skill Haste, ATK Amp, and the resistance value you need. The full [Pinot Noir build](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-pinot-noir-cookie-build/) explains where that support fits outside this fight.

Dark Choco stays for DEF Down. Devil Cookie can fill the job on some accounts, but Dark Choco is the safer default here. Give him Focus and Skill Haste, plus enough defense to survive. Skill Amp no longer makes this stat debuff stronger.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="sugar-runes" title="Build Sugar Runes around each job">

Damage dealers share a simple starting point: ATK Amp, Skill Amp, and Skill Haste. Add Focus to Scorpion when the damage over time effect misses too often. Wind Archer and Milky Way can stay offensive because they are not carrying the main debuff check.

Supports need a little more judgment:

- Macaron, Pomegranate, Skating Queen, Tiger Lily, and Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician want Skill Haste and Skill Amp because their eligible buffs improve with better casts.
- Pinot Noir wants Focus, Skill Haste, and ATK Amp. Do not spend a fortune trying to improve Healing Received Down with Skill Amp.
- Dark Choco wants Focus and Skill Haste. Add HP or damage reduction if he dies early.
- Nameless Cake Hound wants Skill Haste and HP Amp so the defensive effect stays available.

Do not rebuild twelve Rune pages in one afternoon. Fix Scorpion first, then the weakest support that keeps dying, followed by the better of Rye and Melon Soda. Use the site's [recommended teams](/teams/) to see whether those same Cookies also earn a place in other modes before spending rare rerolls.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pet-loadout" title="Keep the three-Pet package together">

Use Holy Baby Drop, Hot Doggie, and Panda Dumpling in both formations. Holy Baby Drop raises allied ATK, and Hot Doggie supplies Skill Amp Up. Panda Dumpling completes the anti-lift package beside Pinot Noir, which helps the lineup keep attacking instead of losing casts to displacement.

Copy these three exactly before experimenting. Swapping Panda Dumpling for a prettier damage Pet can look stronger on paper, then lose more time when the formation gets lifted.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="brightseeker-tea-knight" title="Upgrade the team with Brightseeker and Tea Knight">

Brightseeker has the cleanest premium upgrade path because her Light damage matches the Dark boss. Even one copy can beat Wind Archer or Milky Way in this slot. Replace whichever of those two you were using, then keep the rest of the formation stable while you compare scores. The [Brightseeker build](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-brightseeker-cookie-build-team/) covers her offensive Rune priorities and five-star target.

Tea Knight is the next change. Keep Dark Choco. Remove the weaker of Rye and Melon Soda instead, then add Tea Knight for Boss DMG Up. This correction matters because dropping DEF Down can erase much of the gain you expected from the new Cookie.

<GuideTip title="Do not replace Dark Choco first">
Brightseeker takes the Wind Archer or Milky Way slot. Tea Knight takes the weaker Rye or Melon Soda slot. Dark Choco keeps applying DEF Down.
</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="retry-method" title="Use unlimited retries without wasting upgrade materials">

Save both presets and run each three to five times. Record the best result, not the average of two unlucky openings. If the score swings but nobody dies, the team probably needs more attempts rather than a rebuild. If the same Cookie dies early every time, fix that Rune page or add defense before changing the damage core.

Only change one variable between tests. Swap Wind Archer for Milky Way, run again, then compare. Later, add Brightseeker. When Tea Knight is ready, replace Rye or Melon Soda based on your account. Those extra minutes are cheaper than panic rerolling twelve Rune pages after one bad attempt.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="guild-conquest-faq" title="Guild Conquest team FAQ">

### What is the best CookieRun: Crumble Guild Conquest team without Brightseeker?

Use Wind Archer, Scorpion, Tiger Lily, Pomegranate, Melon Soda, Nameless Cake Hound, Macaron, Rye, Pinot Noir, Skating Queen, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, and Dark Choco. Replace Wind Archer with Milky Way if Milky Way has much better investment.

### Which Pets should I use against Extra-Stuffed Piñata?

Use Holy Baby Drop, Hot Doggie, and Panda Dumpling. The loadout adds ATK and Skill Amp while supporting the formation's resistance to lift effects.

### Is Wind Archer or Milky Way better for Guild Conquest?

Wind Archer has the higher result when both have similar investment. A promoted Milky Way with stronger Sugar Runes can still beat an underbuilt Wind Archer, so run both presets several times.

### Who should Brightseeker replace in Guild Conquest?

Brightseeker replaces Wind Archer or Milky Way. If you also add Tea Knight, replace the weaker of Rye and Melon Soda. Keep Dark Choco for DEF Down.

### Why does my Guild Conquest damage change between attempts?

Targeting, crits, debuff applications, and cast timing introduce variance. Entries are unlimited, so repeat a sound lineup several times and use its best score before spending more resources.

</GuideSection>

Brightseeker replaces Wind Archer or Milky Way. If you also add Tea Knight, replace the weaker of Rye and Melon Soda. Keep Dark Choco for DEF Down.
Why does my Guild Conquest damage change between attempts?
Targeting, crits, debuff applications, and cast timing introduce variance. Entries are unlimited, so repeat a sound lineup several times and use its best score before spending more resources.
