cookie-run-crumble-level-100-exp-priorit.text:
import { GuideSection } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Cookie EXP feels plentiful until you need several teams. Then you have to choose: finish a damage dealer's climb to level 100, catch up a healer, or give a fragile support enough levels to survive.

For a stage team that uses Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, give Milk the first level-100 push. Follow with the damage dealers you actually field, then your healer. The remaining slots can catch up as survival demands. Pomegranate can often wait longer than the others.

Levels also affect two less obvious things: who enters Crumble Dungeon early and who receives a Welfare effect aimed at your highest-ATK ally. That makes resetting a level useful, but only when you know which number you need to change.

<GuideSection id="exp-priority" title="Choose a working team before spending the EXP">

Late-game EXP shortages come from trying to maintain too many Cookies at once. A new stage team needs one set of units, Arena wants another, and suddenly every promising pull needs levels. You cannot solve that by treating each new Cookie as an urgent project.

Pick the lineup you are pushing with today. If you still need a workable composition, use the [recommended teams](/teams/) to settle the twelve slots before spreading more EXP. Then look at what fails: the team dies, the timer runs out, or an important support never survives long enough to cast.

For stage progression, use this order:

1. Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician.
2. The damage dealers doing the team's actual damage.
3. The healer you rely on, such as Herb.
4. Other active Cookies, raised enough to stay alive.
5. Pomegranate, if she already survives and delivers her buffs.

This order assumes those Cookies belong in your team. It is not a reason to pull Milk blindly or level an unused healer. The [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/) can help compare long-term investments, but a Cookie's rank alone does not tell you where the next batch of EXP should go.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="milk-first" title="Why Milk takes the first level-100 slot">

Milk gets several useful gains from the same level increase. His healing scales with his ATK, and his allied buff also depends on his own ATK. Higher levels raise that stat while adding HP and DEF to help him stay in the fight.

That combination puts him ahead of a support whose main contribution changes little with raw stats. Keeping Milk alive protects the team's healing, buffing, and synergy contribution at once. An underleveled Milk can leave several other expensive Cookies struggling.

Keep him at the top of the stage team's level spread while you work toward 100. After that, feed the carries. A healthy team still needs enough damage to beat the timer, so Milk taking first place does not mean the attackers should stay low indefinitely.

Pomegranate is the useful contrast. Her core buff does not gain the same benefit from raising her personal ATK. She still gains basic stats from levels, and those stats matter when she dies. But if she already survives the whole attempt, her next levels usually have less urgency than Milk's or a carry's.

There is no universal minimum level for her. Watch the fight. If she misses later casts because she falls over, move her back up the queue.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="arena-survival" title="In Arena, level the Cookie who dies first">

Arena starts with the same two priorities: Milk, then your working damage dealers. The third priority changes. Instead of automatically feeding Herb or another healer, check which teammate dies first.

That Cookie may need the HP and DEF from more levels. A support who survives to cast can do more for the result than a healer who receives another upgrade while the same teammate still disappears immediately.

Look for a repeated failure, not one awkward loss. If the same slot dies before contributing across several comparable fights, try raising it. If everyone survives and you still lose, go back to the damage dealers rather than adding levels to the healthiest support.

Make one adjustment at a time. Level changes are easier to judge when you keep the lineup and other equipment steady. You want to know whether extra survival bought another useful skill, not just whether the Power number increased.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="dungeon-entry" title="Crumble Dungeon uses Power for the initial 40">

The initial Crumble Dungeon roster shows 40 Cookie portraits. Their selection and entry priority follow individual Combat Power, from higher to lower. A Cookie you want early can sit behind a less useful one simply because its displayed Power is lower.

Levels give you a way to change that order. Resetting a level-100 Oven Wanderer lowers his Power. Raising a lower-rarity Cookie such as GingerBrave can put GingerBrave ahead of him and move GingerBrave into that initial group.

This example explains the sorting rule; it does not make GingerBrave an automatic best pick. Choose the Cookie for a job first, then adjust the numbers needed to bring it forward.

Check the entry display again after changing levels. Do not assume rarity decides the order, and do not confuse the initial 40 with a claim that only 40 Cookies can participate in the entire run. The practical check is whether the Cookie you intended to move now appears where you need it.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="welfare-atk" title="Make the highest-ATK Welfare effect reach Milk">

Combat Power controls that dungeon entry order. The Welfare effect discussed here checks a different number: the highest ATK among your allies. Making Milk the leader does not, by itself, guarantee that he receives it.

ATK Amp Sugar Runes can push Milk toward the top. But another attacker may still have more ATK, particularly if its levels and equipment are stronger. Compare the actual ATK values rather than the total Power or the size of the leader portrait.

Consider a setup where Milk displays about 582 ATK and an attacker displays over 600, using the same on-screen units. Resetting that attacker and rebuilding it to a lower level might bring its displayed ATK to about 575. Milk now sits above that attacker.

You are not finished if a second ally still displays 598. Check every competing Cookie. Leave a clear margin instead of trying to win a near tie at the last displayed decimal.

The [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) helps separate ATK Amp from other stats when you review those builds. Changing a stat that sounds offensive will not necessarily change which ally has the highest ATK.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="reset-tradeoffs" title="Do not sacrifice the whole team to win one ATK check">

Lowering a carry's level also lowers the carry's stats. Getting the Welfare effect onto Milk can improve his contribution, but that gain has to outweigh what the attacker loses. A cleaner ATK ranking can still produce a worse run.

Record the original levels and ATK values before resetting anything. Read the reset confirmation, including its costs and what it returns. Then rebuild in small steps and stop below Milk's ATK if that is the goal.

Try the same content again. Check whether Milk's improved contribution helps the team survive or deal more damage overall. If the run gets worse, revisit the setup instead of lowering every attacker further.

This option matters most when you have a limited Rune budget. Chasing enough ATK Amp rolls to beat every carry can get expensive. A measured level adjustment gives you another approach, but neither approach deserves unlimited spending.

Keep the investment tied to a team you use now. Your preferred lineup may change later, and a costly set of Milk-specific rolls may not remain your account's next priority.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="next-exp-batch" title="Give the next batch of EXP a specific job">

Before spending the next batch, check Milk and the active carries first. After that, look for a teammate who dies too early. Only start adjusting dungeon entry or Welfare targeting when you have a specific Cookie and a specific number in mind.

Keep enough flexibility for the mode you are actually trying to clear. You can leave a stable support lower, raise a fragile Arena slot, or hold back a carry while testing Welfare targeting. For the broader daily routine around those upgrades, the [fast account growth guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-fast-account-growth-guide/) covers the order of stage pushes, dungeon attempts, and permanent account gains.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="level-100-faq" title="Cookie EXP and level-100 FAQ">

### Who should reach level 100 first?

For a stage team using Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, prioritize Milk, then your active damage dealers, then your healer. Raise other supports when they need more survival.

### Does Pomegranate need level 100?

Not immediately if she survives and delivers her buffs. Her core buff does not benefit from personal ATK in the same way Milk's does, so other active Cookies can take priority.

### Can levels change Crumble Dungeon entry order?

Yes. Levels change individual Combat Power, which determines the initial 40-Cookie selection and entry priority. Recheck the entry display after adjusting the roster.

### Will choosing Milk as leader guarantee the Welfare buff?

No. The Welfare effect that targets the highest-ATK ally still checks ATK. Milk must exceed the other relevant allies, and lowering their levels can cost damage.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-pinot-noir-cookie-bui.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Pinot Noir Cookie gives Multi-strike teams something they have been missing: a provider who can make enemy healing worse instead of adding another buff that gets overwritten. That matters most in PvP, where a fight can look won until four healers drag every health bar back up.

The pull is appealing, but the build needs restraint. Pinot Noir does not need a pile of damage stats, and a free account does not need ten stars on day one. Build the support effect first, reach the five-star breakpoint when the budget allows it, then let future standard pulls handle the long promotion grind.

<GuideSection id="why-pinot-noir-matters" title="Why Pinot Noir changes healer matchups">

Pinot Noir grants Multi-strike and applies Healing Received Down. The combination is awkward for defensive teams in the best possible way. Your attackers receive their synergy while the opposing healers get less value from every recovery cast.

The anti-heal effect lasts five seconds and returns fast enough to cover most of a fight. That is much better than a tiny burst window that disappears before your damage Cookies cast. Against a team carrying four or five healers, even one reduced recovery cycle can leave a target low enough for Rye Cookie or Melon Soda Cookie to finish.

Pinot Noir also brings Knock-up Resistance Up. It protects the lineup from displacement and control during boss attacks, and it makes PvP openers less likely to scramble the team before its skills begin cycling. This does not make every team immortal. It does give a fragile Multi-strike core more time to do its job.

<GuideTip title="Do not judge Pinot Noir by personal damage">

Check whether enemy health stays down and whether your Multi-strike receivers cast cleanly. A support can decide the fight while sitting near the bottom of the damage screen.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="five-star-breakpoint" title="Five stars is the sensible first target">

At five stars, Pinot Noir grants two Multi-strike points instead of one and improves the healing reduction. That extra synergy point matters because it makes a full Multi-strike core easier to activate without twisting the rest of the lineup around one provider.

Five stars is a strong stopping point, not a demand to empty the account immediately. Pinot Noir remains in the standard pool, so regular Cookie Cutters can add copies later. Ten stars may improve a support you use everywhere, but forcing it during one pickup banner is a huge cost. Those crystals could secure the next limited Cookie or fix several unfinished members of the main team.

New players have a different problem. If Scorpion, Rye, or Macaron still needs an important five-star promotion, regular pulls still have value today. A roster that is roughly a month old and already has its core promotions can afford to save regular Cookie Cutters until a new Cookie enters the standard pool.

Before chasing extra copies, check Pinot Noir's current placement on the [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/). A promotion is easier to justify when the Cookie still solves the modes your account plays most.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="best-sugar-rune-stats" title="Do not roll Skill Amp for stronger anti-heal">

Pinot Noir's Healing Received Down and Knock-up Resistance Up both ignore Skill Amp. Do not reroll for Skill Amp to strengthen either effect. Use Focus when enemy Resistance blocks the debuff, and consider Accuracy when attacks miss.

Skill Haste looks tempting until you compare the timers. The resistance effect can last about ten seconds on a roughly 9.5-second cycle. The healing reduction lasts five seconds while its skill cycles in about 3.25 seconds. Both already have generous coverage, so compare more Haste with a stat that fixes missed attacks or resisted debuffs.

Focus can help when a boss resists the anti-heal. Accuracy is a situational alternative if attacks fail to connect, though it is rarely the first PvP target. Use the stat the fight asks for and stop rerolling once the set does its job; Skill Amp does not strengthen the resistance effect. The [Skill Amp fix and Rune refund guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-skill-amp-fix-rune-refund/) explains the restriction, while the [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) has a budget plan for locks and rerolls.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="multi-strike-teammates" title="Choose receivers that use the extra attacks">

Pinot Noir replaces the old habit of reaching automatically for Orange Cookie or Grapevine whenever a team needs Multi-strike. Orange still gives CRIT support, and Grapevine still heals, but Pinot Noir brings the anti-heal effect that neither one covers.

Rye Cookie is a clean damage partner after five stars. Her short cooldown lets her punish the health that enemy healers fail to restore. Melon Soda Cookie gives the core broader pressure. Macaron Cookie receives Multi-strike and contributes CRIT Chance Up, while Herb Cookie turns the pet's ATK bonus into stronger healing. Space Doughnut's Royal Excellence also receives Multi-strike and fits aggressive PvP formations.

Do not cram every receiver into the same preset. Start with Pinot Noir, two or three receivers, a frontline, and enough sustain to reach the second skill cycle. The rest depends on the mode. Browse the tested [CookieRun: Crumble Teams](/teams/) before copying a greedy damage shell into a boss fight that needs two defenders.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="chargemellow-pet" title="Chargemellow completes the Multi-strike core">

Chargemellow adds one Multi-strike synergy point and gives ATK to allies receiving that synergy. The pet therefore does two jobs at once: it helps activate the setup and rewards the Cookies already built around it.

That ATK is useful on Rye and Melon Soda, but Herb also deserves attention because healing scales with ATK. A three-star Chargemellow can already earn a slot when the extra synergy point completes the formation. Do not compare the pet only by rarity or raw Power. Check whether removing it breaks the active synergy and lowers several Cookies at once.

Use the [Pets list](/pets/) to compare Chargemellow with elemental damage or CRIT options. If Multi-strike is already comfortably active, another pet may solve the stage better.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pull-plan" title="Use a pull plan instead of chasing the lucky run">

Regular Cookie Cutters become more useful when a fresh SSR joins the standard pool. Saving them for a roster update gives every pull a chance to produce the new Cookie while still adding older copies. Spending them randomly between updates removes that timing advantage.

Diamonds and premium cutters should be treated differently. Keep them for limited or pickup banners where the target and milestones justify the cost. Once Pinot Noir reaches five stars, stopping is reasonable. Standard pulls can continue the promotion later, and the account keeps enough currency for whatever lands next.

Luck can make a short stash look brilliant, but it is not a plan. Set a promotion target before pulling, turn off automatic pulls when you are close, and stop when the target is complete. The extra copy after five stars feels good for ten seconds. Running out of diamonds on the next banner feels bad for much longer.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="mistakes-to-avoid" title="Avoid the expensive Pinot Noir mistakes">

- Do not build ATK and CRIT as if Pinot Noir were the team's carry.
- Do not force Skill Haste when the important effects already overlap their cooldowns.
- Do not rush ten stars while the main damage Cookies still lack their promotion breakpoints.
- Do not slot every Multi-strike receiver and leave the team without a frontline.
- Do not spend all premium currency after reaching the five-star synergy upgrade.

The most common mistake is simpler: players see a new SSR, max everything, then test it in a random preset. Pinot Noir needs receivers who benefit from Multi-strike and opponents whose healing or control makes the support package matter.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="quick-build" title="Quick Pinot Noir build">

1. Aim for five stars to reach two Multi-strike points and stronger Healing Received Down.
2. Do not roll Skill Amp for anti-heal or Knock-up Resistance Up. Use Focus against resistant bosses.
3. Pair Pinot Noir with Rye, Melon Soda, Macaron, Herb, or Space Doughnut's Royal Excellence.
4. Use Chargemellow when its extra synergy point completes the core.
5. Save premium currency after the five-star target and collect later copies from standard pulls.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pinot-noir-faq" title="Pinot Noir Cookie FAQ">

### Is Pinot Noir Cookie worth pulling?

Pinot Noir is a strong target for Multi-strike and PvP accounts because the kit combines a synergy grant with Healing Received Down and Knock-up Resistance Up. Accounts that still lack basic five-star damage dealers should fix those promotion gaps before chasing a luxury ten-star support.

### What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Pinot Noir Cookie?

Healing Received Down and Knock-up Resistance Up both ignore Skill Amp. Focus helps against resistant bosses, and Accuracy has occasional use when attacks miss. Skill Haste is less urgent because the important effects already overlap their cooldowns.

### Does Pinot Noir need five stars?

Five stars is the best first stopping point. It raises the Multi-strike grant to two points and improves the healing reduction. Pinot Noir works earlier, but that promotion makes team building much easier.

### Who works well with Pinot Noir Cookie?

Rye, Melon Soda, Macaron, Herb, and Space Doughnut's Royal Excellence all receive Multi-strike. Pick two or three that fit the mode, then add frontline and healing instead of filling every slot with damage.

### Is Chargemellow worth using with Pinot Noir?

Yes, when the pet's extra Multi-strike point activates the core. Chargemellow also raises ATK for synergy receivers, which helps damage dealers and improves Herb Cookie's healing.

</GuideSection>

segments.text: Chargemellow adds one Multi-strike synergy point and gives ATK to allies receiving that synergy. The pet therefore does two jobs at once: it helps activate the setup and rewards the Cookies already built around it.

That ATK is useful on Rye and Melon Soda, but Herb also deserves attention because healing scales with ATK. A three-star Chargemellow can already earn a slot when the extra synergy point completes the formation. Do not compare the pet only by rarity or raw Power. Check whether removing it breaks the active synergy and lowers several Cookies at once.
Use the
Pets list
to compare Chargemellow with elemental damage or CRIT options. If Multi-strike is already comfortably active, another pet may solve the stage better.
Chargemellow completes the Multi-strike core
segments.name: title

segments.text: Regular Cookie Cutters become more useful when a fresh SSR joins the standard pool. Saving them for a roster update gives every pull a chance to produce the new Cookie while still adding older copies. Spending them randomly between updates removes that timing advantage.

Diamonds and premium cutters should be treated differently. Keep them for limited or pickup banners where the target and milestones justify the cost. Once Pinot Noir reaches five stars, stopping is reasonable. Standard pulls can continue the promotion later, and the account keeps enough currency for whatever lands next.

Luck can make a short stash look brilliant, but it is not a plan. Set a promotion target before pulling, turn off automatic pulls when you are close, and stop when the target is complete. The extra copy after five stars feels good for ten seconds. Running out of diamonds on the next banner feels bad for much longer.
Use a pull plan instead of chasing the lucky run
segments.name: title

segments.text: Do not build ATK and CRIT as if Pinot Noir were the team's carry.
Do not force Skill Haste when the important effects already overlap their cooldowns.
Do not rush ten stars while the main damage Cookies still lack their promotion breakpoints.
Do not slot every Multi-strike receiver and leave the team without a frontline.
Do not spend all premium currency after reaching the five-star synergy upgrade.

The most common mistake is simpler: players see a new SSR, max everything, then test it in a random preset. Pinot Noir needs receivers who benefit from Multi-strike and opponents whose healing or control makes the support package matter.
Avoid the expensive Pinot Noir mistakes
segments.name: title

segments.text: Aim for five stars to reach two Multi-strike points and stronger Healing Received Down.
Do not roll Skill Amp for anti-heal or Knock-up Resistance Up. Use Focus against resistant bosses.
Pair Pinot Noir with Rye, Melon Soda, Macaron, Herb, or Space Doughnut's Royal Excellence.
Use Chargemellow when its extra synergy point completes the core.
Save premium currency after the five-star target and collect later copies from standard pulls.
Quick Pinot Noir build
segments.name: title

segments.text: Is Pinot Noir Cookie worth pulling?

Pinot Noir is a strong target for Multi-strike and PvP accounts because the kit combines a synergy grant with Healing Received Down and Knock-up Resistance Up. Accounts that still lack basic five-star damage dealers should fix those promotion gaps before chasing a luxury ten-star support.
What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Pinot Noir Cookie?

Healing Received Down and Knock-up Resistance Up both ignore Skill Amp. Focus helps against resistant bosses, and Accuracy has occasional use when attacks miss. Skill Haste is less urgent because the important effects already overlap their cooldowns.
Does Pinot Noir need five stars?

Five stars is the best first stopping point. It raises the Multi-strike grant to two points and improves the healing reduction. Pinot Noir works earlier, but that promotion makes team building much easier.
Who works well with Pinot Noir Cookie?

Rye, Melon Soda, Macaron, Herb, and Space Doughnut's Royal Excellence all receive Multi-strike. Pick two or three that fit the mode, then add frontline and healing instead of filling every slot with damage.
Is Chargemellow worth using with Pinot Noir?
Yes, when the pet's extra Multi-strike point activates the core. Chargemellow also raises ATK for synergy receivers, which helps damage dealers and improves Herb Cookie's healing.
Pinot Noir Cookie FAQ

cookie-run-crumble-pinot-noir-multistrik.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

You copied a strong Pinot Noir team, hit Start, and watched the boss flatten it anyway. That does not mean the lineup is fake. It means a twelve-Cookie formation is not a magic password.

Promotion, Sugar Runes, Pet levels, research, and total Power all change how the same team behaves. One account survives with a single healer. Another loses a frontline Cookie before the first clean damage cycle. The useful skill is not memorizing one screenshot. It is knowing whether your account should lean into Multi-strike, Scorpion, or a safer mix of both.

The two complete teams below give you a starting point. Use the Multi-strike team as the general recommendation. Move to the Scorpion team when a boss needs stronger damage over time, Duration support, or better protection from knock-up.

<GuideSection id="why-copied-teams-fail" title="Find out why the copied team fails on your account">

Start with the failure, not the roster. If the team dies early, more damage will not fix it. If everyone lives but the boss barely moves, another healer will only make the loss take longer. Watch the first 20 seconds and put the run into one of three buckets:

- A Cookie dies before the second skill cycle.
- The team survives, but the boss HP falls too slowly.
- Damage starts slowly, then accelerates once repeated hits and debuffs overlap.

The third result is normal for Multi-strike. Its opening can look unimpressive before the repeated attacks line up. Do not rebuild the team five seconds into the test. Give it a full attempt, then compare two or three runs.

Raw Power still matters in story. A clever formation can lose when its Power sits far below the stage recommendation. Check the [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/) before funding a replacement, but remember that a finished SSR can beat a new premium Cookie with poor promotion and unfinished Runes.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="choose-team-path" title="Choose Multi-strike or Scorpion before changing slots">

The Multi-strike path is the better default for a developed Pinot Noir. Pinot grants the synergy, Chargemellow adds another point, and several Cookies in the formation benefit from the repeated-hit package. The damage often ramps instead of exploding immediately.

The Scorpion path trades some of that broad pressure for a clearer boss plan. Scorpion wants Multi-shot and Duration support, while Octo Wasabi supplies Duration. This version also keeps more defensive tools, so it is easier to tune when a hammer, snowman, or tornado-like attack keeps tossing the team into the air.

Do not blend the two plans at random. Pick one, save it as a preset, and test it intact. The [recommended teams page](/teams/) is useful for comparing complete formations without turning every failed run into twelve simultaneous swaps.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="multistrike-team" title="Start with the Pinot Noir Multi-strike team">

This is the team to build first. Wind Archer and Brightseeker add serious damage, while Melon Soda and Rye keep pressure on priority targets. Macaron raises CRIT Chance, Skating Queen improves CRIT damage, and Pomegranate brings Skill Amp Up. Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician and Herb cover healing. Nameless Cake Hound cuts incoming damage, while Dark Choco handles DEF Down.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Pinot Noir Multi-strike boss team"
  description="Use this as the general boss preset. Pinot Noir and Chargemellow complete the Multi-strike package while two healers, Nameless Cake Hound, and Dark Choco keep the damage cycle stable."
  cookieIds={["cookie0070", "cookie4013", "cookie3001", "cookie0126", "cookie4019", "cookie0063", "cookie0059", "cookie0515", "cookie4010", "cookie0018", "cookie4024", "cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet0069", "pet4005", "pet4001"]}
/>

Use Panda Dumpling, Chargemellow, and Holy Baby Drop in that order. Chargemellow is not a decorative stat stick here. Removing it can break the reason several Cookies were selected. Holy Baby Drop raises team ATK, and Panda Dumpling helps the anti-lift package beside Pinot Noir.

If Herb feels unnecessary because Milk is highly promoted and well built, Herb becomes a flexible slot. Replace him with your strongest trained damage dealer, not automatically the rarest Cookie. Brightseeker is a clean option when built. Milky Way or Oven Wanderer can win on an account where their promotion and Power are much higher.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="scorpion-team" title="Use the Scorpion team for stubborn bosses">

Switch to this version when Scorpion's damage over time is the better answer or when knock-up keeps stealing skill casts. The formation keeps Pinot Noir, then adds Octo Wasabi for Duration. Tiger Lily supports Multi-shot, and Ion Cookie Robot gives the frontline breathing room.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Scorpion anti-knock-up boss team"
  description="Use this safer Scorpion preset when displacement or incoming damage breaks the run. Octo Wasabi supports Duration, while Ion, Herb, Milk, Nameless Cake Hound, and GingerBright reduce the chance of an early collapse."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie4010", "cookie0018", "cookie4019", "cookie0136", "cookie0063", "cookie0181", "cookie0126", "cookie0040", "cookie4024", "cookie4006", "cookie0003"]}
  petIds={["pet0069", "pet0110", "pet4001"]}
/>

Multiple Multi-shot providers do not stack identical buffs into one giant number. The strongest active version applies. Keeping more than one provider still helps because their skill windows do not start and end together. You are buying uptime, not a secret double bonus.

Ion is the first safety valve. If nobody is in danger, replace Ion with a damage dealer. If the team remains fragile, keep Ion and inspect the Cookie that dies first. One sensible defensive Rune line is cheaper than replacing half the formation.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="fix-boss-control" title="Stop knock-up from deleting your damage window">

Hammer attacks, snowman hits, and Cool Mint-style tornado effects can lift Cookies at the exact moment they should cast. The lost time looks like weak damage even when your offensive stats are fine.

Pinot Noir raises knock-up resistance, and Panda Dumpling strengthens that job. Together they can turn a long airborne interruption into a brief bump. The Cookie lands faster, keeps formation, and gets back to casting. Against a boss built around displacement, that practical uptime can beat a greedier Pet loadout.

Do not remove both anti-lift pieces for ATK just because the Power number turns green. If the boss controls the team again, you traded real actions for prettier arithmetic. The detailed [Pinot Noir build](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-pinot-noir-cookie-build/) explains which Rune stats help her keep this support role reliable.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="swap-rules" title="Change one slot according to the actual problem">

When the team survives but lacks damage, cut a defensive slot before cutting a synergy provider. Ion is the obvious first test in the Scorpion setup. Herb can leave the Multi-strike setup when Milk already supplies enough healing. Add Brightseeker, Milky Way, Oven Wanderer, or another finished carry based on promotion and Rune quality.

When HP swings wildly, reverse that logic. Restore Ion, keep Herb, or use a defensive Pet. Majestic King Choco Drop helps accounts that own and level it. A more accessible damage reduction option can do the same job less elegantly. Elegant is overrated when the boss is chewing on slot four.

Dark Choco is usually safer than Devil for DEF Down. A promoted Dark Choco can maintain useful stacks and has a much better chance of staying alive. Test Devil only when the team already survives and the boss needs a sharper debuff window.

<GuideTip title="The one-change rule">
Save the original preset. Change one Cookie or one Pet, then run it twice. If you change four pieces together, even a win teaches you almost nothing.
</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rune-priorities" title="Spend Sugar Runes on Cookies that keep returning">

Pomegranate, Milk, Scorpion, Macaron, and a promoted Dark Choco deserve attention because they appear across many teams. Finish the Cookies that solve several modes before polishing a niche substitute.

Scorpion wants enough Focus to land the important effect, then offensive stats and Skill Haste. Pomegranate, Macaron, and Milk value Skill Haste and eligible Skill Amp. Dark Choco needs Focus and Skill Haste, plus enough HP or damage reduction to finish the fight. Your main attackers want ATK Amp, CRIT stats, and Skill Amp.

Do not chase a perfect page while eleven teammates wear leftovers. The [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) gives a safer order for locks and rerolls. A good spread across the full team usually beats one glorious carry surrounded by cardboard.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="hybrid-team" title="Build a hybrid only when late progression demands it">

Around the middle of the 220s and beyond, a pure Multi-strike setup can stop gaining enough damage. That is where a hybrid becomes useful. Keep the stable support core, then add Scorpion plus Multi-shot providers. Choose the third Pet according to the direction you want: Hot Doggie for a neutral Skill Amp option, Octo Wasabi for a stronger Scorpion lean, or Chargemellow for more Multi-strike pressure.

The final slots answer the run. Add Ion when the formation breaks. Add a trained attacker when survival is comfortable. Use GingerBright when ATK Down matters, or another healer when the health bars refuse to settle. Strawberry Crepe can join a Multi-strike-leaning hybrid, but only after the account bonus for three Defense Cookies makes the frontline less flimsy. Before that breakpoint, Strawberry Crepe has an alarming habit of becoming a very expensive floor decoration.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pinot-team-faq" title="Pinot Noir team FAQ">

### Which Pinot Noir team should I build first?

Start with the Multi-strike team. It has the broader damage package and works as the better general boss preset. Use the Scorpion team when damage over time, Duration support, or anti-knock-up stability matters more.

### Why does Multi-strike damage look low at the start?

Its repeated attacks, buffs, and debuffs need time to overlap. The boss HP can move slowly at first, then fall much faster once the full cycle starts. Judge the completed attempt, not the opening seconds.

### Do multiple Multi-shot providers stack their buffs?

No. The strongest identical active synergy applies. Multiple providers still improve uptime because each Cookie activates the effect during a different skill window.

### Should I use Dark Choco or Devil Cookie for DEF Down?

Use a well-promoted Dark Choco as the safe default. Try Devil only when the team survives comfortably and needs a stronger short damage window.

### When should I remove Herb Cookie?

Remove Herb only when Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician already keeps the team healthy. If a Cookie dies before the next skill cycle, Herb was not the problem.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-power-guide-stage-dam.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

A boss can survive with a sliver of health even when your rotation looks clean. You retry, move a Cookie, swap one support, and still lose to the same timer. Then you claim a day of rewards, buy a few small upgrades, and the fight suddenly looks easy.

That jump is not always the extra ATK printed on the upgrade. Story stages compare your team's Power with the stage's Recommended Power. Falling below it can reduce the damage your lineup deals. A small account upgrade may push the team into a better damage band, which is why a routine Resolve node can feel stronger than its stat line suggests.

<GuideSection id="why-power-walls-happen" title="Why a stage wall can appear overnight">

Hard bosses still care about mechanics. Rowdy Bikers rewards wide attacks because its targets split apart, while a single boss usually favors focused damage. Power sits underneath that matchup. Bring the right team too far below the stage requirement and the game can cut its output before your good composition gets a fair attempt.

Claiming a day of Auto Hunt rewards can change the fight even when the lineup stays fixed. Levels, Resolve, research, gear, and promotions raise the total together.

Do not treat every failed run as proof that twelve Cookies are wrong. First check whether the team is close on damage, badly under the Recommended Power, or dying to a mechanic. Those are three different problems.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="read-the-damage-penalty" title="Read Recommended Power as a damage check">

The game does not show the full damage curve in the stage screen, so the exact percentages should be treated as working estimates. The useful pattern is clear: being far under the requirement can cut damage much harder than the visible Power gap suggests.

Stage 10-1 provides a simple example. Its Recommended Power is about 135,000. At roughly 13,000 Power, or 10% of that target, the estimated output is only about 1% of normal damage. At 20% of the target, the estimate rises to roughly 15%. The curve is not a clean one-for-one ratio.

Going above the recommendation may also raise damage beyond the normal baseline. The observed estimate tops out near 120%, but there is no reason to overbuild every old stage just to chase that bonus. Your goal is a reliable clear, not bullying a chapter you already finished.

<GuideTip title="Use the numbers as a diagnosis">

The exact percentage matters less than the direction. If a healthy team times out while sitting well below Recommended Power, raise the total before rewriting the whole formation.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="stage-35-10-example" title="What the 35-10 wall looks like">

Stage 35-10 asks for about 4.2 million Power. A lineup around 3.3 to 3.4 million sits near 80% of the recommendation, and the working estimate puts its damage around 75% of normal. That is enough to make a good team look strangely weak.

Suppose the boss survives with 10% health. Replacing the entire lineup may introduce worse synergies and lower levels. Raising the same team by a few hundred thousand Power can be the cleaner fix because it improves the stage multiplier while keeping the rotation that almost worked.

Claim the idle rewards, level the active twelve, buy an affordable Resolve node, and try again. A sharp change after those modest upgrades usually points to a better Power band, not a secret build.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="team-versus-power" title="Keep the team, then test the Power gap">

Raw Power cannot turn the wrong damage type into the right one. An AoE roster can still stall against a strict single-target timer, and a boss team can waste too much time on split waves. Start with a formation built for the fight. The [recommended Teams](/teams/) page covers story, boss, F2P, and farming setups, while the [Tier List](/tier-list/) helps decide which Cookies deserve scarce levels and promotions.

Once the basic matchup is correct, compare the Power gap. A higher-Power Cookie can be worth a temporary slot when the team is just below a useful threshold. Check what you lose before confirming the swap. Breaking Multi-strike, Duration, healing, or the only defensive slot can cost more than the extra number gives back.

Use the [Team Builder](/tools/team-builder/) to lay out all twelve positions and three Pets before spending materials. It is much cheaper to spot a missing synergy there than after upgrading a replacement Cookie.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="cheap-power-upgrades" title="Cross the next breakpoint without wasting materials">

Start with upgrades that help the whole active lineup or cost very little:

1. Claim Auto Hunt and quest rewards before testing the wall again.
2. Bring the twelve Cookies you use to the current practical level cap.
3. Spend cheap Resolve coins, with ATK first when the timer is the problem.
4. Finish short Gnome Laboratory nodes instead of saving every material for one expensive project.
5. Equip unused higher-Power gear long enough to test whether the stage multiplier changes.
6. Promote Cookies when the next star adds a real skill upgrade or a large stat jump.

Resolve is easy to underestimate. A node may add only a small amount of ATK to each Cookie, yet it also raises the team total. Cheap research works the same way. Finish the short upgrades, clear more stages, and let the new rewards fund the slow project.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="gear-power-tradeoff" title="Use high-Power gear without worshipping the green arrow">

Equipment stats do not contribute equally to displayed Power. Accuracy can add a surprisingly large amount, so an Accuracy-heavy piece may push the lineup across a stage threshold even when that Cookie does not need more Accuracy for the fight.

That does not make the piece universally better. Under a harsh stage penalty, the higher total may win because it restores part of your damage. After the team reaches a workable multiplier, ATK, CRIT, Skill Amp, Skill Haste, Focus, or defensive stats may produce the cleaner clear. Test the fight instead of letting one green arrow make the decision.

The [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) explains the broader stat tradeoffs. If skills miss or debuffs fail after Power is high enough, use the [Accuracy and Focus guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-accuracy-focus-guide/) to fix that separate check.

PvP should be judged on its own results. The stage penalty discussed here is a PvE progression issue. Do not gut a working Arena build simply because another piece displays more Power.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="f2p-power-walls" title="Plan around the F2P slowdown">

Free accounts will feel the gap more as stage requirements climb. Paid memberships speed up AFK income and add dungeon attempts, so falling away from an early leaderboard position does not mean your account is broken.

Plan around daily progress instead. Free summons will fill more of the roster, duplicate copies will improve promotions, and some SR Cookies become excellent at five stars. The [beginner progression guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-beginner-progression-guide/) has a daily route for turning idle rewards into permanent account gains.

If a wall lasts one evening, that is normal. If it lasts several days, check the failure instead of waiting blindly. A timer loss, a dead frontline, and a resisted debuff need different fixes.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="power-failure-checklist" title="Use this checklist before the next retry">

- The team survives but times out: compare your Power with the recommendation and add focused damage.
- The boss ends below 10% health: chase the cheapest nearby Power breakpoint before changing the core.
- The frontline dies early: add defense, healing, or a better position. More damage will not protect a dead carry.
- Important skills miss: check Accuracy. If debuffs land inconsistently, check Focus.
- Split targets waste your attacks: switch to an AoE formation.
- One boss absorbs everything: replace broad wave damage with single-target pressure.

Run one controlled test after each change. Swapping four Cookies, three Pets, and half the gear at once only tells you that something changed. It does not tell you which upgrade solved the stage.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="power-guide-faq" title="CookieRun: Crumble Power FAQ">

### Does Power reduce my damage in story stages?

Falling below a stage's Recommended Power can reduce the damage your lineup deals. The exact curve is not shown clearly in-game, so use combat results and the size of the Power gap as your diagnosis.

### Should I choose Power or a better team composition?

Use the right composition first, then raise its Power. Boss mechanics still decide whether you need AoE, single-target damage, healing, or defense. Power helps that team operate without a severe stage penalty.

### Why did a tiny Resolve upgrade make the boss much easier?

The Resolve stats helped, but the extra team Power may also have crossed a better damage band. That can make a small upgrade feel much larger than the printed ATK increase.

### Is Accuracy gear worth using only for Power?

It can be worth a temporary test when you are just below a stage threshold. Once the team reaches a workable multiplier, compare the actual clear and return to stats that fit the Cookie if the Accuracy is unnecessary.

### Can F2P players get past late Power walls?

Yes, but the pace slows. Claim idle rewards, push dungeon first clears, finish cheap research, spend Resolve, and promote the main lineup. Treat a short wall as an account-building day rather than a reason to empty every resource into one Cookie.

</GuideSection>

That jump is not always the extra ATK printed on the upgrade. Story stages compare your team's Power with the stage's Recommended Power. Falling below it can reduce the damage your lineup deals. A small account upgrade may push the team into a better damage band, which is why a routine Resolve node can feel stronger than its stat line suggests.

Hard bosses still care about mechanics. Rowdy Bikers rewards wide attacks because its targets split apart, while a single boss usually favors focused damage. Power sits underneath that matchup. Bring the right team too far below the stage requirement and the game can cut its output before your good composition gets a fair attempt.

segments.text: The game does not show the full damage curve in the stage screen, so the exact percentages should be treated as working estimates. The useful pattern is clear: being far under the requirement can cut damage much harder than the visible Power gap suggests.

Stage 10-1 provides a simple example. Its Recommended Power is about 135,000. At roughly 13,000 Power, or 10% of that target, the estimated output is only about 1% of normal damage. At 20% of the target, the estimate rises to roughly 15%. The curve is not a clean one-for-one ratio.

Going above the recommendation may also raise damage beyond the normal baseline. The observed estimate tops out near 120%, but there is no reason to overbuild every old stage just to chase that bonus. Your goal is a reliable clear, not bullying a chapter you already finished.
The exact percentage matters less than the direction. If a healthy team times out while sitting well below Recommended Power, raise the total before rewriting the whole formation.

Claim Auto Hunt and quest rewards before testing the wall again.

cookie-run-crumble-princess-bari-cookie-.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Your Charge Cookies reach the enemy damage dealer, swing once, and disappear. The rest of your team follows them a few seconds later. Princess Bari Cookie helps with that opening, but putting her in the lineup does not make every dive safe.

**For story, build enough survival to keep Bari working, then favor useful offensive rolls. For Arena, start with Damage Reduction and ATK Amp.** Keep strong Skill Haste or Skill Amp rolls too. Her protective buffs do not scale with Skill Amp, but her damage still benefits from it.

Copying a strong roster can get expensive when you cannot tell what went wrong. Here is a complete story formation, the two Herb swaps worth trying, and a way to tell whether your next upgrade should help Bari survive or finish her target.

<GuideSection id="bari-charge-protection" title="What Princess Bari actually fixes">

Princess Bari is a Fire Charge Cookie with TSSR rarity. She attacks with her branch weapon, provides Charge allies with damage reduction and immunity to knock-up and knockback, and rushes an enemy with high ATK to deal damage.

Those protections address a familiar problem. A Charge Cookie needs to reach a useful target and keep attacking. Getting lifted or pushed around wastes that opportunity. Bari helps the Charge group stay involved while reducing the punishment it takes.

Oven Wanderer Cookie makes sense beside her in Arena for that reason. Bari helps Wanderer keep attacking after the dive. That pairing does not mean Wanderer received another direct buff, or that every team should replace its current damage dealer with him.

She also works in story without a whole squad built around charging. Cherry Cola is a useful partner there, but Bari can contribute without Cherry Cola occupying another slot. Use the [Cookie tier list](/tier-list/) to compare investment options across your roster before spending on a second attacker just to complete a pairing.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-story-team" title="A complete Princess Bari story team">

This preset uses 12 Cookies and three Pets. Read the first row from left to right, then the second row. The numbered portraits below follow that order.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Princess Bari story progression team"
  description="Twelve Cookies in row order, with Hot Doggie, Chargemellow, and Holy Baby Drop. Try Herb in place of Strawberry Crepe or Scorpion if allies keep dying."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059","cookie0181","cookie0037","cookie0018","cookie4019","cookie0518","cookie4013","cookie4010","cookie0126","cookie0081","cookie4024","cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet0111","pet4005","pet4001"]}
/>

* **First row:** Macaron, Scorpion, Cheesecake, Skating Queen, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, and Strawberry Crepe.
* **Second row:** Brightseeker, Pinot Noir, Pomegranate, Princess Bari, Nameless Cake Hound, and Dark Choco.
* **Pets:** Hot Doggie, Chargemellow, and Holy Baby Drop. All three Pets in this setup are level 20.

Scorpion occupies the red-haired slot in the first row. Cherry Cola is not part of this particular preset. If you want to try Cherry Cola alongside Bari, treat that as a separate change to this lineup.

The Pet choices support damage through Skill Amp, Multi-strike support, and ATK. Keep their levels in mind when comparing results with your own account. Matching three icons does not reproduce the same investment.

You can also find this formation on the [Teams page](/teams/). Start with its full lineup so you have a clear comparison, then change the slot that addresses your failed run. Replacing four Cookies at once makes it much harder to tell which swap helped.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-herb-swaps" title="When to bring Herb instead">

This formation leaves out a dedicated Herb slot. It still includes Milk, so treating it as a team with no healing would give the wrong impression. A developed roster can get through many fights this way; a weaker account may lose Cookies before its damage gets going.

If that happens, try **Herb in Strawberry Crepe's slot**. This gives you a straightforward survival adjustment while retaining Scorpion. Run the same stage again and check whether the extra healing lets your damage dealers stay active long enough to finish.

The other option is **Herb in Scorpion's slot**. Choose between those swaps by looking at the fight. Scorpion's poison can supply useful extra damage against a single boss. Removing Scorpion when the boss already survives with a sliver of health may solve one problem and create another.

Neither substitution is a promise that a low-Power team can copy a developed roster's results. Story progression still asks you to raise account strength. Use the preset while you continue those upgrades.

Also keep the easier story difficulty in perspective. Faster clears after adding Bari can reflect both her contribution and reduced stage difficulty. A smoother run is welcome. It does not prove that one Cookie caused the entire improvement.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-sugar-runes" title="Sugar Runes: separate story from Arena">

For story, watch Bari's health before spending on more defensive rolls. If she consistently lives through the fight, piling on Damage Reduction may leave the actual problem untouched. You might need more damage, or a different targeting pattern, rather than a sturdier Bari.

Strong rolls in **ATK Amp, Skill Amp, or Skill Haste** are reasonable to keep. There is no need to discard a useful Rune because it misses one supposedly perfect combination. Your promotion level and existing rolls can change which stat helps most on the stage that has you stuck.

Arena changes the survival question. An enemy ranged lineup can deliver enough burst to kill your Charge Cookies as they arrive. **Damage Reduction plus ATK Amp is a sensible starting priority** here: help Bari survive the opening and hurt the target she reaches.

Do not turn that priority into a fixed number of defensive lines for every account. If she already survives but cannot help finish the enemy attacker, more defense may not improve the result. If she vanishes immediately, another damage roll will not keep her alive.

The Skill Amp wording needs particular care. The exclusion applies to the protective buffs; it does not switch off Skill Amp for Bari's damage. A high Skill Amp roll can still be useful. You simply should not expect it to strengthen those buffs as well.

For a wider spending order across the roster, the [Sugar Rune investment guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-sugar-rune-investment-priority/) helps you decide whether Bari should receive the next upgrade at all. Keep a serviceable set while you work on the Cookie actually holding back your team.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-arena-matchups" title="Why a Bari Arena team can still collapse">

Bari and Oven Wanderer can put pressure on a high-ATK enemy, but reaching that enemy is only the first part of the job. The attacking group has to survive and kill something useful. When it fails to secure that kill, the rest of the formation can fall apart quickly.

This is especially painful against opponents with stronger stats or higher promotion. Your Charge group commits to the enemy formation, fails to remove the damage dealer, and dies in place. From there, the surviving ranged attackers can tear through the Cookies left behind.

A team without Bari can therefore beat one that uses her. Heavy ranged burst offers a clear example: it can punish the entry before Bari's side gets its first kill. Her presence alone tells you very little about who wins the matchup.

After a loss, follow the opening rather than staring only at the final damage totals:

1. Find the enemy Bari actually approached.
2. Check whether your Charge Cookies died on arrival or stayed alive without finishing that target.
3. Look at what happened to your other damage dealers while the fight moved around them.

That gives you a useful next change. Early deaths point toward survival or an unfavorable opponent. A living dive group with no kill points toward damage, target durability, or a stat gap. If the Power numbers seem misleading, check the [Arena Power gap guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-arena-power-gap-guide/) before investing more resources on the strength of that number alone.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-upgrade-priorities" title="Spend after checking one failed fight">

Bari improves with promotion, but there is no universal star count here that suddenly makes every matchup work. Compare what an upgrade can solve with what the fight shows. More stats will not necessarily fix a targeting pattern that sends damage away from the enemy you need to remove.

For a story test, keep the stage and other slots consistent. Watch one attempt with the current preset. If allies die, try one Herb swap. If everybody lives and the boss survives, retain the damage slots and review offensive investment. If the fight scatters awkwardly around Bari's target, try another Cookie in her slot before rerolling an entire Rune set.

For Arena, compare opponents with similar formations when you can. One win against a softer ranged team does not settle a build. An opponent with much higher promotion can also overwhelm a workable setup. Look for repeated early deaths or missed kills, then spend on the problem you keep seeing.

If the same team now survives its opening and finishes the target, keep the working Runes. You can leave the next reroll for a Cookie that still needs it.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bari-build-faq" title="Princess Bari build FAQ">

### Does Princess Bari need Cherry Cola?

No. They can work together in story, but the 12-Cookie preset here uses Bari without Cherry Cola. Try the complete formation first, then judge swaps by survival, damage, and targeting in your own fights.

### Is Skill Amp wasted on Princess Bari?

No. Skill Amp affects her damage, even though it does not scale the protective buffs covered by the skill's exclusion. Keep a strong roll if it improves your available set; do not expect stronger protection from it.

### Who should Herb replace in this story team?

Try Strawberry Crepe or Scorpion. Keep Scorpion when poison helps you finish a single boss. If survival is the main problem, compare the two swaps on the same stage before deciding which damage slot to give up.

### Does Bari make a Charge team safe against ranged burst?

No. A strong ranged team can still kill the Charge group on entry. Damage Reduction helps with survival, but promotion gaps, enemy damage, and whether your team finishes its first target still matter.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-resource-guide-accoun.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

CookieRun: Crumble is generous with buttons and stingy with second chances. The costly mistakes look harmless when you make them. Leave the wrong formation active or spend currency to clear a red dot, and three days later the account is short on the material it needs.

This resource guide fixes eight habits that quietly tax progression. None requires a perfect roster. Most take less than a minute to correct, which is nice because the game already gives us enough menus to babysit.

<GuideSection id="leave-the-right-auto-hunt-team" title="1. Leave the right Auto Hunt team active">

Closing the game does not rescue a bad farming formation. Auto Hunt keeps using the team and stage you selected, so the preset on screen matters after you put the phone down.

Use a farming team that clears quickly without losing a single Cookie. One death often becomes two, then the formation spends part of each cycle waiting for a full wipe and revival. A lone healer may survive forever, but survival without kills is a very polite way to earn almost nothing from the live battle side.

Watch several waves before logging off. If the frontline drops, lower the stage or add enough healing and defense to keep all 12 slots working. Then restore area damage and movement effects until the clear is brisk. Save that formation as its own preset. The recommended [Teams](/teams/) give you a better starting shell than whatever the Auto button assembled from your highest Power numbers.

A few hours online and offline produce similar base payouts for an ordinary account. The formation causes the painful gap. The [hidden mechanics guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-tips-hidden-mechanics/) explains the two reward tracks if the totals still look strange. Fix the preset, claim before storage fills, and let your battery sleep too.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="skip-the-standard-banner" title="2. Skip the standard banner when a useful pickup exists">

The standard Cookie banner is easy to justify because every pull feels productive. It also spreads your odds across a wide pool. You can burn a large crystal stack and leave with several Cookies that are one copy closer to nowhere.

A pickup banner gives the spending a target. That matters because promotion stars feed long-term account growth and can unlock a Cookie's important skill breakpoint. Five stars is a sensible minimum target for a featured Cookie you expect to use. Seven stars can make sense when that promotion activates the part of the kit your team needs, but it is not a universal quota.

Do not pull just because the featured art is shiny. Check the [Tier List](/tier-list/), inspect the next promotion effect, and ask whether the Cookie belongs in more than one formation. If the answer is no, keep saving.

<GuideTip title="One banner, one job">

Choose the promotion you want before the first pull. Stop when you reach it. A banner timer is not permission to turn the remaining crystals into random duplicates.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="protect-guild-medals" title="3. Protect Guild Medals from forgettable purchases">

Guild Medals arrive too slowly to spend like Coins. The shop mixes hard-to-replace account materials with items you can farm elsewhere, and the cheaper item is not automatically the better deal.

Start with the bottleneck. Stellar currency deserves attention because regular free income is thin. Dungeon keys can also beat a pile of common material when one extra run reaches a first-clear reward or opens the next Oven Lab step. Materials that already accumulate through Auto Hunt, daily stages, or routine missions belong lower on the list.

Check what blocks progress this week. If a key opens a useful dungeon clear, buy it. If Stellar progress has stopped because the currency is dry, save for that. Clearing a red shop notification is a lousy reason to create a two-week wait.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="claim-hidden-mission-rewards" title="4. Open every mission tab before you log out">

Daily, weekly, challenge, and event missions do not always share one claim button. The roulette screen is a common offender: the wheel is obvious, while its separate mission list sits beside it and can hold an unclaimed final reward.

Make the tab check part of your last login. Open the daily, weekly, challenge, and current event lists. A completed task left unclaimed pays exactly zero.

For roulette spending, batches of five are a comfortable middle ground. Ten at once gives you fewer chances to stop after landing the reward you wanted. The outcome still depends on luck, so do not invent a pattern where none exists. The useful habit is claiming the attached milestones before the event closes.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="spend-arena-tickets" title="5. Spend Arena tickets even when your rank is ugly">

Players often hoard Arena tickets because a loss feels pointless. The ticket was already pointless while sitting at the cap.

Arena attempts build Fame and earn seasonal currency. Fame bonuses can improve other content, so the account keeps something useful even when the match history looks rude. A 2% bonus seems small until it applies across a developed roster and repeated boss attempts.

Use the tickets on opponents you can reasonably challenge. Do not spend ten minutes refreshing for a perfect victim or reach reset with a full stack. The account bonus matters more than protecting a pretty win rate.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="climb-the-research-tree" title="6. Climb the research tree before filling every branch">

The research tree rewards players who move upward. Filling every lower node first feels tidy, but it delays the upgrades that add reward attempts and reduce future costs. It also leaves you with fewer research durations to fit around real life.

Take the required path upward one step at a time. Prioritize permanent economy upgrades, extra reward counts, and research cost reductions. Skip side chests or minor branches until the main route has opened the useful nodes above them.

Higher tiers give you projects with different timers. A seven-hour job can cover sleep, while a shorter one fits the afternoon. Filling the bottom row first can leave you with awkward timers and an idle lab. An empty queue costs more than one unfinished side stat.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="stop-rerolling-stellar-links" title="7. Stop rerolling a good Stellar Link board">

Perfect Stellar Link coverage is a luxury project. For an account with limited currency, a roll above 80% can be good enough to keep while the rest of the roster catches up. Locking more sections raises the next reroll cost, so every attempt becomes harder to justify.

Keep a strong board and rebuild the currency pile. Return later when one additional match would improve a Cookie you use often. Chasing all six connections because the empty space looks annoying is expensive interior decorating.

A near-perfect link around a mediocre lineup does not become a good team. Settle the board and spend again when you can name the benefit before pressing reroll.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="claim-equipment-milestones" title="8. Claim equipment pull milestones immediately">

Equipment pulls have milestone rewards, including a visible claim after a set number of pulls. Do not assume extra progress stacks safely behind an unclaimed reward. When the counter reaches the milestone, stop and collect it before pulling again.

Nothing looks broken while the pull animation keeps working. You notice the loss later, after the next batch fails to build the progress you expected.

Use a simple rule for every summon screen: pull, check the counter, claim, then continue. It takes two taps and protects materials that took much longer to earn.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="resource-recovery-route" title="A 10-minute recovery route for a messy account">

If you have made several of these mistakes, do not restart. Put the account on a cleaner route today:

1. Select a stable Auto Hunt formation and watch three full waves.
2. Claim every daily, weekly, event, and equipment milestone reward.
3. Spend capped Arena tickets and collect the available shop currency.
4. Cancel the urge to pull. Write down the next Cookie promotion you are saving for.
5. Start the highest useful research node that fits your next offline window.
6. Leave Guild Medals and Stellar currency alone until a named upgrade needs them.

That route will not create an SSR from thin air. It stops the leaks while you wait for the next real upgrade. For the broader order of dungeons, Oven gear, Resolve, and Pets, use the [beginner progression guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-beginner-progression-guide/).

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="resource-guide-faq" title="CookieRun: Crumble resource guide FAQ">

### Does my Auto Hunt team matter while CookieRun: Crumble is closed?

Yes. The game keeps using the selected farming formation, so leave a fast team that survives the current stage without losing a Cookie. Closing the game does not fix a weak preset.

### Should I pull the standard or pickup Cookie banner?

Save crystals for a pickup banner that features a Cookie you plan to promote. A standard banner has no focused promotion target, while a useful pickup can turn the same spending into a real five-star breakpoint.

### What should I buy with Guild Medals?

Protect Guild Medals for scarce account upgrades and the dungeon keys that solve your current bottleneck. Avoid spending them on materials the account already earns reliably elsewhere.

### Why should I use Arena tickets if I lose often?

Arena attempts still build Fame and earn seasonal currency. Fame bonuses help account performance outside Arena, so unused tickets throw away permanent progress even when your rank is modest.

### Do equipment pull milestone rewards carry over?

Do not assume they do. Claim the visible reward when the equipment pull counter reaches its milestone before making more pulls, or later progress may be wasted behind an unclaimed reward.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-rye-cookie-build-team.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Rye Cookie is easy to dismiss. At low promotion, her skill reads like plain damage: roughly 400% ATK every four seconds with no healing, shield, or fancy debuff attached. That looks thin beside an SSR skill packed with extra effects.

The comparison changes at five stars. Rye gains two additional hits and reaches roughly 600% total damage per cast while keeping the four-second cooldown. She also fires from range and hits enemies ahead, so the skill connects more reliably than a melee attack that can be interrupted halfway through. This is when Rye stops feeling like an inexpensive placeholder and starts carrying stages.

<GuideSection id="five-star-breakpoint" title="Five stars is the real starting line">

Do not judge a one-star Rye against a promoted SSR and call the experiment finished. Her five-star upgrade adds two hits rather than a small side stat. The extra shots turn a modest skill into short-cooldown burst that can clear waves and remove weakened PvP targets.

That promotion is still a real cost. Rye is an SR, so getting copies is more realistic than maxing a premium unit, but it does not happen for free. If she is below five stars, keep her usable rather than pouring every rare Rune material into her. Save the expensive locks until the extra hits exist.

At five stars, adventure stages move faster because the skill returns every four seconds. In PvP, Rye may not lead the total damage chart, but she can delete one target early and turn the rest of the fight into a numbers advantage.

<GuideTip title="Wait for the part that matters">

Use Rye before five stars if your roster needs her, but postpone the expensive build. The promotion changes her skill enough that early damage tests undersell the finished Cookie.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="why-the-skill-works" title="Why the simple skill works">

Rye's skill does not need a paragraph of effects because its timing does the work. A four-second cooldown gives her repeated chances to finish whatever the rest of the team has damaged. The attack reaches enemies ahead too, which lets one cast hit more than the front target.

During adventure waves, Rye contributes steady area damage without walking into melee range. In Arena, she acts more like a finisher. Wind Archer Cookie or Milky Way Cookie can soften several enemies, then Rye's next cast removes the low-health Cookie before a healer recovers them.

Do not read too much into one damage screen. A stronger account can make any lineup look clever. Watch who Rye targets, how often she casts, and whether those casts change the fight. A clean knockout is worth more than padding the total against a tank that never dies.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="orange-multistrike-core" title="Orange Cookie fixes the team around Rye">

Rye receives Multi-strike, and Orange Cookie is the easiest provider to build around. Orange also gives CRIT Chance Up. Her synergy effect lasts ten seconds while her cooldown is shorter than ten seconds, so the buff can stay active through most of the fight.

Rye gets repeated shots and a large CRIT boost without waiting for a narrow burst window. Melon Soda Cookie also receives Multi-strike and fits the same offensive shell. Herb Cookie uses the synergy too, which lets you add serious healing without wasting the provider slot. Macaron Cookie and Space Doughnut's Royal Excellence offer more options when you change modes.

The practical core is Rye plus Orange, then whatever the stage needs. Add Melon Soda for more damage, Herb for healing, or a sturdy frontline when the opener is the problem. Check each Cookie's Granted and Received effects in the [Cookie list](/cookies/) before assuming a shiny unit activates the synergy.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="teams-by-mode" title="Build Rye teams for the mode">

For general PvE, start with Rye, Orange, a frontline, and enough healing to survive the first skill cycle. Pomegranate Cookie, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, Cheesecake Cookie, and Macaron Cookie can raise damage through Skill Amp, ATK, or CRIT support. You do not need every buffer at once. Pick the ones that also solve the stage's survival problem.

Single-target bosses need a different approach. Pair Rye with Scorpion Cookie so the team has focused damage after wave clear stops mattering. Rowdy Truck is a useful warning: an adventure lineup that cruises through normal stages can stall there until you remove broad damage and add Scorpion or stronger sustain.

PvP can use Rye beside Wind Archer and Milky Way. The two larger area threats pressure the whole team while Rye finishes exposed targets on her short cooldown. This setup is aggressive. If it loses before Rye's second cast, replace one damage slot with defense instead of adding even more damage.

Use the [Team Builder](/tools/team-builder/) to check your twelve slots rather than copying a lineup with promotions you do not have.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="recommended-team" title="Recommended Rye Cookie team">

Start with this lineup for general stages. Check Rye's current place on the [Tier List](/tier-list/) before spending rare upgrade materials, then compare the [recommended teams](/teams/) when a boss calls for more defense or focused damage.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="12-Cookie Multi-strike lineup"
  description="Orange activates Multi-strike for Rye, Melon Soda, Macaron, and Herb. Nameless Cake Hound holds the front while Scorpion handles single targets."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0053", "cookie3001", "cookie0126", "cookie0040", "cookie4024", "cookie0181", "cookie0515", "cookie0037", "cookie0023", "cookie4019", "cookie0063"]}
  petIds={["pet4004", "pet0184", "pet4001"]}
/>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="sugar-rune-stats" title="Best Sugar Rune stats for Rye">

Aim for SR or higher effects once your Rune supply can support several Cookies. Rye has four clean offensive targets:

- ATK% raises every hit.
- CRIT Chance makes the repeated shots convert more often.
- CRIT DMG increases the payoff from Orange Cookie's CRIT support.
- Skill Amp strengthens the cast directly.

Skill Haste is usable, but it is not my first lock. One point gives about 1% cooldown reduction, and Rye already casts every four seconds. Shaving a small fraction from that timer often adds less than a strong ATK or CRIT roll.

Take a good offensive SR before chasing a useless SSR. Rye needs several teammates, and burning the whole account budget on one perfect Rune usually leaves the support core half built. The [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) has a fuller reroll budget if the lock button keeps winning.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="fire-pets" title="Pets for a Fire damage core">

Rye and Scorpion are both Fire damage dealers, so a focused Pet setup can buff both:

- Sweet n' Sour gives all allies CRIT DMG.
- Floral Froglet gives Fire allies more CRIT DMG.
- Holy Baby Drop gives all allies ATK.

This trio also helps Nameless Cake Hound or Vampire Cookie when they occupy another damage slot. Hot Doggie is a reasonable Skill Amp alternative, while Gold Drop works when the team needs more CRIT Chance. Compare effects on the [Pets list](/pets/) before using a high-rarity Pet that buffs the wrong element.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="bad-matchups" title="When Rye is the wrong answer">

Rye is much less convincing before five stars. She also loses value when a boss demands pure single-target damage, the team cannot keep Multi-strike active, or she dies before cycling the skill.

The failed run tells you what to change. Scorpion covers focused damage. Orange restores the missing synergy. If survival is the problem, remove a greedy attacker for Herb, Milk, or a defensive Cookie instead of rebuilding every slot.

Rye cannot excuse low combat power either. An underpowered team may still suffer a stage penalty. Promotion, levels, gear, and the rest of the lineup have to keep up.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="quick-build" title="Quick Rye Cookie build">

1. Reach five stars before judging Rye's ceiling.
2. Pair her with Orange Cookie for Multi-strike and CRIT Chance Up.
3. Roll ATK%, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, or Skill Amp on Sugar Runes.
4. Add Scorpion for strict boss fights and Melon Soda for broader pressure.
5. Use Fire damage Pets when Rye and Scorpion share the team.
6. Replace one attacker with healing or defense if Rye cannot reach her second cast.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rye-cookie-faq" title="Rye Cookie FAQ">

### Does Rye Cookie need five stars?

Five stars is the important breakpoint because it adds two hits and raises the skill from roughly 400% to 600% total damage per cast. She can fill a slot earlier, but the promoted version is the one worth building around.

### What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Rye Cookie?

Prioritize ATK%, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, and Skill Amp. Skill Haste is acceptable, but the four-second base cooldown makes it less urgent than a strong offensive roll.

### Who is Rye Cookie's best teammate?

Orange Cookie is the cleanest partner because she grants Multi-strike and CRIT Chance Up with near-continuous uptime. Scorpion Cookie is the best addition when the team needs more single-target boss damage.

### Is Rye Cookie good in PvP?

Yes, especially as a burst finisher. She can remove damaged enemies quickly, although another Cookie may show more total damage over the full fight.

### Which Pets work with Rye Cookie?

Sweet n' Sour, Floral Froglet, and Holy Baby Drop form a strong Fire damage setup by adding CRIT DMG, Fire ally CRIT DMG, and ATK. Hot Doggie or Gold Drop can replace one slot when the account needs Skill Amp or CRIT Chance.

</GuideSection>
