cookie-run-crumble-skill-amp-fix-rune-re.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Skill Amp used to be the lazy answer to almost every Sugar Rune question. Damage dealer? Add Skill Amp. Healer? Add Skill Amp. Debuffer with one useful line of text? Sure, pile it on there too. The August 27 adjustment finally puts a fence around that stat, and several familiar builds no longer get the effect players rolled for.

The change does not make Skill Amp bad. It stops the stat from strengthening specific debuffs, and it prevents DEF Down from pushing an enemy below zero DEF. If that debuff was the reason you rolled Skill Amp, the Rune needs a new job.

<GuideSection id="what-changed" title="What the Skill Amp fix changes">

Two combat rules changed together. First, DEF Down can reduce a target to zero DEF, but it cannot create negative DEF anymore. Before the fix, stacking enough DEF Down made an enemy take extra damage after its defense was already gone. That worked in PvE and PvP, so teams could gain more from a debuffer than the skill text suggested.

Second, Skill Amp no longer strengthens debuffs that reduce a target's stats. ATK Down, DEF Down, Accuracy Down, and similar effects now use their stated value. The same restriction applies to the affected Damage Taken Down effects. Skill Amp still improves damage, healing, shields, and eligible buffs when the skill allows it. Read each skill line before rerolling.

<GuideTip title="Keep the Rune until you read the skill">

Do not strip Skill Amp from every Cookie. Check which part of the skill receives it. A healer or damage dealer may keep the full benefit while a pure stat debuffer gets almost nothing useful.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="affected-cookies" title="The 11 Cookies that need a Rune check">

The original Sugar Rune refund summary names 11 Cookies. Check its GingerBrave entry against the notice: current game data puts ATK Down on GingerBright. The build checks below still apply:

- Devil Cookie, Pancake Cookie, and Dark Choco Cookie use DEF Down.
- Onion Cookie uses ATK Down. GingerBrave does not: current game data assigns that debuff to GingerBright. Check the name in the original refund notice before relying on the historical list below.
- Cocoa Cookie, Angel Cookie, Ion Cookie Robot, and Nameless Cake Hound have affected defensive effects.
- Gumball Cookie and Vampire Cookie carry other stat reductions that no longer scale the old way.

That list is a reason to inspect builds, not a command to bench 11 Cookies. Dark Choco still brings DEF Down. Ion Cookie Robot is still a sturdy defender. Nameless Cake Hound still has a job when a Fire frontline fits the team. What changed is the return from Skill Amp and from stacking too much of the same reduction.

Before spending new materials, check where each Cookie sits on the current [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/). A Cookie with several useful jobs can absorb a weaker interaction. A one-trick debuffer has a much harder argument.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="defense-floor" title="Stop paying for DEF below zero">

The zero DEF floor punishes overlap. If Dark Choco and Devil Cookie already remove all of a boss's defense, another DEF Down effect cannot push the damage higher through negative defense. The extra slot may be better spent on CRIT support, elemental damage, healing, or a Cookie who survives long enough to cast twice.

You will notice the change most on low-DEF targets and teams that stacked several reductions. High-DEF bosses can still give DEF Down plenty of room to work. Test the same stage with the same Pets, then watch the clear time rather than trusting the displayed Power number. If the run barely changes, your team was not living off negative DEF. If damage falls off a cliff, the old interaction was doing more work than the lineup admitted.

The [Accuracy and Focus guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-accuracy-focus-guide/) still matters here. Focus helps a debuff land. It does not make that debuff stronger, and it cannot move DEF below the new floor.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="devil-cookie-build" title="Devil Cookie loses the easiest build">

Devil Cookie takes the ugliest hit because DEF Down is the main reason to bring him. His personal damage is modest, and he is fragile enough that teams often spend another slot keeping him alive. Skill Amp used to improve the debuff that justified all that babysitting. It now gives a small damage gain that rarely pays for the Rune.

Move Devil toward survival first. HP, DEF, or Damage Reduction can keep him alive for the cast that matters. Skill Haste is worth testing when another application helps after the first debuff expires. Focus still has a purpose against resistant enemies. Full Skill Amp is difficult to defend unless a later balance change adds another eligible effect.

He is not automatically useless. A boss with enough DEF and low enough pressure can still make his reduction worthwhile. Replace him when he dies early or when another Cookie already reaches the DEF floor.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="tank-builds" title="Retune Ion and the defensive group carefully">

Ion Cookie Robot shows why a blanket Rune reset would be silly. Skill Amp may still help an eligible shield or another part of the skill, but it no longer improves the affected reduction. If the old build existed mainly to stretch that defensive effect, try a tank set or Skill Haste and compare survival across a full fight.

Cocoa, Angel, and Nameless Cake Hound deserve the same treatment. Read each effect separately. Keep Skill Amp when the remaining healing, shield, damage, or buff is worth the stat. Replace it when the blocked line was the whole point.

The [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) has the safer reroll order. Lock one strong line at a time. Trying to rebuild four defenders on refund day is a quick way to turn compensation into another shortage.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pinot-noir-rule" title="Pinot Noir already follows the new rule">

Pinot Noir Cookie is not part of the refund group because the kit launched with the restriction in its text. Skill Amp does not increase Healing Received Down. That anti-heal effect is already strong enough to pressure healer teams at its printed value.

Pinot Noir's Knock-up Resistance Up also ignores Skill Amp. Do not keep a Rune expecting it to strengthen either the anti-heal or the resistance buff. Focus can help the debuff land against resistance, while Skill Haste offers limited value because the important timers already have good coverage.

The updated [Pinot Noir build](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-pinot-noir-cookie-build/) separates those jobs so you can choose the Rune stat that solves your current problem.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rune-refund" title="Use the September 1 refund once">

Sugar Rune reroll materials spent on the listed Cookies are scheduled for refund on September 1. That gives affected accounts room to rebuild without paying twice for a rule that was not clear before the fix.

Take a screenshot of each current set before changing it. Write down the replacement stat and the content where that Cookie plays. After the refund arrives, rebuild one high-use Cookie and test it before touching the next. Do not roll extra lines now just to chase compensation. Nothing about the refund makes a bad roll useful, and last-minute spending may not behave the way you hope.

Devil is the obvious first audit. Ion, Dark Choco, and Nameless Cake Hound come next when they appear in several presets. A Cookie sitting unused at level 20 can wait. The refund does not expire because the red dot looks impatient.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rebuild-checklist" title="A practical team audit after the fix">

1. Mark every affected Cookie in your saved presets.
2. Check whether two or more Cookies stack DEF Down on the same target.
3. Run one familiar boss or stage before changing Runes and record the clear time.
4. Replace Skill Amp only where the blocked effect was the main reason for the build.
5. Repeat the same fight with the new set before rebuilding another Cookie.

Use the tested [CookieRun: Crumble Teams](/teams/) as a baseline when an old preset loses too much damage. Swap one slot at a time. Replacing Devil, changing three Pets, and rerolling Ion in the same test tells you nothing except that the result is different.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="skill-amp-faq" title="Skill Amp fix FAQ">

### Did CookieRun: Crumble nerf Skill Amp?

Skill Amp still boosts damage, healing, shields, and eligible buffs. It no longer strengthens debuffs that reduce target stats, and DEF Down cannot push a target below zero DEF. The stat is narrower, not useless.

### Which Cookies receive the Sugar Rune refund?

The original refund summary lists Devil, Pancake, Dark Choco, GingerBrave, Onion, Cocoa, Angel, Ion Cookie Robot, Nameless Cake Hound, Gumball, and Vampire Cookie. Check the GingerBrave entry against the notice: current game data gives ATK Down to GingerBright.

### Is Devil Cookie still worth using?

Devil can still help against targets with enough DEF, but Skill Amp no longer improves his main debuff. Build enough survival to cast reliably, then test Focus or Skill Haste if the fight needs them.

### When is the Sugar Rune refund?

The announced refund is scheduled for September 1. It covers Sugar Rune reroll investment on the listed affected Cookies.

### Does Skill Amp improve Pinot Noir's anti-heal?

No. Healing Received Down and Knock-up Resistance Up both ignore Skill Amp. Do not roll it to strengthen either effect; use Focus when enemy Resistance blocks the debuff.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-strawberry-crepe-cook.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTeamFormation } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

Strawberry Crepe Cookie has a Tank label, so the obvious move is to load their Sugar Runes with HP and Damage Reduction. That obvious move also throws away the reason to use them.

Crepe Crasher is a four-second area attack with pushback. At its highest listed upgrade, the hit reaches 159.2% of ATK with a 2.75 effect radius. Rapid Fire can repeat that hit, and Chargemellow gives the team another Rapid Fire point while raising ATK for its receivers. Strawberry Crepe is less a wall and more a short-range damage dealer wearing the wrong name tag.

A pure defensive page may keep them alive, but it can turn a potential 840,000-damage Arena result into a Cookie that survives long enough to achieve very little. Build damage first, then add one survival line only when the same matchup keeps killing them before a second cast.

<GuideSection id="role-mismatch" title="Stop treating the Tank label as build advice">

Strawberry Crepe pushes enemies away, but the skill does not grant the sort of shield, heal, or large defensive buff that would make them a dependable solo frontline. They still take real punishment at close range. A Tank icon does not cancel that problem.

Their useful loop is simple. Walk into a group, swing the crepe arms, push the pack, then repeat four seconds later. More Rapid Fire activations turn each cast into a much nastier burst. Crowded story waves are the cleanest target because the 2.75 radius can hit several enemies instead of spending the whole animation on one body.

The [CookieRun: Crumble Tier List](/tier-list/) can help you compare investment options, but do not read a letter grade as an order to strip a finished five-star carry. Strawberry Crepe becomes attractive when you already have Pinot Noir, Chargemellow, and enough offensive Runes to support the loop.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="aoe-team" title="Copy the full AoE team">

Use this formation for story stages, tower rooms, and bosses that bring extra waves. It is deliberately heavy on immediate damage. Macaron raises CRIT Chance, Pomegranate adds Skill Amp Up, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician covers ATK and healing, and Herb adds another heal. Pinot Noir and Chargemellow complete the Rapid Fire package. If that support is still a new project, the [Pinot Noir build](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-pinot-noir-cookie-build/) explains the useful promotion target.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Strawberry Crepe rapid AoE team"
  description="This complete wave-clearing formation gives Strawberry Crepe a Rapid Fire package, two healers, and Nameless Cake Hound to protect the short-range damage core."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0181", "cookie3001", "cookie0126", "cookie4024", "cookie0063", "cookie4013", "cookie0515", "cookie4010", "cookie4019", "cookie0518", "cookie0103"]}
  petIds={["pet4005", "pet4001", "pet0111"]}
/>

Scorpion, Melon Soda, Brightseeker, and Rye occupy the flexible damage slots. If one is underpromoted, replace that Cookie before breaking the support core. Rye is the easiest cut below five stars. Melon Soda or Brightseeker can also leave when another trained damage dealer has much better Runes.

Dark Choco supplies the safer DEF Down option. Nameless Cake Hound lowers incoming damage, which Strawberry Crepe appreciates more than their Tank label suggests. Copy the formation first, run the stage, then adjust one flexible damage slot at a time. The [recommended teams page](/teams/) helps when the stage needs a different balance of healing, control, and single-target damage.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="devil-team" title="Use Devil when you can afford the risk">

Devil Cookie can replace Dark Choco when a stronger DEF Down window matters more than stability. The other eleven Cookies and all three Pets stay unchanged, so you can compare the swap without changing half the experiment.

<GuideTeamFormation
  title="Strawberry Crepe Devil burst team"
  description="Swap Dark Choco for Devil when faster DEF Down pressure can finish the fight. This version hits harder but gives you less room for an unlucky opener."
  cookieIds={["cookie0059", "cookie0181", "cookie3001", "cookie0126", "cookie4024", "cookie0063", "cookie4013", "cookie0515", "cookie4010", "cookie4019", "cookie0518", "cookie0023"]}
  petIds={["pet4005", "pet4001", "pet0111"]}
/>

Devil is squishy, and Strawberry Crepe is already easier to kill than their role suggests. If Devil disappears before the important burst, the prettier debuff number bought nothing. Return to Dark Choco for difficult pushes or opponents with strong openers.

In Arena, the Devil version can punish a team that gives you time. It is much less comfortable against Rye. A good Rye opener can remove a Cookie before your first rotation settles, even when your displayed Power is higher. Espresso and Adventurer can also spoil the test by controlling the unit you wanted to measure. Arena results need several attempts, not one clean damage report.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="pet-loadout" title="Use the three Pets as one package">

Chargemellow is the piece that changed the build. It grants one Rapid Fire point and raises ATK for Rapid Fire receivers. Strawberry Crepe, Rye, Melon Soda, Macaron, Herb, and Pinot Noir all gain something from the completed package.

Holy Baby Drop raises ATK for the full lineup. That also improves healing that scales with ATK, which makes the Pet less selfish than it looks. Hot Doggie supplies Skill Amp. The stat still improves the damage and eligible buffs that this formation cares about after the stat-debuff correction.

Do not remove Chargemellow because another Pet has more stars. Test what happens to the active synergy first. A lower-star Pet that turns on repeated casts can improve six Cookies at once. The raw Power loss may look ugly while the clear becomes faster.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="sugar-runes" title="Build Sugar Runes for damage">

Start with four stats:

- ATK Amp
- CRIT Chance
- CRIT DMG
- Skill Amp

Those lines improve the job Strawberry Crepe performs in this formation. Skill Haste is acceptable, but the four-second cooldown already cycles quickly. A strong Skill Haste roll is worth keeping. It is not worth discarding a better offensive page to chase one.

Use the [gear and Sugar Rune guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-gear-sugar-rune-stats-guide/) before locking an expensive page. You do not need four perfect labels on every Rune. You need enough useful offense that Crepe Crasher hurts every time Rapid Fire repeats it.

Add HP Amp or Damage Reduction only after you see the same survival problem more than once. One defensive line can be sensible in Arena. Turning the whole page into tank stats is a panic response that removes the build's best feature.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="damage-tests" title="Read the damage without fooling yourself">

A clean Arena fight produced about 840,000 damage, close to one million. In a separate close matchup, Strawberry Crepe died early and still matched the damage of a ten-star Milky Way. Those numbers explain the interest, but they do not guarantee the same result on every account.

Target count changes everything. The 2.75 radius loves packed enemies and waves. A lonely boss wastes the area advantage, so a focused single-target attacker may win. Survival changes the result too. Dying before the next four-second cycle turns a great damage page into a short demonstration.

Compare three runs. If Strawberry Crepe lives and the result stays weak, inspect Rapid Fire and the offensive Runes. If they die at the same moment every time, add one defensive line or move back to Dark Choco. If Rye deletes someone at the opener, stop treating that match as a neutral damage test.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="investment" title="Decide whether to invest now">

Build Strawberry Crepe when you need fast AoE clearing, own Pinot Noir, and can field Chargemellow without dismantling another important team. They also make sense when regular pulls have already given you several promotion stars. A forgotten promoted SSR is cheaper to finish than a brand-new premium carry.

Wait when your main damage dealers are still below their important star breakpoints or when Chargemellow would remain too weak to use. Strawberry Crepe fits many formations, but twelve slots fill quickly. Do not copy the top Arena accounts blindly. Those players often counter the same small group of opponents and hide Cookies to protect matchup information.

Save the full AoE preset and build one offensive Rune page. Run the stage that currently blocks you three times. Compare the clear time and note when Strawberry Crepe dies. If the stage gets faster, keep investing. If only the damage report gets prettier while the team still collapses, fix the support package before buying another reroll.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="strawberry-crepe-faq" title="Strawberry Crepe Cookie FAQ">

### Is Strawberry Crepe Cookie a tank or a damage dealer?

They have the Tank role, but this build treats them as an AoE damage dealer. Crepe Crasher provides damage and pushback without enough built-in protection to justify a full defensive Sugar Rune page.

### What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Strawberry Crepe Cookie?

Prioritize ATK Amp, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, and Skill Amp. Skill Haste is a useful secondary roll. Add one HP Amp or Damage Reduction line only when they repeatedly die before another cast.

### Which Pets work best with Strawberry Crepe Cookie?

Use Chargemellow, Holy Baby Drop, and Hot Doggie. Chargemellow grants Rapid Fire and ATK to its receivers, Holy Baby Drop raises team ATK, and Hot Doggie adds Skill Amp.

### Is Strawberry Crepe Cookie good in Arena?

Yes, especially against grouped teams that cannot remove or control them early. Rye burst and heavy control can end the run before the damage cycle develops, so test several opponents instead of judging one result.

### Should I use Dark Choco or Devil Cookie?

Dark Choco is the safer DEF Down option. Devil can create a stronger offensive window but dies more easily. Use Devil when the opponent gives the team time, then return to Dark Choco when survival becomes unreliable.

</GuideSection>

Macaron raises CRIT Chance, Pomegranate adds Skill Amp Up, Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician covers ATK and healing, and Herb adds another heal. Pinot Noir and Chargemellow complete the Rapid Fire package. If that support is still a new project, the
Pinot Noir build
explains the useful promotion target.
Strawberry Crepe rapid AoE team
segments.name: title

segments.text: This complete wave-clearing formation gives Strawberry Crepe a Rapid Fire package, two healers, and Nameless Cake Hound to protect the short-range damage core.
segments.name: description

segments.text: Scorpion, Melon Soda, Brightseeker, and Rye occupy the flexible damage slots. If one is underpromoted, replace that Cookie before breaking the support core. Rye is the easiest cut below five stars. Melon Soda or Brightseeker can also leave when another trained damage dealer has much better Runes.

Dark Choco supplies the safer DEF Down option. Nameless Cake Hound lowers incoming damage, which Strawberry Crepe appreciates more than their Tank label suggests. Copy the formation first, run the stage, then adjust one flexible damage slot at a time. The
recommended teams page
helps when the stage needs a different balance of healing, control, and single-target damage.
Copy the full AoE team
segments.name: title

segments.text: Devil Cookie can replace Dark Choco when a stronger DEF Down window matters more than stability. The other eleven Cookies and all three Pets stay unchanged, so you can compare the swap without changing half the experiment.
Strawberry Crepe Devil burst team
segments.name: title

segments.text: Swap Dark Choco for Devil when faster DEF Down pressure can finish the fight. This version hits harder but gives you less room for an unlucky opener.
segments.name: description

segments.text: Devil is squishy, and Strawberry Crepe is already easier to kill than their role suggests. If Devil disappears before the important burst, the prettier debuff number bought nothing. Return to Dark Choco for difficult pushes or opponents with strong openers.

In Arena, the Devil version can punish a team that gives you time. It is much less comfortable against Rye. A good Rye opener can remove a Cookie before your first rotation settles, even when your displayed Power is higher. Espresso and Adventurer can also spoil the test by controlling the unit you wanted to measure. Arena results need several attempts, not one clean damage report.
Use Devil when you can afford the risk
segments.name: title

segments.text: Chargemellow is the piece that changed the build. It grants one Rapid Fire point and raises ATK for Rapid Fire receivers. Strawberry Crepe, Rye, Melon Soda, Macaron, Herb, and Pinot Noir all gain something from the completed package.

Holy Baby Drop raises ATK for the full lineup. That also improves healing that scales with ATK, which makes the Pet less selfish than it looks. Hot Doggie supplies Skill Amp. The stat still improves the damage and eligible buffs that this formation cares about after the stat-debuff correction.

Do not remove Chargemellow because another Pet has more stars. Test what happens to the active synergy first. A lower-star Pet that turns on repeated casts can improve six Cookies at once. The raw Power loss may look ugly while the clear becomes faster.
Use the three Pets as one package
segments.name: title

segments.text: Start with four stats:
ATK Amp
CRIT Chance
CRIT DMG
Skill Amp

Those lines improve the job Strawberry Crepe performs in this formation. Skill Haste is acceptable, but the four-second cooldown already cycles quickly. A strong Skill Haste roll is worth keeping. It is not worth discarding a better offensive page to chase one.
Use the
gear and Sugar Rune guide
before locking an expensive page. You do not need four perfect labels on every Rune. You need enough useful offense that Crepe Crasher hurts every time Rapid Fire repeats it.

Add HP Amp or Damage Reduction only after you see the same survival problem more than once. One defensive line can be sensible in Arena. Turning the whole page into tank stats is a panic response that removes the build's best feature.
Build Sugar Runes for damage
segments.name: title

segments.text: A clean Arena fight produced about 840,000 damage, close to one million. In a separate close matchup, Strawberry Crepe died early and still matched the damage of a ten-star Milky Way. Those numbers explain the interest, but they do not guarantee the same result on every account.

Target count changes everything. The 2.75 radius loves packed enemies and waves. A lonely boss wastes the area advantage, so a focused single-target attacker may win. Survival changes the result too. Dying before the next four-second cycle turns a great damage page into a short demonstration.

Compare three runs. If Strawberry Crepe lives and the result stays weak, inspect Rapid Fire and the offensive Runes. If they die at the same moment every time, add one defensive line or move back to Dark Choco. If Rye deletes someone at the opener, stop treating that match as a neutral damage test.
Read the damage without fooling yourself
segments.name: title

segments.text: Build Strawberry Crepe when you need fast AoE clearing, own Pinot Noir, and can field Chargemellow without dismantling another important team. They also make sense when regular pulls have already given you several promotion stars. A forgotten promoted SSR is cheaper to finish than a brand-new premium carry.

Wait when your main damage dealers are still below their important star breakpoints or when Chargemellow would remain too weak to use. Strawberry Crepe fits many formations, but twelve slots fill quickly. Do not copy the top Arena accounts blindly. Those players often counter the same small group of opponents and hide Cookies to protect matchup information.

Save the full AoE preset and build one offensive Rune page. Run the stage that currently blocks you three times. Compare the clear time and note when Strawberry Crepe dies. If the stage gets faster, keep investing. If only the damage report gets prettier while the team still collapses, fix the support package before buying another reroll.
Decide whether to invest now
segments.name: title

segments.text: Is Strawberry Crepe Cookie a tank or a damage dealer?
They have the Tank role, but this build treats them as an AoE damage dealer. Crepe Crasher provides damage and pushback without enough built-in protection to justify a full defensive Sugar Rune page.
What are the best Sugar Rune stats for Strawberry Crepe Cookie?
Prioritize ATK Amp, CRIT Chance, CRIT DMG, and Skill Amp. Skill Haste is a useful secondary roll. Add one HP Amp or Damage Reduction line only when they repeatedly die before another cast.
Which Pets work best with Strawberry Crepe Cookie?
Use Chargemellow, Holy Baby Drop, and Hot Doggie. Chargemellow grants Rapid Fire and ATK to its receivers, Holy Baby Drop raises team ATK, and Hot Doggie adds Skill Amp.
Is Strawberry Crepe Cookie good in Arena?

Yes, especially against grouped teams that cannot remove or control them early. Rye burst and heavy control can end the run before the damage cycle develops, so test several opponents instead of judging one result.
Should I use Dark Choco or Devil Cookie?

Dark Choco is the safer DEF Down option. Devil can create a stronger offensive window but dies more easily. Use Devil when the opponent gives the team time, then return to Dark Choco when survival becomes unreliable.
Strawberry Crepe Cookie FAQ

cookie-run-crumble-sugar-rune-investment.text:
import { GuideSection } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

You finish rolling a damage dealer's Sugar Runes, enter the same stage, and barely move the boss's health bar. Worse, Milk loses a buff that used to keep the team working. You gained ATK, but the run got worse.

CookieRun: Crumble rewards investment in Cookies you use across several modes, but the stat you choose can also change who receives support effects. A stronger attacker can accidentally take a buff you meant for Milk, Macaron, or Skating Queen.

**Start your Sugar Rune work with Milk, then Pomegranate and the supports you regularly field.** Keep Crystal spending on a separate plan. Pinot Noir can deserve your next promotion while Milk deserves your next Rune materials. Promotions develop the Multi-strike lineup; the Rune work fixes the support setup you already use.

<GuideSection id="milk-rune-budget" title="Give Milk the first serious Rune budget">

Milk Cookie's Crunchy Strong Pediatrician, shortened to Milk here, earns early investment because the same support appears in many working teams. ATK Amp helps push Milk to the top of the team's ATK ranking for effects that select the strongest attacker, including the intended Welfare recipient.

That target matters more than filling every slot with matching letters. A Rune setup can keep one or two Skill Amp or Skill Haste lines if Milk still wins the ATK check. You do not need to erase useful rolls just to make the page look tidy.

Check your roster against the [CookieRun: Crumble tier list](/tier-list/) before committing scarce materials. A high rank helps you shortlist investments, but frequency of use settles the order. Milk appearing in your daily teams deserves more attention than a specialist you bring out once a week.

There is a limit to this recommendation. An ATK-heavy Milk build supports a particular targeting plan. If you switch that plan, the ideal Rune mix can change. Get the setup working, then spend elsewhere before chasing tiny improvements on every line.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="check-buff-targets" title="Check the 10% leader bonus before rerolling">

The displayed ATK comparison can mislead you. Milk's relevant leader bonus adds 10% to ATK, DEF, and HP, and that bonus is not already included in the stat value you are checking. Include it when you work out the intended highest-ATK Cookie.

For a simple example, 100,000 displayed ATK becomes 110,000 after a 10% increase. Compare the other Cookie under the applicable battle conditions too. The example explains the arithmetic; it does not set a minimum ATK target for your account.

Then watch Macaron's opening skill. Macaron selects the ally with the highest ATK, so the recipient gives you a practical check. If the skill goes somewhere other than Milk, stop rolling and find the Cookie that overtook him.

You can raise Milk's ATK or reduce a competing Cookie's level. The second option can cost damage, so use the smallest adjustment that restores the intended target. Repeat the opening after each change. A stat screen helps you estimate; the skill recipient tells you whether the setup behaves as expected.

Pomegranate introduces another targeting decision. If you want her beam on Macaron and Skating Queen, excessive ATK Amp on damage dealers can make those targets harder to arrange. The [Milk Dungeon buff setup](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-dungeon-milk-buff-guide/) explains that more demanding support-target plan. Decide which version you want before rolling several attackers.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="support-rune-stats" title="Build Pomegranate, Skating Queen, and Macaron next">

Pomegranate's straightforward Rune target is Skill Amp. Start by aiming for an SSR Skill Amp first line, where crafting costs are lower. That is a sensible place to spend deliberately because she supports so many teams.

A second SSR line is a budget choice. If materials are tight, accept SR Skill Amp on the later lines and move to the next Cookie. If chasing that second SSR leaves you with nothing for Milk or Herb, keep the SR roll.

Skating Queen generally wants Skill Amp and Skill Haste. Those stats improve the support job without forcing a complicated ATK contest. Macaron has a similarly practical default: prioritize Skill Amp when you cannot afford to rebuild the Runes whenever you change formations.

Players with large reroll reserves can use ATK Amp on these supports to raise their targeting priority. That can help direct Pomegranate or Macaron effects toward the desired recipients. It also asks you to control the rest of the team's ATK, which gets awkward when you keep changing damage dealers.

For an ordinary material budget, stay with the simpler support stats. Check the [recommended teams](/teams/) to see which supports recur in the formations you use. Invest in that shared group first, then work on Cookies specific to one fight.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="survival-and-debuffs" title="Keep the debuffers and healers alive">

After the shared supports, pick the next Rune owner by the failure you can see. A dead healer and a missed debuff call for different fixes.

- Dark Choco wants Skill Haste and Focus for the debuff role. Keep one Damage Reduction line if he dies too quickly, then reconsider it once survival improves.
- Pinot Noir puts Skill Haste first and Focus second. Give the Cookie that enables your Multi-strike team enough attention to do that job reliably.
- Herb often needs Damage Reduction because he can fall before the healing helps. Skill Amp, Skill Haste, and useful ATK rolls are also worth keeping.
- Nameless Cake Hound can use Damage Reduction or Skill Haste. Favor survival when the front line collapses before the team settles into its rotation.
- Scorpion benefits from Focus when you need debuffs to land consistently. Reaching five stars does not mean every application will ignore enemy Resistance.

Avoid treating this as a queue you must finish from top to bottom. If Herb dies in every attempt while Dark Choco already survives, Herb gets the next useful defensive roll. You can come back to Dark Choco after Herb survives the opening.

For most damage dealers, Skill Amp and Skill Haste are practical starting choices. ATK Amp can help damage, but check the support targets again after adding it. A roll that steals Pomegranate's beam can leave the overall team worse off even when that attacker's personal stats rise.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="crystal-priorities" title="Spend Crystals on promotion breakpoints">

Promotion priority follows a different order from Rune priority. In a Multi-strike account choosing between Pinot Noir and Cherry Cola, aim for Pinot Noir's five-star target first. Pinot Noir supplies the synergy that the team uses; Cherry Cola benefits from it. Building the enabler first gives the rest of the formation a clearer purpose.

With a larger Crystal reserve, the next plan is Pinot Noir at seven stars, followed by Cherry Cola at five. Treat those as spending targets, not entry requirements. You can try Cherry Cola in a story team before reaching five stars, and a lower promotion does not automatically make the formation unusable.

After those targets, saving for another update is reasonable. Further promotions depend on what you can afford and how much you use the Cookie. Decide where to stop before opening the summon screen. It is much easier to keep a budget before the next pull starts looking irresistible.

Brightseeker has a separate five-star consideration for players who can comfortably afford the investment. The summoned drone count rises from two to three at that point. That is a concrete reason to consider five stars, but it does not make the target mandatory for a limited budget.

Use these priorities when the relevant summons are available. Do not empty your reserves because a roster page contains an unfinished star row. Level resets make EXP allocation easier to correct; a spent Crystal budget needs time to rebuild.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="chargemellow-level-10" title="Make Chargemellow a limited Pet exception">

Cookie promotions contribute to Stellar Link unlock conditions. Pets do not, which is why ordinary Pet summoning is a weaker default use of Crystals for this plan.

Chargemellow has a specific exception: level 10 raises its Multi-strike synergy contribution to two. For a team built around that synergy, reaching the breakpoint can justify attention even when you normally keep Crystals away from Pets.

**Set level 10 as the target, then reassess further Pet spending.** The exception is for completing an important synergy contribution. It does not justify continuing Pet pulls indefinitely or neglecting Pinot Noir's promotion plan.

If Chargemellow already meets the target, return to the Cookie budget. Check what you own before summoning; an old recommendation to reach a breakpoint cannot help you twice.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="exp-allocation" title="Allocate EXP after choosing your buff targets">

When EXP is scarce, give Milk the highest level first. Raise the damage dealers next, then the healers. Keep the remaining Cookies at a more even level instead of spreading every upgrade equally across the full roster.

The reset feature lets you redistribute levels when the team changes. You can rebuild an allocation from level one if necessary, but do not dismantle a working roster merely to copy an example. Check whether a smaller change solves the targeting problem first.

The [level 100 EXP priority guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-level-100-exp-priority-guide/) covers the larger allocation decision. For this Rune plan, the check is simpler: after changing levels, confirm that Milk still receives the intended highest-ATK effect.

Before your next crafting session, choose one Cookie and one reason to improve it. Perhaps Milk needs to regain the opening buff, or Herb needs to survive long enough to heal. Keep a useful result, test the same fight, and stop when that problem is solved. Save the remaining materials for the next Cookie whose build needs work.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="rune-priority-faq" title="Sugar Rune spending FAQ">

### Who should get Sugar Runes first?

Start with Milk for the highest-ATK support setup, then Pomegranate and the supports you use across several teams. Move a fragile healer or failing debuffer ahead when that Cookie is the reason attempts collapse.

### Does Milk need ATK Amp on every line?

No. One or two Skill Amp or Skill Haste lines can stay if Milk still meets the intended ATK ranking. Include the relevant 10% leader bonus and check Macaron's opening recipient before replacing useful Runes.

### Should I force SSR on every Pomegranate line?

Aim for SSR Skill Amp on the cheaper first line. A second SSR is optional; SR Skill Amp on later lines is a reasonable stopping point when materials need to cover several Cookies.

### Is five-star Scorpion guaranteed to land debuffs?

No. Five stars does not remove the enemy Resistance check. Focus helps when failed applications disrupt the run, so keep it in consideration even after promotion.

</GuideSection>

cookie-run-crumble-tips-hidden-mechanics.text:
import { GuideSection, GuideTip } from "@/components/guide-mdx";

CookieRun: Crumble can waste your progress without showing a red warning. A debuff misses, but the damage screen only tells you the final number. A high-Power Arena team loses to a smaller roster. Auto Hunt keeps running, yet the gold gain is miserable because eleven Cookies died and Herb has been healing himself for ten minutes.

Most of these failures come from a small icon or a rule the game barely explains. Check these nine systems before spending crystals or rebuilding a team that was almost fine.

<GuideSection id="read-battle-icons" title="1. Check whether the debuff landed">

A skill hitting the target does not prove its debuff worked. Watch the icons beside the enemy. An ATK Down, DEF Down, poison, or other status should appear after the hit. If the icon never shows, your Cookie dealt the direct damage but failed the second half of the job.

Scorpion Cookie can build up to 20 poison stacks, so the number beside the status tells you whether her damage engine is running or coughing on the first turn. A stalled counter can point to low Focus or a missed application. Do not judge the build from one large result screen when the opening ten seconds already exposed the problem.

Tap a Cookie during combat to inspect its live buffs. The same habit catches inactive synergies. A Granted effect looks impressive on the lineup screen, but it has no value when nobody receives it.

The [Accuracy and Focus guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-accuracy-focus-guide/) explains how to separate a missed hit from a resisted status. That distinction saves a lot of bad gear rerolls.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="scorpion-five-star" title="2. Treat Scorpion's five-star promotion as a real breakpoint">

Scorpion Cookie changes sharply at five stars. Her Multi-shot value rises from 2 to 3, which lets a single skill cycle build poison much faster. With the right setup, one cast can reach roughly 10 stacks. Before that promotion, the same team cannot create the same opening pressure.

More Multi-shot providers do not keep adding together. The game uses the strongest received value. Filling three slots with providers will not turn level 3 into level 9. Use one reliable provider and give the other slots different jobs.

This is why rarity alone is a lazy way to judge Cookies. A promoted SR with a skill breakpoint can beat an underbuilt SSR that has no useful connection to the team. Check the current [Tier List](/tier-list/) for investment priorities, then look at what the next promotion changes before spending duplicates.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="spend-crystals-on-cookies" title="3. Stop feeding crystals to the Pet banner">

Free Pet tickets arrive through normal play, while Cookie promotions feed more of the account. Stellar content cares about Cookie promotion progress, not Pet promotion progress. That makes crystal spending on Pets hard to defend unless a specific Pet solves an immediate team problem and free tickets are nowhere close.

Cookie pickup banners give the spending a clearer purpose. If the featured Cookie belongs in several teams, use the pickup period to push beyond the first copy. Five stars unlocks major breakpoints for some Cookies, and a six to eight-star target can be reasonable for a unit you expect to keep. Do not chase that range on a benchwarmer just because the banner clock is red.

The boring rule works: free tickets for Pets, crystals for a planned Cookie promotion. Your shiny Pet will not open the next Stellar gate.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="stop-perfect-stellar-links" title="4. Quit chasing a perfect Stellar Link board">

Stellar Points disappear much faster than they return. A free account that rolls around 70% coverage has a usable board. Light spenders can aim through the 80s. Low 90s becomes a serious cost, while 96% is territory for accounts that can afford repeated attempts. These are stopping points, not sacred rules.

The ugly number is 100%. Repeated testing puts the expected cost near 400,000 Stellar Points. Take a good board and revisit it after the currency pile grows again.

<GuideTip title="Lock less than your ego wants">

Every locked section makes another reroll more expensive. A board that covers the important nodes at 78% can move the account farther than a 90% project that leaves every other upgrade starved.

</GuideTip>

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="power-is-not-a-verdict" title="5. Stop treating team Power as a verdict">

A small Power advantage does not guarantee an Arena win. Gear, promotion stars, active synergy matches, and the actual formation can overturn it. Scorpion's five-star jump is one example: the displayed number rises, but the faster poison setup matters more than the size of that rise.

An opponent with a deliberate formation can beat twelve individually strong Cookies sharing nothing. Losing with a modest Power advantage is normal.

Use the recommended [Teams](/teams/) as working formations, then adjust them around the Cookies you have promoted. The [Power guide](/guides/cookie-run-crumble-power-guide-stage-damage/) covers the separate PvE penalty tied to Recommended Power. Arena results need a team check, not the story-stage formula.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="shop-for-bottlenecks" title="6. Buy the currency the game refuses to give you">

Mileage and monthly shops tempt you with a wall of decent items. Start with the bottleneck. Dungeon keys create another reward run and help gear progression, so they beat cosmetic convenience or a material already building every hour.

Stellar Points deserve similar treatment in monthly exchanges because regular income is thin. Chocolate-related materials accumulate over time. Stellar Points often do not. When both appear and the account cannot clear the shop, buy the item that has no dependable replacement.

Check what is stopping progress today. A Dungeon key you can spend on a first-clear floor beats another pile of material you cannot use.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="separate-auto-hunt-rewards" title="7. Separate both kinds of Auto Hunt rewards">

Auto Hunt has two reward tracks that look like one. Passive rewards are based on the farthest stage reached and accumulate at the listed per-minute rate. Live battle rewards come from the team fighting on screen. One can keep paying while the other falls apart.

You can test it. Leave only a durable healer alive. The passive counter still increases after a minute because it follows stage progress. The live gold gain can drop to almost nothing because the healer is not killing enemies. That does not mean Auto Hunt is broken. It means the surviving team is terrible at the live part.

Push the campaign to raise the passive rate. Tune a separate farming formation for live fights instead of trusting the boss preset.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="leave-a-survival-farm-team" title="8. Leave a farming team that refuses to die">

Before closing the game, select a formation that can survive the current Auto Hunt stage without losing a Cookie. A healer left alone may live forever, but forever is a long time to earn no live kill rewards. Lower the farming stage if that keeps all twelve Cookies working.

Damage still matters. The team needs enough healing or defense to stay intact, then enough area damage to keep the wave moving. Watch several cycles before trusting it. If one frontline Cookie drops every third wave, the setup is not stable just because the results looked fine for 20 seconds.

Save it as a farming preset. Forcing one formation into every mode usually produces a funny screenshot and a bad inventory.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="know-offline-progress" title="9. Know what offline play cannot do">

Going offline does not push story stages. Auto Hunt stays on the current stage and stores rewards there, even when your team could clear several more chapters. Open the game and advance manually when Power jumps, then let the better stage raise the passive rate.

Leaving the game open has one extra benefit. Repeatable monster-kill tasks can be claimed while live Auto Hunt keeps counting enemies, including the 2,000-monster objective. Offline farming cannot press the claim button for you. If you are nearby, letting the game run and collecting the repeat reward can add more crystals.

Do not keep the screen awake all night for a tiny difference. Testing found no meaningful loss in the base payout from closing the game. Push first, select the safe farming preset, then log off before the storage cap fills.

</GuideSection>

<GuideSection id="hidden-mechanics-faq" title="CookieRun: Crumble hidden mechanics FAQ">

### How do I know whether a debuff landed in CookieRun: Crumble?

Watch the status icons beside the target and the stack counter. If the expected icon or stack does not appear after the hit connects, the debuff failed and the rest of that damage plan may be weaker.

### Should I spend crystals on Cookies or Pets?

Cookie pickup banners are usually the stronger crystal target because Cookie promotions affect more progression systems, including Stellar content. Use free Pet tickets first and spend crystals on a Cookie you plan to promote and keep using.

### How much Stellar Link coverage is enough?

Stop at a result that fits your income. Around 70% can be acceptable for a free account, the 80s suit a light spender, and low 90s or better cost much more. Chasing 100% can erase a huge stockpile for a tiny gain.

### Why can a lower-Power team beat me?

Displayed Power misses important context. Promotion breakpoints, gear effects, active synergies, positioning, and a team built for the mode can beat a slightly larger number.

### Does offline Auto Hunt clear new story stages?

No. Offline Auto Hunt keeps farming the current stage and stores passive rewards. It does not push the campaign forward, even when the account is strong enough to clear the next stage.

</GuideSection>

A high-Power Arena team loses to a smaller roster. Auto Hunt keeps running, yet the gold gain is miserable because eleven Cookies died and Herb has been healing himself for ten minutes.
Most of these failures come from a small icon or a rule the game barely explains. Check these nine systems before spending crystals or rebuilding a team that was almost fine.

A skill hitting the target does not prove its debuff worked. Watch the icons beside the enemy. An ATK Down, DEF Down, poison, or other status should appear after the hit. If the icon never shows, your Cookie dealt the direct damage but failed the second half of the job.

Scorpion Cookie can build up to 20 poison stacks, so the number beside the status tells you whether her damage engine is running or coughing on the first turn. A stalled counter can point to low Focus or a missed application. Do not judge the build from one large result screen when the opening ten seconds already exposed the problem.
Tap a Cookie during combat to inspect its live buffs. The same habit catches inactive synergies. A Granted effect looks impressive on the lineup screen, but it has no value when nobody receives it.
The
Accuracy and Focus guide
explains how to separate a missed hit from a resisted status. That distinction saves a lot of bad gear rerolls.

segments.text: Scorpion Cookie changes sharply at five stars. Her Multi-shot value rises from 2 to 3, which lets a single skill cycle build poison much faster. With the right setup, one cast can reach roughly 10 stacks. Before that promotion, the same team cannot create the same opening pressure.

More Multi-shot providers do not keep adding together. The game uses the strongest received value. Filling three slots with providers will not turn level 3 into level 9. Use one reliable provider and give the other slots different jobs.
This is why rarity alone is a lazy way to judge Cookies. A promoted SR with a skill breakpoint can beat an underbuilt SSR that has no useful connection to the team. Check the current
Tier List
for investment priorities, then look at what the next promotion changes before spending duplicates.
2. Treat Scorpion's five-star promotion as a real breakpoint

segments.text: Free Pet tickets arrive through normal play, while Cookie promotions feed more of the account. Stellar content cares about Cookie promotion progress, not Pet promotion progress. That makes crystal spending on Pets hard to defend unless a specific Pet solves an immediate team problem and free tickets are nowhere close.

Cookie pickup banners give the spending a clearer purpose. If the featured Cookie belongs in several teams, use the pickup period to push beyond the first copy. Five stars unlocks major breakpoints for some Cookies, and a six to eight-star target can be reasonable for a unit you expect to keep. Do not chase that range on a benchwarmer just because the banner clock is red.
The boring rule works: free tickets for Pets, crystals for a planned Cookie promotion. Your shiny Pet will not open the next Stellar gate.
3. Stop feeding crystals to the Pet banner

segments.text: Stellar Points disappear much faster than they return. A free account that rolls around 70% coverage has a usable board. Light spenders can aim through the 80s. Low 90s becomes a serious cost, while 96% is territory for accounts that can afford repeated attempts. These are stopping points, not sacred rules.
The ugly number is 100%. Repeated testing puts the expected cost near 400,000 Stellar Points. Take a good board and revisit it after the currency pile grows again.
Every locked section makes another reroll more expensive. A board that covers the important nodes at 78% can move the account farther than a 90% project that leaves every other upgrade starved.

segments.text: A small Power advantage does not guarantee an Arena win. Gear, promotion stars, active synergy matches, and the actual formation can overturn it. Scorpion's five-star jump is one example: the displayed number rises, but the faster poison setup matters more than the size of that rise.
An opponent with a deliberate formation can beat twelve individually strong Cookies sharing nothing. Losing with a modest Power advantage is normal.

Teams
as working formations, then adjust them around the Cookies you have promoted. The
Power guide
covers the separate PvE penalty tied to Recommended Power. Arena results need a team check, not the story-stage formula.
